Focusing your fire enables you to target an enemy for immediate destruction. Make a ranged Strike with an automatic weapon, expending three times the ammo and gaining a +4 circumstance bonus to damage. This bonus increases to +6 at 11th level and +8 at 15th level.

entities.name: Overwatch
entities.description:
**Trigger** A suppressed creature within your weapon's first range increment makes a ranged attack or leaves a square during a move action it's using.

You concentrate fire on a specific target operating within your weapon's threat range. Make a ranged Strike against the triggering creature, ignoring the unwieldy trait of weapons you wield for this Strike. On a critical hit, if the triggering action was a move action, you disrupt that action.

entities.name: Run Hot
entities.description:
**Requirements** You're wielding an area weapon.

You hold down the trigger and push your weapons to their absolute limits with a ceaseless barrage of firepower. Area Fire twice with the required weapon, ignoring the unwieldy trait of your weapon. Creatures in the area of the second Area Fire attack gain a +2 circumstance bonus to their save.

After you use this action, your weapon must cool off and can't be used until after your next turn or until you take any amount of cold damage.

entities.name: Familiar
entities.description: You've programmed a clever little mascot, uploaded into a body of pure magic. The resulting creature is a loyal companion and assists you in your day-to-day life. You gain a familiar.

entities.name: Signal Relay
entities.description:
**Requirements** You have line of effect to a tech minion under your control within 120 feet.

You transfer a spell between yourself and your minion. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell that affects only you, other than a polymorph spell, the spell affects your minion instead of you.

entities.name: Tech Talk
entities.description: You can freely speak with technology. You can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the Diplomacy skill with tech creatures. You don't need to share a language to communicate with such creatures in this way, although some creatures might lack the ability to communicate using spoken language and need to communicate using writing.

entities.name: Universal Spell Bus
entities.description: You can piggyback on magic frequencies from your spell database to access your stored *spell chips* and *spell gems*. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell from a *spell chip* or *spell gem*, you don't have to be holding the item to activate it.

entities.name: Greater Magic Hack
entities.description: You've made a breakthrough well suited to your preferred strategies. You learn the greater magic hack of your chosen programming language.

entities.name: Liminal Hyperlink
entities.description: You can hack reality, connecting two separate locations with a magical hyperlink and enabling fast travel between them. You gain the Liminal Hyperlink magic hack.

entities.name: Overwhelming Energy
entities.description: You overcharge your spell to bypass your enemy's defenses. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell, the spell ignores an amount of the target's resistance to acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic damage equal to your level. This applies to all damage the spell deals, including persistent damage and damage caused by an ongoing effect of the spell, such as the wall created by Wall of Fire. A creature's immunities are unaffected.

entities.name: Turbocharge Armaments
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes

If your next action is to Cast a Spell that requires a saving throw against a single target, you channel the magic through your weapon. Make a Strike against the target. On a hit, in addition to the normal effects of the Strike, the target takes a –1 circumstance penalty to its save against the spell (–2 circumstance penalty on a critical hit).

entities.name: Turbocharge Batteries
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes

**Requirements** You have an overclocked tech minion.

You channel energy from your overclocked tech minion into your spell database. If your next action is to Cast a Spell, you siphon surplus magical energy to cause your overclocked minion to Stride and erupt in a burst of flames and lightning after the spell resolves. It deals floor @actor.level -4 /2 d4 fire , floor @actor.level -4 /2 d4 electricity |options:area-damage damage in a 10-foot ( save against your spell DC) and is destroyed. At 12th level and every two levels thereafter, increase the fire and electricity damage you deal by 1d4.

entities.name: Turbocharge Lattice
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes

Magical circuitry blazes to life on your body and empowers your spells' code. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell by activating a *spell chip* or *spell gem*, heighten the spell up to two ranks lower than the highest-rank spell slot you can cast.

entities.name: Turbocharge Shielding
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes

If your next action is to Cast a Spell with a duration of no longer than 10 minutes that targets a single creature, you can amplify and reroute the defensive barrier being generated by your armor to empower your target. You Overclock Armor, immediately lose all your temporary Hit Points, and grant the same amount of temporary Hit Points you lost to the target of the spell. These temporary Hit Points last until the spell ends.

entities.name: Advanced Cross-Platform Application
entities.description: You've mastered another programming language. You learn the advanced magic hack of the same programming language as the magic hack you learned with Cross-Platform Application.

Stats.Prerequisites: Advanced Magic Hack, Greater Magic Hack, Cross-Platform Application

entities.name: Double Jailbreak
entities.description: You can modify spells beyond compare. Once per hour, when you use Jailbreak Spell to apply the spellshape granted by your programming language to a spell, you can apply both the basic and advanced jailbreak benefits from your programming language. The spell you modify must still meet all the usual requirements of the spellshape and of both jailbreak effects.

entities.name: Hardware Expansion
entities.description: You can overclock a wider variety of gear. When you take this feat, select one programming language other than your own. You gain the overclock boost benefits of that programming language, meaning you can select that type of gear when you Overclock Gear instead of the type normally allowed by your original programming language. You don't gain the firmware enhancement, Overclock Pulse, or other benefits of that programming language.

entities.name: Reactive Firewall
entities.description:
**Trigger** You would be hit, but not critically hit, by an attack.

**Requirements** Your gear is overclocked.

A wall of data bursts from your overclocked gear to shield you from harm. The attacker must roll its attack roll a second time and take the lower result.

entities.name: Cache Caster
entities.description: During your daily preparations, you gain one extra spell slot of your highest rank, which you can use only to prepare or Download Spells from your spell cache.

entities.name: Debug Spell
entities.description: You adjust the parameters of a spell to operate at maximum efficiency. If your next action is to Cast a Spell that deals damage or restores Hit Points, any die you roll for damage or healing that has a result of less than 2 becomes 2 instead.

entities.name: Recalculate Coordinates
entities.description:
**Requirements** You have an active spell affecting an area or a single ally within 60 feet.

The battlefield isn't always as predictable as you'd like, so you've devised a method to shift around your spell effects after they've been deployed. If the required spell affects an area, you move the spell's area to a new location, and the spell no longer affects its previous area. If the required spell affects a single ally, you move the spell to a new ally, and the spell no longer affects its previous target. The new area or target must meet any of the spell's usual requirements, including range and line of effect from you when you Recalculate Coordinates. Regardless of the required spell's area or target, the spell's remaining duration is reduced by half.

entities.name: Tashtari Cluster
entities.description: You apply the outdated technique of clustering identical systems to form a parallel computing cluster to your magic, allowing you to manage more than one piece of overclocked gear at once. You can have up to two pieces of overclocked gear at once, and you overclock up to two pieces of gear whenever you Overclock Gear. Only one piece of overclocked gear is no longer overclocked when you use Jailbreak Spell.

entities.name: Download All
entities.description: You can take an extra moment when you access your spell cache to gain nearly unlimited access to its contents. When you Download Spell, you can do so as a single action instead of a free action. If you do, you can download any number of spells in your spell cache into any number of your available spell slots, replacing spells on a one-for-one basis and filling spell slots as usual when you Download Spell.

entities.name: Script Kiddie
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes

**Trigger** Your turn begins.

Arcane scripts from the infosphere can be easily transferred from one spell database to another, allowing technomancers access to spellshapes without having to know exactly how they work. Until the end of your turn, you gain a single spellshape feat from the technomancer class that has a level requirement of no more than half your level.

entities.name: Copy-Paste Spell
entities.description: You copy the components of your spell before casting it from your database, maintaining a copy that duplicates the spell's effects. If your next action is to Cast a Spell of 4th rank or lower that has no duration, the spell's energy remains temporarily copied. You can Cast the Spell a second time before the end of your next turn without expending a spell slot.

entities.name: Pirate Spell
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes

**Trigger** You critically succeed at a saving throw against an enemy's spell, or an enemy critically fails at a spell attack roll against you.

You decompile an enemy's spell and take its lingering magical energy for yourself. You gain the ability to cast the triggering spell one time before the end of your next turn, even if it's not on your spell list or is of a higher rank than you can cast. This doesn't cost you a spell slot or other resources. If you cast it using a spellshape against the creature that originally cast it, that creature cannot use any reactions that would trigger from you Casting the Spell. Use your own spellcasting statistics for this spell, as you do for other spells you cast.

entities.name: Speedrun
entities.description: You briefly hack reality, allowing you to pass through walls, ignore damage, and phase through enemies. You gain the Speedrun magic hack.

entities.name: Dynamic Frequency Scaling
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes

Your magic protects the delicate lattice of your *spell gems* from damage so they can be used more than once. If your next action is to Cast a Spell from a *spell gem*, instead of being destroyed, the *spell gem* becomes a temporary item that can't be sold and lasts only until you use it again or the next time you make your daily preparations (whichever comes first). If your next action is to Cast a Spell from a *spell chip* that has already been used once today, it becomes Broken on a failure (but is still destroyed on a critical failure).

entities.name: Energy Sink
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes

Your magic is directed into your armor to protect you from harm. If your next action is to Cast a Spell that deals at least one type of energy damage (acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic), you gain resistance to an energy damage type of your choice equal to twice the spell's rank for 1 minute. You get the resistance regardless of whether or not your spell dealt damage.

entities.name: Enhanced Familiar
entities.description: You infuse your familiar with additional magical energy, increasing its abilities. You can select four familiar or master abilities each day, instead of two.

entities.name: Thermoelectric Phase Change
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes

You alter the type of energy output of your magic. If your next action is to Cast a Spell with no duration that has an elemental trait (air, earth, fire, metal, water, or wood) and deals one type of damage, replace the elemental trait with a different elemental trait and the damage it deals with one of the damage types corresponding to the selected trait: air (electricity or sonic), earth (bludgeoning or piercing), fire (fire), metal (acid or slashing), water (cold), wood (poison).

entities.name: Auto Spellshape
entities.description: You exploit magical shortcuts to effortlessly alter your spells. You can use spellshape single actions as free actions.

entities.name: God Mode
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes

You understand the nuanced beauty of arcane code and can modify it in ways other spellcasters can hardly fathom. Use up to three single-action technomancer spellshape feats. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell, apply all of these spellshapes to that spell.

entities.name: Root Access
entities.description: You've cracked the root access of arcane magic itself. You gain an additional 10th-rank spell slot.

entities.name: Alakablam
entities.description:
**Requirements** You're wielding a ranged weapon, and your most recent action was to Cast a Spell from a *spell gem*.

You take the delicate remains of a consumed spell gem and load it into your ranged weapon as magic ammunition. Overclock Gear, ignoring its usual trigger. Until the end of your turn, the weapon deals an extra 1d6 force damage and gains the arcane trait if it didn't have it already. If the spell dealt a different type of damage, the Strike deals this type of damage instead (or your choice of one type of damage if the spell dealt multiple types of damage).

entities.name: Black Hat Trick
entities.description: You've learned how to exploit the vulnerabilities of glitching creatures to force them to do your bidding for a short time. You gain the Black Hat Trick magic hack.

entities.name: Expanded Cache
entities.description: You've expanded your spell cache. Select any two spells that are in your spell database; each spell you select must be of a different rank. The selected spells are temporarily added to your spell cache. Each time you gain a new rank of spells, you can remove one of the selected spells from your spell cache and replace it with another spell from your spell database.

entities.name: Incognito Spell
entities.description:
**Requirements** You control an overclocked minion.

When you apply the Conceal Spell spellshape to a spell, you can manifest the spell from one of your overclocked minions instead of yourself. Use the minion's space to determine the spell's source, range, and area of effect, but line of sight and line of effect must be met from both you and your minion when the spell is cast. If the spell has a range of touch, you can have the minion deliver the spell to a creature within its reach.

entities.name: Overclock Onlaunch
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per day

**Trigger** You roll initiative.

You've programmed your gear to be ready to overclock at a moment's notice. You Overclock Gear, ignoring its trigger.

entities.name: Spell Protection Protocol
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes

Your subroutine diverts a portion of your spell's energy to create a shield. If your next action is to Cast a Spell, you or your minion with the tech trait gains temporary Hit Points equal to double the rank of the spell that last 1 minute. If the spell deals at least one type of energy damage (acid, cold, electricity, fire, force, sonic, vitality, or void), you or your minion gain resistance to an energy damage type of your choice equal to the spell's rank for as long as the temporary Hit Points remain.

entities.name: Technological Superiority
entities.description: Whether out of practicality or sentimentality, you keep all your technological tools at your disposal in impeccable condition—even if they're only at your disposal for a minimal amount of time. Tech creatures under your control, including minions, within a 30-foot around you gain a +2 status bonus to saving throws and resistance to electricity damage equal to half your level rounded up.

entities.name: Active Defense Firewall
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes

You bind a hostile spell into your armor. If your next action is to Cast a Spell with a hostile effect that targets one creature, you store the spell in your armor instead. The spell must use a spell slot and take 2 or fewer actions to cast. Your armor can store only one spell in this way; you can't use Active Defense Firewall while you already have a spell stored.

When a creature touches or damages you with an unarmed melee attack or non-reach melee weapon, you can Cast the Spell stored in your armor as a reaction, targeting the triggering creature. Only the creature that triggered the reaction is affected by the spell.

You can Dismiss Active Defense Firewall. If you do, you immediately restore the spell to its spell slot.

entities.name: Advanced Magic Hack
entities.description: Delving into your chosen programming language has led to a magical breakthrough. You learn the advanced magic hack of your chosen programming language.

entities.name: Booming Bootloader
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes

Your summoned creature appears with unexpected fanfare and brilliant destruction. If your next action is to Cast a Spell with the summon trait, all creatures in a 10-foot around the creature you summoned take 1d4 sonic |options:area-damage damage per spell rank of the spell cast, with a basic  save against your spell DC.

entities.name: Log Spell Execution
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes

You decode a temporary copy of an executed spell into your spell cache. If your next action is to Cast a Spell from a *spell chip* or *spell gem*, temporarily add the spell to your spell cache. It remains in your cache until you use Download Spell to replace a prepared spell with the logged spell or until the next time you use Log Spell Execution. You can use this spellshape only to log spells that appear on the arcane spell list.

entities.name: Overclock Spell Cache
entities.description:
**Trigger** You Cast a Spell not modified by a jailbreak effect.

**Requirements** Your gear is overclocked.

You route excess magical energy into your spell cache. Your gear is no longer overclocked. Once during the next minute, you can Cast a Spell directly from your spell cache, up to the same rank as the triggering spell, without using a spell slot.

entities.name: Virtualized Data Transmission
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes

**Requirements** You're wielding a ranged tech weapon.

You digitize yourself using your magic and transmit yourself across the battlefield as rapidly as a message sent through the infosphere. If your next action is to Cast a Spell with a range and an area, you teleport yourself and your gear to one open space within the spell's area. You can choose to arrive before or after the spell takes effect.

entities.name: White Hat Hack
entities.description:
**Trigger** You Cast a Spell not modified by a jailbreak effect.

**Requirements** Your gear is overclocked.

You're an expert in testing the cyber defenses of tech gear and defending against incoming attacks, and you know how to use excess magic energy to troubleshoot your tech when these defenses are inevitably breached. You target tech creatures or items of a number up to the rank of the triggering spell that are within 100 feet of you. You reduce the Glitching condition of the targets by half the triggering spell's rank (minimum 1). For the next minute, affected targets roll flat checks to recover from the glitching condition twice and use the higher result; this is a fortune effect.

entities.name: Cross-Platform Application
entities.description: You believe that adaptability and a diverse skill set is the key to success. You learn the initial magic hack of a programming language other than your chosen programming language.

entities.name: Grenade Spell
entities.description:
**Requirements** You're holding a grenade requiring a Reflex save.

If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell with a burst area that requires a basic Reflex save, the spell doesn't take effect and is instead installed into the required grenade. Until the end of your next turn, any creature caught in the area of that grenade is also affected by the installed spell; creatures don't attempt a separate Reflex save against the spell and instead use the same result they rolled against the grenade. Resolve the grenade's effects first, then the spell's effects.

entities.name: Incredible Familiar
entities.description: Your familiar is imbued with even more magic. You can select six familiar or master abilities each day, instead of four.

entities.name: Jury-Rigged Turbocharge
entities.description: You've designed a magical application to enhance technology. You gain the Jury-Rigged Turbocharge magic hack.

entities.name: Leverage Specs
entities.description: You use your knowledge of creatures and their specifications to magically overcome their defenses. When you critically succeed at a check to Recall Knowledge about a creature, the creature takes a –1 circumstance penalty to its AC and saving throws against your spells and the attacks of your minions with the tech trait for a number of rounds equal to your Intelligence modifier.

entities.name: Spell Library
entities.description: You've expanded your spell cache to store more spells than most. During your daily preparations, you can add one spell to your spell cache of each rank of spell you can cast, selecting from the spells in your spell database. The spells remain in your spell cache until your next daily preparations.

entities.name: Split Tunneling
entities.description: You program a ranged spell to split and hit two foes at once. If your next action is to Cast a Spell without a duration that requires an attack roll against a single target, you can choose a second target within range. You roll a single attack roll and compare the result to the AC of each target. This counts as one attack for your multiple attack penalty. To the second target, the spell deals only half the damage it would normally deal for its degree of success and has no effects beyond the spell's initial damage (such as imposing conditions or penalties).

entities.name: Anchoring Strike
entities.description:
**Requirements** Your quantum field is active.

Battle can be disorienting, but for you, the intense mental effort of striking your targets lends you additional clarity and focus. Make a Strike. The Strike gains the following success and critical success effects.

**Critical Success** The Strike gains the anchoring trait. You can reroll the damage dice rolled for this strike, but you must use the second result, even if it's worse.

**Success** The Strike gains the anchoring trait.

entities.name: Debris Zone
entities.description: Whether it's covered in debris, partially flooded, or otherwise troublesome to traverse, the area of your quantum field becomes difficult terrain.

entities.name: Otherworldly Spell
entities.description: Your spell has an odd appearance or cosmetic effect. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell, creatures with the ability to Cast that Spell don't automatically know what the spell is. In addition, creatures that witness your spellcasting take a –2 circumstance penalty to checks to identify the spell with Recall Knowledge and checks to counteract the spell and its effects.

entities.name: Soothing Anchor
entities.description:
**Frequency** once every 10 minutes

**Requirements** Your last action was to Sustain your quantum field or had the anchoring trait.

You concentrate more deeply on your anchor to soothe yourself. You gain temporary Hit Points equal to your character level that last for 1 round.

entities.name: Greater Warp
entities.description: You breach the veil of paradoxical understanding. You gain the greater warp spell for your paradox.

entities.name: Share Quantum Aura
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes

You temporarily share your quantum field with an ally. You cause your quantum field to emanate from an ally you can see instead of yourself. The ally gains all the benefits of your quantum field, and your warp spells originate from your ally instead of you until your quantum field deactivates. If you cast warp spells at other targets, you must still have line of sight to the target, but the spell originates from your ally for purposes of determining its range and line of effect.

entities.name: Twisted Dark Zone
entities.description: You expose this reality to a realm of pure darkness filled with gibbering voices and otherworldly entities. The area of your quantum field functions as though it were an area of 2nd-rank Darkness. Creatures that begin their turn in the area must succeed at a  save against your class DC or become Confused for 1 round (this is an incapacitation effect). The creature then becomes immune for 24 hours. If this *darkness* is successfully counteracted, the quantum field's other effects remain.

entities.name: In Another Life
entities.description: Whenever you rest, you behold different versions of yourself in other realities. During your daily preparations, select one ancestry feat for your ancestry that you meet the prerequisites for and don't already have. You gain that feat until your next daily preparations.

entities.name: Radiant Zone
entities.description:
The reality you conjure is much brighter than your own. The area of your quantum field becomes bright light. Creatures who begin their turn in your quantum field must attempt a  save against your class DC; creatures with light blindness treat their result as one step worse.

**Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Failure** The creature is Dazzled for 1 round.

**Critical Failure** The creature is Blinded for 1 round, then dazzled for 1 round.

entities.name: Sense Abnormalities
entities.description: You possess an uncanny sixth sense for ambient magic. You can sense the presence of magic auras as though you were always using a 1st-rank Detect Magic spell. This detects magic in your field of vision only. When you Seek, you gain the benefits of a 3rd-rank *detect magic* spell on things you see (in addition to the normal benefits of Seeking). You can turn this sense off and on with a free action at the start or the end of your turn.

entities.name: Borrow Spell
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per day

**Trigger** You use an action that Sustains your quantum field, and the quantum field is still active.

By reaching across both time and space, you can borrow the use of a spell from a version of yourself inhabiting another reality. During this turn, you can cast one spell without spending a spell slot to do so. The spell must be in your repertoire.

entities.name: Multiverse Magic
entities.description: Your paradoxical nature has given you access to magic that isn't associated with your spellcasting tradition. You can have one spell in your spell repertoire (not one on your paradox's spell list) that isn't from your spellcasting tradition. Select this spell when you select this feat. You can cast that spell as a spell of your spellcasting tradition, and it becomes a signature spell. You can change the spell you choose when you gain a level.

entities.name: Persistent Quantum Field
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per day

You can create a stable quantum field. You Warp Reality with a duration of 1 minute.

entities.name: Folded Paradoxes
entities.description: Your paradoxical nature has become multifaceted. During daily preparations, you can replace one of your paradox spells with a spell of another paradox that grants training in the prerequisite paradox skill.

Stats.Prerequisites: master in a paradox skill for a paradox other than your chosen paradox

entities.name: Zone Overlap
entities.description:
**Requirements** Your quantum field is active with one zone affecting it.

You cause a second zone to overlap your quantum field. You can choose to apply another zone you're able to create, or apply the existing zone again, improving its effects as follows: Danger Zone deals 1 extra damage, Debris Zone becomes greater difficult terrain, and Twisted Dark Zone ignores the temporary immunity of creatures that previously critically succeeded at the save for 1 round.

entities.name: Complete Transposition
entities.description: The multiverse is a complex game—you use alternate realities to move creatures on the board. When you use the Sustain action to move your quantum field, you can teleport any number of creatures within the quantum field's original area to squares of your choice in its new area. You also teleport any items they're wearing or holding. This gives the Sustain action the teleportation trait. Each target can attempt a  save against your class DC. Targets who succeed at the save are unaffected.

entities.name: Infinite Magic
entities.description: You borrow spells from other realities. Twice per day, you can cast a 9th-rank or lower spell after you've run out of spell slots of the appropriate spell rank; the two spells you cast with this feat must be of different spell ranks.

entities.name: Fundamental Understanding
entities.description:
**Trigger** A creature, trap, or similar object within your quantum field casts a spell that you don't have in your spell repertoire, and you're aware of the casting.

If the triggering spell is common and you're trained in the associated skill for the spell's tradition, you automatically identify the spell being cast (you still roll to attempt to get a critical success but can't get a worse result than a success). You or a visible ally within 60 feet targeted by this spell gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your saving throw or your AC against it (or a +2 circumstance bonus if you rolled a critical success).

entities.name: Predictive Positioning
entities.description:
**Trigger** An enemy damages you.

**Requirements** Your quantum field is active.

You reposition to a space you'd occupy in a different reality, free from incoming danger. You instantly teleport up to your Speed to an area within your quantum field. This movement doesn't trigger reactions based on movement and ignores hazards and terrain, but can't pass through walls or other such obstructions.

entities.name: Scrub Psyche
entities.description:
**Trigger** You or an ally fail a save against a mental effect while within your quantum field.

You scrub all traces of the triggering effect from the target's mind. The target rerolls their saving throw against the triggering effect and must use the second result, even if it's worse.

entities.name: Warp Wounds
entities.description:
**Trigger** An enemy damages you.

**Requirements** An enemy or willing ally is in your quantum field.

Your reality shifts to partly overlap with another in which someone else was injured in your stead. You gain resistance to all damage against the triggering attack equal to half your level, and one enemy or willing ally in your quantum field takes damage of the same type equal to the amount of damage prevented this way, with a  save against your class DC.

entities.name: Quantum Negation
entities.description: You expose a target to a reality in which they don't exist. You learn the Quantum Negation warp spell.

entities.name: Quantum Research
entities.description: You become a true embodiment of your paradox and surpass what mortals can achieve in your reality. You gain an additional 10th-rank spell slot.

entities.name: Meandering Mind
entities.description:
**Requirements** Your quantum field is active.

You allow your mind to wander to things you find pleasant, briefly shutting out all realities and protecting you from harm. You gain a +2 status bonus to saving throws against mental effects until the start of your next turn.

entities.name: Quantum Recycle
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per day

**Trigger** You cast a 2nd-rank or higher spell, and the spell targets a creature or area within your quantum field.

You expertly manipulate the effects of your quantum field to ensure that some of the energy from your spell is preserved and can be harnessed again. You regain an expended spell slot one spell rank lower than the triggering spell.

entities.name: Spellsurge Ammo
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per turn

**Trigger** You cast a non-cantrip spell.

You siphon spell energy into one weapon or grenade you're wielding. Until the end of your turn, the weapon or grenade deals extra force damage equal to the rank of the spell and gains the magical trait if it didn't have it already. If the spell deals damage, the extra damage becomes the same type as the triggering spell.

entities.name: Enlarge Quantum Field
entities.description: Your quantum field slowly encroaches on reality. Increase your quantum field's radius by 10 feet. Until your quantum field deactivates, once per turn when you Sustain the quantum field, increase its radius by an additional 5 feet (to a maximum of 50 additional feet).

entities.name: Predict Outcome
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per hour

You spend 10 minutes opening yourself to the mysteries of the multiverse by peering across different timelines or analyzing probability simulations. You gain the effects of Augury, except you learn only about the dangers ahead; any results of "good" are instead "nothing," and results of "mixed" are instead "bad."

If you're legendary in Arcana or Occultism, you take only 1 minute to Predict Outcome.

entities.name: Quantum Aura
entities.description: You can become the nexus of the warped reality you create. Each time you use Warp Reality to activate your quantum field, you can choose for your quantum field to be an aura around you that moves with you. If you do, your Warp Reality action gains the aura trait, and the quantum field you create is a 10-foot-radius emanation.

entities.name: Advanced Warp
entities.description: Your paradox begins to cement itself across your life. You gain the advanced warp spell for your paradox.

entities.name: Danger Zone
entities.description: Your quantum field merges with a more dangerous reality, becoming hazardous terrain that deals 1 damage to an enemy each time it enters a square in the area. You choose the damage type when you use Danger Zone, selecting from the following: acid, bludgeoning, cold, electricity, fire, piercing, slashing, or sonic. Increase the damage by 1 at 12th, 16th, and 20th levels.

entities.name: Quantum Entanglement
entities.description: You prevent creatures from leaving your quantum field and returning to reality. Until the start of your next turn, any creature who begins its turn inside your quantum field must succeed at a  saving throw against your witchwarper class DC to move outside your quantum field. On a failure, the action is disrupted. A creature that succeeds at this save is immune to your Quantum Entanglement for 24 hours.

entities.name: Augmented Body
entities.description:
You implant one augmentation with an item level equal to your character level or lower. This augmentation doesn't count against your total implant limit. The first time you take this feat, the augmentation you receive is free as long as its item level is 1 or lower. You can upgrade this augmentation by swapping it out with another augmentation when you gain a level or by spending downtime replacing the augmentation as though changing out a feat. When you swap out the augmentation, you must pay the difference between the original and new augmentation each time you upgrade.

**Special** You can select this feat multiple times, choosing a different augmentation each time. Retraining this feat requires paying the cost of the original augmentation.

entities.name: Barricade
entities.description: You hastily create a barricade using nearby items, junk, or debris. The barricade provides lesser cover for you and one other ally, though you can Take Cover to increase this benefit to standard cover. The barricade is flimsy and falls apart at the end of your next turn.

entities.name: Prescient Planner
entities.description:
**Cost** the Price of the chosen item

**Requirements** You haven't used this ability since the last time you were able to purchase goods.

You regularly create convoluted plans and contingencies, using your resources to enact them. You take 1 minute to remove your backpack, then carefully remove an item you hadn't previously declared that you purchased—you intuited that you would come to need the item and purchased it at the latest opportunity. The item must be a piece of adventuring gear, and can't be a weapon, armor, serum, magic item, or other treasure. It must be common with a level no higher than half your level, and its Bulk must be low enough that carrying it wouldn't have made you encumbered.

entities.name: Akiton Battery Hack
entities.description:
**Requirements** You have a free hand and are holding a battery with at least 10 charges.

With a couple quick adjustments, you Craft an electromag grenade using the held battery. The grenade is Commercial grade if the battery has at least 10 charges, Tactical if the battery has at least 40 charges, or Advanced if the battery has at least 60 charges. If you're legendary in Crafting, you can Craft a Superior grenade using a battery with at least 100 charges. Grenades crafted using Akiton Battery Hack last until the end of your next turn, after which they're harmlessly discharged and no longer function as a battery or grenade.

entities.name: Arcane Sense
entities.description: You can cast 1st-rank Detect Magic at will as an arcane innate spell. If you're a master in Arcana, the spell is heightened to 3rd rank; if you're legendary, it is heightened to 4th rank.

entities.name: Bargain Hunter
entities.description: You can Earn Income using Diplomacy, spending your days hunting for bargains and reselling at a profit. You can also spend time specifically seeking a great bargain on an item; this works as if you were using Earn Income with Diplomacy, except instead of gaining money, you purchase the item at a discount equal to the money you would have gained, gaining the item for free if your earned income equals or exceeds its cost. Finally, if you select Bargain Hunter during character creation at 1st level, you start play with an additional 20 credits.

entities.name: Battle Medicine
entities.description:
**Requirements** You're holding or wearing a medkit.

You can patch up wounds, even in combat. Attempt a Medicine check with the same DC as for Treat Wounds and restore the corresponding amount of HP; this doesn't remove the wounded condition. As with Treat Wounds, you can attempt checks against higher DCs if you have the minimum proficiency rank. The target is then immune to your Battle Medicine for 1 day. This does not make them immune to, or otherwise count as, Treat Wounds.

entities.name: Blend In
entities.description: You know how to blend in and become a forgettable face in the crowd. While in a crowd of at least 10 other creatures, you can roll a Society check in place of a Stealth check when using the Avoid Notice exploration activity to see if enemies notice you. While in a settlement, you can use Society in place of Deception when Impersonating a non-specific individual.

entities.name: Crowd Surfing
entities.description: You move through crowds without slowing down. You can move at full Speed in crowds. Treat areas truly packed with people as difficult terrain instead of greater difficult terrain.

entities.name: Cyberbully
entities.description: Whether you are a hacktivist or reformed troll, you know to irritate people anonymously in digital spaces, pushing their buttons even when it means resorting to cruel personal attacks. You can use Intimidation to coerce without the usual penalty from being anonymous on the infosphere.

entities.name: Deadlift
entities.description:
**Requirements** You aren't Fatigued.

For 1 minute, you can carry 4 more Bulk than normal before becoming encumbered. The amount you can carry increases to 6 at expert, 8 at master, and 10 at legendary. When the benefits of this feat end, you become Fatigued for 10 minutes.

entities.name: Digital Ambassador
entities.description: As long as you're using a comm unit, datapad, or computer to communicate, when you attempt to use a skill action with the linguistic trait on a creature that doesn't understand the language you're using, roll a DC 15. On a success, the effect works as if the creature understood the language you're using. If you're Legendary in Society, the DC is 10 (DC 10).

entities.name: Digital Branding
entities.description: You use acting, video editing, and propaganda to convince people of your lies online, even if they don't know who you are in the real world or think you are someone else. You can use Deception to Lie without the usual penalty for being anonymous on the infosphere.

entities.name: Digital Diversion
entities.description:
**Requirements** You are holding or wearing a hacking toolkit and have a free hand.

Whether it's a sudden comm unit ping or a warning alarm on an equipment display, you can Create a Diversion by using Computers instead of Deception on an adjacent target carrying, wearing, or wielding a tech item.

create-a-diversion variant=distracting-words skill=computers

create-a-diversion variant=gesture skill=computers

create-a-diversion variant=trick skill=computers

entities.name: Dirty Trick
entities.description:
**Requirements** You have a hand free and are within melee reach of an opponent.

You hook a foe's boot clasps together, pull their visor from their eyes, loosen their mag-belt, or otherwise confound their mobility through an underhanded tactic. Attempt a Thievery check against the target's Reflex DC.

**Critical Success** The target is Clumsy 1 until they use an Interact action to end the impediment

**Success** As critical success, but the condition ends automatically after 1 round.

**Critical Failure** You fall Prone as your attempt backfires.

entities.name: Electrical Engineer
entities.description: You can fuel battery-powered devices by drawing electricity from different sources. Doing so takes 1 minute of work and an adjacent source of power appropriate to the device. If the source of power is a technological creature or hazard, it must have been destroyed within the last 10 minutes and provides charges equal to twice its level. If the source is a facility capable of charging a battery, the battery-powered device operates as if the battery were always fully charged. If you're a master in Crafting, you can connect a device to a power source as a 3-action activity. If you're legendary, it takes 1 action.

entities.name: Express Driver
entities.description: You know how to get there fast. When calculating your travel Speed for the day while piloting a vehicle, you can attempt a Piloting check to increase your vehicle's travel Speed for long-term overland or aerial travel. The DC is determined by the GM but is typically based on the vehicle's piloting DC or a difficulty based on the environment, whichever is harder. On a success, double your vehicle's travel Speed for the day. This has no effect on your vehicle's movement in encounters or on starships traveling through the Drift.

entities.name: Fabricator
entities.description: You know how to configure and print tech items out of UPBs in creator capsules. You must have the formula to create the item in a creator capsule and pay an amount of UPBs equal to the material price of the item, reducing the materials used based on the result of your Crafting check. Unlike normal Crafting, this process takes minutes instead of days (depending on the grade of creator capsule used), but you can't spend additional time working on the item. A creator capsule is consumed when you successfully Craft an item but not when you roll a failure or critical failure. You don't need the Tech Crafting skill feat to craft tech items using Fabricator, but you can't use Fabricator to create magical equipment unless you have Magical Crafting.

entities.name: Face in the Crowd
entities.description:
You know how to get lost in a crowd. You can use cover from crowds to Hide and Sneak, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to your Stealth checks when in a crowd of at least 10 creatures and a +4 circumstance bonus to your Stealth checks when in a crowd of at least 100 creatures. Hidden creatures don't count as members of a crowd. If you're a master in Deception you only need 5 creatures to get these bonuses.

Effect: Face in the Crowd

entities.name: Favored Disguise
entities.description: You create a favored disguise that you can call upon at a moment's notice. When you Impersonate, you can decide that the disguise becomes your favored disguise. If you have a holoskin or can Change Shape, you can always adopt your favored disguise when Impersonating. You still roll Deception for the Impersonate check but count any critical failure results as failures instead. You can have one favored disguise and gain an additional favored disguise you can employ at expert, master, and legendary proficiency in Deception.

entities.name: Hit Record
entities.description: You're constantly recording, aiming for that perfect camera angle or sound bite. You can perform the Livestream exploration activity at the same time as other exploration activities. In addition, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to checks to Earn Income that use your footage, such as Performance or Infosphere Lore, as long as you have at least 8 hours of footage recorded since the last time you attempted to Earn Income. If you're a master in Performance, this bonus increases to +2; if you're legendary in Performance, this bonus increases to +3.

entities.name: Hologram Skeptic
entities.description: You easily spot the tiny glitches and imperfections in holograms. Even if you aren't Searching, you always attempt a check to disbelieve holograms and effects with the illusion and tech traits that normally require you to Search or Interact with them.

entities.name: Inject Serum
entities.description: You can administer medicine using injection weapons. You can load an injection weapon with a hypopen, poison, or serum as an Interact action. When you successfully Strike with an injection weapon loaded in this way, you deal no damage. Instead, you administer the loaded substance to the target of the Strike.

entities.name: Intimidating Shot
entities.description: You attempt to Demoralize a foe with your ranged weapon by firing it into the air, using ammo equal to the weapon's expend and the weapon's maximum range rather than the usual range of 30 feet. This check doesn't take a –4 circumstance penalty if the target doesn't share a language with you.

entities.name: Junk Cobbler
entities.description:
When in a junk-rich environment, you can spend 4 hours to attempt a Crafting check to scavenge the materials you need to Craft a non-consumable item of 2nd level or lower. The GM determines the DC based on the level of the item you're attempting to Craft. During your daily preparations, you must perform some maintenance on this junk item or it falls apart and gains the broken condition. You can only have one junk item at a time. If you're an expert in Crafting, you can have two junk items at a time. If you're a master in Crafting, you can have four junk items at a time. If you're legendary in Crafting, you can have eight junk items at a time and can Craft junk items of an item level up to half your level.

**Critical Success** You locate suitable raw materials worth half the Price of the item you intend to Craft.

**Success** You locate raw materials worth one-quarter the Price of the item you intend to Craft.

**Failure** You fail to locate any raw materials.

**Critical Failure** Poor materials ruins 10 percent of the raw materials you use to Craft your item.

entities.name: Just Kidding
entities.description:
**Trigger** An ally critically fails to Coerce, Make an Impression, or Request.

You attempt to play off a social misstep as a joke. Attempt a Performance check against the same DC as your ally's check. If you succeed, your ally treats their critical failure as a failure.

Stats.Traits: auditory, emotion, fortune, general, linguistic, mental, skill

entities.name: Living Missile
entities.description:
**Trigger** You end your movement adjacent to an enemy.

**Requirements** You're Flying using a tech item, such as a jetpack or jump jets.

Soaring head-first into your foe, you shove skill=acrobatics them, rolling an Acrobatics check in place of the usual Athletics check. On a success or critical success, you can Fly after your target rather than Stride, even if you don't have a fly Speed.

entities.name: Management Material
entities.description: Anyone who speaks with you about a job, workplace, or office skill set assumes you're a professional in that setting unless you intentionally present yourself differently. You can use Society to Make an Impression on a professional or to Impersonate a type of professional or a specific individual professional. If you use the normally required skills in those situations, you receive a +1 circumstance bonus to the check instead.

entities.name: Nanomedical Safeguards
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per day

You've integrated medical nanites into your body. You activate these nanites to gain the benefits of one hypopen with a level equal to half your level or lower (minimum 1).

entities.name: Open-Source Research
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per hour

**Requirements** You have a comm unit and infosphere access.

Infosphere archivists have lived by the credo that information wants to be free, and you know where to find it. You Access Infosphere. On a critical failure, in addition to the usual effects, your comm unit becomes Glitching 5.

entities.name: Phishing Expertise
entities.description: You're skilled at running digital fraud schemes. You can Create a Forgery using Computers instead of Society. Digital forgeries are compared against your Computers DC. Using information gained from a successful forgery usually requires additional checks, including Deception and Society, and casting too wide a net runs the risk of a potential victim figuring out your ruse and turning you in to the authorities.

entities.name: Phreaker
entities.description:
You've learned how to hack using alternative methods. You can use Computers to Disable a Device or Hack a system using any computer, comm unit, or terminal instead of a hacking toolkit. If you're an expert in Computers and the equipment you use is at least 3rd level, you gain a +1 item bonus to Disable a Device or Hack.

**Special** If you have the Combat Hack or Digital Diversion skill feat, you can use this feat to Combat Hack or Create a Diversion without a hacking toolkit.

entities.name: Pit Stop
entities.description: You've learned that in the heat of a race or the frenzy of a chase there's no time to slow down for repairs. You know how to maintain a vehicle without having to slow down. You can perform the Repair activity on a moving vehicle, without the need for a stable surface.

entities.name: Plant Rumor
entities.description:
**Trigger** You perceive a creature attempting a check using Deception, Diplomacy, or Intimidation against another creature's Will DC.

You intercede in a conversation to subtly damage another's reputation and make their argument less compelling. The creature targeted by the triggering check gains a +2 circumstance bonus to its Will DC for that check.

Effect: Plant Rumor

entities.name: Principled Packer
entities.description: You have a reliable system for loading gear. You can open and close a backpack as part of the same Interact action as retrieving a stowed item from it. When using a container, increase the amount of Bulk of items that container can hold that doesn't count against your Bulk limits by 1. If you're an expert in Survival, increase the amount by 2. If you're a master in Survival, increase the amount by 3. If you're legendary in Survival, increase the amount by 4.

entities.name: Programmer
entities.description: You can write computer programs. You can Earn Income using Computers, spending your time programming apps for clients. You can also Craft items with the virtual trait. You can use Programmer to Craft tech items that don't have the virtual trait, but you can only cover up to a quarter of the item's cost in raw materials; the remaining Crafting has to be completed by someone using the Crafting skill.

entities.name: Quick Coercion
entities.description: You can coerce a creature after 1 round of conversation instead of 1 minute. You still can't Coerce a creature in the midst of combat, or without engaging in a conversation.

entities.name: Quick Install
entities.description: You take only 1 minute to Install an Upgrade. If you're legendary in Crafting, you can Install an Upgrade as a 3-action activity.

entities.name: Quick Starter
entities.description: You fly vehicles like you're trying to steal them. Reduce the number of actions to Take Control of an uncontrolled vehicle by one. If this would reduce the number of actions to zero, you can Take Control as a free action. Additionally, you gain the Punch It! action.

entities.name: Repair Expert
entities.description: You restore items to pristine condition. When you succeed at a Crafting check to Repair an item, you restore additional Hit Points to that item equal to your Intelligence modifier. Additionally, you can use Crafting to Treat Wounds on constructs, substituting a repair toolkit for a medkit. You can use Battle Medicine and Continual Recovery with Crafting instead of Medicine while treating constructs, but you must still meet the feats' prerequisites to qualify for these feats.

entities.name: Seasoned
entities.description: You've mastered the preparation of many types of food and drink. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to checks to Craft food and drink, including serums if you have Serum Crafting. If you are a master in one of the prerequisite skills, this bonus increases to +2.

Stats.Prerequisites: trained in Alcohol Lore, Cooking Lore, or Crafting

entities.name: Serum Crafting
entities.description: You can Craft serums and medical items with the consumable trait, though some have other requirements. When you select this feat, you gain formulas for four common serums of 2nd level or lower.

entities.name: Specialty Crafting
entities.description:
Your training focused on Crafting one particular kind of item. Select one of the specialties listed below; you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Crafting checks to Craft items of that type. If you are a master in Crafting, this bonus increases to +2. If it's unclear whether the specialty applies, the GM decides. Some specialties might apply only partially. For example, if you were making an Abadarcorp travel suit and had specialty in textiles, the GM might give you half your bonus because the item requires both armorsmithing and textiles to craft.

SpecialtyApplicable Items

ArmorsmithingArmor, shields and upgrades

ArtistryFine art, including jewelry and solarian crystals

AutomotivesVehicles, including spaceships

ChemicalsAlcohol, ammunition, explosives, and fuel

ComputerComm units, datapads, and virtual items

EngineeringTech gadgets and accessories

GunsmithingFirearms and firearm upgrades

Life ScienceBiotechnology and some pharmaceuticals

RoboticsDrones, mechs, and robots

TextilesClothing, leather, and polymer armor

entities.name: Survey Wildlife
entities.description: You can spend 10 minutes assessing the area around you for signs of creatures. Attempt a Survival check against a DC determined by the GM based on how obvious the signs are. On a success, you can attempt a Recall Knowledge check with a –2 penalty to learn more about the creatures just from these signs. If you're a master in Survival, you don't take the penalty.

entities.name: Terrain Expertise
entities.description:
Your experience in navigating a certain type of terrain makes you supremely confident while doing so. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Survival checks in one of the following types of terrain, chosen when you select this feat: aquatic, arctic, desert, forest, mountain, plains, sky, space, swamp, or underground.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once, choosing a different type of terrain each time.

entities.name: Trick Magic Item
entities.description:
You examine a magic item you normally couldn't use in an effort to fool it and activate it temporarily. For example, this might allow a soldier to cast a spell from a spell gem or spellchip or allow a mystic to cast a spell that's not on their connection's tradition list using a spell gem. You must know what activating the item does, or you can't attempt to trick it.

Attempt a check using the skill matching the item's magic tradition, or matching a tradition that has the spell on its list, if you're trying to cast a spell from the item. The relevant skills are Arcana for arcane, Nature for primal, Occultism for occult, Religion for divine, or any of the four for an item that has the magical trait and not a tradition trait. The GM determines the DC based on the item's level (possibly adjusted depending on the item or situation).

If you activate a magic item that requires a spell attack modifier or spell DC and you don't have proficiency in the relevant statistic, use your level as your proficiency bonus and the highest of your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifiers. If you're a master in the appropriate skill for the item's tradition, you instead use the trained proficiency bonus; if you're legendary, you instead use the expert proficiency bonus.

**Success** For the rest of the current turn, you can spend actions to activate the item as if you could normally use it.

**Failure** You can't use the item or try to trick it again this turn, but you can try again on subsequent turns.

**Critical Failure** You can't use the item, and you can't try to trick it again until your next daily preparations.

Stats.Prerequisites: trained in Arcana, Nature, Occultism, or Religion

entities.name: Urban Survivalist
entities.description: You can use Survival in place of Society to Subsist in cities, space stations, and other settlements. You can also use  instead of Perception to notice hazards in these environments; if you find a hazard in this way, you can also use Survival instead of Thievery to Disable the Device.

entities.name: Virtuosic Performer
entities.description:
You have exceptional talent with one type of performance. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus when making a certain type of performance. If you are a master in Performance, this bonus increases to +2. Select one of the following specialties and apply the bonus when attempting Performance checks of that type. If it's unclear whether the specialty applies, the GM decides.

SpecialtyExamples

ActingDrama, live streams, reality shows

ComedyBuffoonery, joke telling, stand-up routines

DanceBallet, ballroom, interpretive, pop, traditional

KeyboardsKeytar, organ, piano

OratoryEpic, ode, poetry, storytelling

PercussionBells, chimes, drum kit, xylophone

SingingBallad, chant, pop, rock, shanty

StringsGuitar, singing coil, theremin

SynthsSynth deck, turn table

WindsHorn, flute, pipes

entities.name: Without a Trace
entities.description: You're an expert at destroying or removing incriminating evidence from a crime scene. When using the Cover Tracks exploration activity, an yone tracking you must succeed at a Perception check against your Deception, Stealth, or Underworld Lore DC (whichever is highest). If you spent 10 minutes cleaning up a crime scene, anyone investigating the scene must succeed at a Perception check against your Deception, Stealth, or Underworld Lore DC (whichever is highest) to uncover any Hidden evidence.

Stats.Prerequisites: trained in Deception, Stealth, or Underworld Lore

entities.name: Akashic Transcendence
entities.description: Your eye opens to greater truths. You can use Akashic Sync once per round instead of once every 10 minutes.

entities.name: Amplify Glitch
entities.description:
Your body builds primal energy that you can unleash to disable technology. Attempt a  check against all glitching creatures, hazards, and items with the tech trait within 20 feet. The DC is equal to the creature or hazard's Fortitude DC or the Fortitude DC of the creature attending the object, or is based on the item's level if it's unattended. Regardless of the results, each target is then temporarily immune to Amplify Glitch for 1 day.

**Critical Success** Increase target's glitching condition value by 4.

**Success** Increase target's glitching condition value by 2.

entities.name: Confounding Aerobatics
entities.description: When you successfully Maneuver in Flight, compare the results of your Acrobatics check against the Reflex DC of one creature you were adjacent to at any point during your movement. On a success, the creature is Off-Guard to the next Strike you make before the end of your turn.

entities.name: Fly Anything
entities.description: You can intuit how even the most interesting vehicles function. You can pilot a ship even if it would be physiologically impossible for you, including those that require telepathy or other supernatural abilities. You can use Piloting instead of Crafting to Repair a part of a vehicle, starship, or mech with a –2 circumstance penalty as long as you have the appropriate parts available to you. You can use Piloting instead of Computers to Hack a vehicle, starship, or mech with a –2 circumstance penalty.

entities.name: Gift Grenade
entities.description:
**Requirements** You're holding a grenade.

You attempt to slip a grenade onto a foe, then slip away before it blows. Attempt a  check against an adjacent creature's Perception DC, then you Stride.

**Critical Success** The grenade explodes after you Stride. The target treats the result of its saving throw as one degree of success worse.

**Success** The grenade explodes after you Stride.

**Failure** The grenade explodes after you Stride, but the target notices your actions. The target treats the result of its saving throw as one degree of success better.

**Critical Failure** The grenade explodes before you Stride, catching you in the blast.

entities.name: Legendary Performer
entities.description: Your fame has spread throughout the galaxy. Creatures who have any listed skill in Society have heard of you and usually have an attitude toward you one step better than normal, depending on your reputation and the creature's disposition. For instance, if you're well-known for cruel and demanding behavior, creatures might be intimidated by you, rather than be friendly toward you. When you Earn Income with Performance, you attract higher-level audiences than your location would allow, as audiences flock to see you. For instance, famous socialites and spectra might travel to a dive bar in a backwater port to hear you perform. Typically, this increases the audiences available to your level or by two levels, whichever is higher.

entities.name: Legendary Professional
entities.description: Your fame has spread throughout the galaxy (for instance, if you have Warfare Lore, you might be a legendary general or tactician). This works as Legendary Performer, except you gain higher-level jobs when you Earn Income with Lore.

entities.name: Legendary Troll
entities.description:
**Requirements** You or your target are using a comm unit, datapad, or other computer.

Attempt a  check against the Will DC of a target within 60 feet. On a success, the target is Off-Guard for 1 round, and on a critical success, it's Confused for 1 round. The target's reaction gives you information about it as though you'd attempted to Recall Knowledge using an appropriate skill and received the same result on your roll. The target is then temporarily immune to your Legendary Troll attempts for 24 hours.

entities.name: Unified Theory
entities.description: You understand the common underpinnings of the four traditions of magic and magical essences. Whenever you use a skill action or a skill feat that requires a Nature, Occultism, or Religion check, depending on the magic tradition, you can use Arcana instead. If you would normally take a penalty or have a higher DC for using Arcana on other magic (such as when using Identify Magic), you no longer do so.

entities.name: Combat Hack
entities.description:
**Requirements** You are holding or wearing a hacking toolkit and have a free hand.

Attempt a Computers check to Hack an adjacent creature, hazard, or item with the tech trait. The DC is equal to the creature, item, or hazard's Fortitude DC, or the Fortitude DC of the creature attending the object. If the target is an unattended object, the GM sets the DC for the check based on the item's level. The target is temporarily immune to your attempts to Combat Hack it for 10 minutes.

**Critical Success** The target becomes Glitching 2.

**Success** The target becomes Glitching 1.

**Critical Failure** If the target has the glitching condition, reduce the value of its glitching condition by 1.

entities.name: Confabulator
entities.description: You pile lie upon lie. Reduce the circumstance bonus a target gains for your previous attempts to Create a Diversion or Lie to it from +4 to +2. If you're a master in Deception, reduce the bonus to +1, and if you're legendary, your targets don't get these bonuses at all.

entities.name: Crowd Control
entities.description:
Your voice can be heard over the noise in a crowd. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Diplomacy checks against crowds. The first time each round you Stride into a square containing a crowd, you can attempt a DC 20 check to move the crowd out of your way. A GM might use a different DC under certain circumstances, such as when the crowd has a level or set DC to disperse.

**Critical Success** As success, and the crowd departs from all adjacent squares as you move.

**Success** The crowd disperses from squares you move into.

**Failure** The crowd doesn't move, but you can continue moving.

**Critical Failure** The crowd forcefully resists you and disrupts your Stride.

entities.name: Delayed Disable
entities.description: Your sabotage takes effect when the time is right. When you Disable a Device, you can delay the device from becoming disabled for up to 24 hours or until someone attempts to use the device. In most cases, creatures have a chance to detect that the device is disabled only if they use the seek action to attempt Perception checks against your Thievery DC. If you rolled a critical success on your Thievery check to Disable a Device, other creatures can't figure out the device will become disabled, and you can safely activate the device without triggering or ending the effect of Delayed Disable.

entities.name: Disinformation Dealer
entities.description: You convince others to do their own research using specifically curated data and misinformation you casually guide them into finding on the infosphere. The first time you fail to Lie to the target (but not critically fail), you convince them that you were given faulty information, the data isn't all in yet, or you were both mislead, and the target doesn't gain a circumstance bonus against your further attempts to Lie to them. If you're a master in Deception, you can fail to Lie twice in the same conversation before they begin to suspect you, or four times if you're legendary in Deception.

entities.name: Dive for Cover
entities.description: When threatened, you can quickly take a dive and find somewhere to hunker down. You Leap, land Prone, and immediately Take Cover, which allows you to hunker down and gain greater cover against ranged attacks.

entities.name: Drift Racer
entities.description: You're well-versed in the street racing technique known as drifting, or sliding your vehicle through the entirety of a curve while maintaining speed and showcasing your driving skills. While piloting a land vehicle, when you perform Piloting actions with the reckless trait, your vehicle only becomes uncontrolled on a critical failure. On a failure, the vehicle moves as described under reckless piloting, except that you, not the GM, control where the vehicle drifts. You can choose to fail (but not critically fail) a reckless Piloting action. The GM, however, has discretion as to when a vehicle you're piloting is too large or unwieldy for this technique to be viable—it's a move that works with sports hovercars and not long-hauler transports (generally).

entities.name: Feign Death
entities.description:
**Trigger** You take damage.

You lie Prone and Impersonate a corpse. As long as you don't take any actions requiring anything other than your mind, you appear dead. To see through your ruse, a creature must succeed at a check against your Deception DC, either by Seeking or Recalling Knowledge. You can Ready an Action without ending this effect if you're a master in Deception.

entities.name: Inventor
entities.description:
You are a genius at Crafting, easily able to determine how things are made and create new inventions. You can spend downtime to invent a common formula that you don't know. This works just like the Craft activity: you spend half the Price of the formula up front, attempt a Crafting check, and on a success either finish the formula by paying the difference or work for longer to decrease the Price. The difference is that you spend the additional time in research, design, and development, rather than in creating an item. Once it's complete, you add the new formula you invented to your formula book.

The GM might allow you to invent uncommon or rare formulas, typically with an increased DC. You need the Magical Crafting feat to invent hybrid and magical formula.

entities.name: Kiss it Better
entities.description:
**Requirements** You have a hand free and are adjacent to an ally who isn't at full Hit Points.

You perform a token medical effort to convince an ally they've recovered from an injury. Attempt a Deception check with the same DC as for Treat Wounds. On a success, the target gains temporary Hit Points equal to half the corresponding amount of Hit Points from Treat Wounds. These temporary Hit Points last 1 round. Kiss It Better doesn't remove the wounded condition. The target is temporarily immune to Kiss It Better for 24 hours.

entities.name: Marathon Streamer
entities.description: Whether you're frequently plugging sponsors, talking to chat, or showing off merch, you're always performing for the cameras. You can Earn Income after Livestreaming for 24 hours in exploration mode. These hours don't need to be consecutive, but each show must be at least 1 hour long to count toward the total number of hours required to roll to determine your earnings. If you're an expert in Performance, you only need 12 hours to receive earnings. If you're a master in Performance, you only need 8 hours. If you're legendary in Performance, you only need 1 hour. You can receive earnings only once per day.

entities.name: Percussive Maintenance
entities.description:
**Requirements** You're holding a tech item that has the glitching condition.

You try to repair an item by smashing it against a hard surface. Attempt a DC 10.

**Critical Success** Reduce the glitching condition by 2.

**Success** Reduce the glitching condition by 1.

entities.name: Primal Sabotage
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes

You can combat technology with the bounty of the natural world. Attempt a  check and smear blood, mud, or another natural substance on an adjacent creature, hazard, or item with the tech trait to disrupt it with primal energy. The DC is equal to the creature's, item's, or hazard's Fortitude DC, or the Fortitude DC of the creature attending the object. If the target is an unattended object, the GM sets the DC for the check based on the item's level. The target is then temporarily immune to your attempts to Primal Sabotage it for 1 hour.

**Critical Success** The target becomes Glitching 2.

**Success** The target becomes Glitching 1.

**Critical Failure** The nature spirits rebuke you, causing a random piece of tech gear you own to become glitching 1.

entities.name: Stunt Maneuver
entities.description: Whether you're a natural ace or a veteran pilot, you can push a vehicle to perform incredible stunts. Remove the reckless trait when you attempt a Stunt with a –1 penalty. If you're a master in Piloting, remove the reckless trait when you attempt a Stunt with a –2 penalty or lower. If you're legendary in Piloting, remove the reckless trait from any Stunt you attempt.

entities.name: Tech Crafting
entities.description: You can Craft level 1 or higher tech items, though some have other requirements. When you select this feat, you gain formulas for four common tech items of 2nd level or lower.

entities.name: Vehicular Menace
entities.description: You're a menace behind the wheel! When you attempt to Run Over creatures with a vehicle you're Piloting, you can attempt to demoralize one creature in your path. If you're a master in Piloting, you can Demoralize up to two creatures in your path, or up to three creatures if you're legendary in Piloting.

entities.name: Power Slide
entities.description: You throw the vehicle into a barely controlled skid, turning sharply to evade pursuit. You Drive with a –2 penalty to your Piloting check, gaining the effects of the Drive action for the same number of actions you spent to Power Slide. At the end of the movement, if you succeed, you can turn the vehicle up to 90 degrees. If you critically succeed at your Piloting check, you can instead turn the vehicle up to 180 degrees.

entities.name: Take the Wheel
entities.description: You Board and Take Control of an adjacent vehicle.

entities.name: Aerobatics Mastery
entities.description:
You can gracefully perform aerial stunts as if flying were second nature. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Acrobatics checks to Maneuver in Flight and can combine two maneuvers into a single action, such as reversing direction while making a steep descent or hovering in gale force winds. The DC of the Acrobatics check is equal to the DC of the most difficult maneuver + 5.

If you're legendary in Acrobatics, you can combine three such maneuvers into a single action; the DC of the Acrobatics check is equal to the DC of the most difficult maneuver + 10. Regardless of the combination, these maneuvers rarely allow you to move further than your fly Speed.

entities.name: Akashic Sync
entities.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes

You can briefly connect to the Akashic Records. You Recall Knowledge using Occultism instead of any other skill as though Occultism were applicable to perform Recall Knowledge for that topic.

**Critical Success** You recall accurately and gain three pieces of information or context.

**Success** You recall accurately and gain two pieces of information or context and a piece of erroneous information, but you don't have any way to differentiate which is which.

**Failure** You gain a piece of information or context and two pieces of erroneous information.

**Critical Failure** You gain three pieces of erroneous information.

entities.name: Booster Rip
entities.description:
**Trigger** You successfully Strike and deal damage with a boost melee weapon charged to deal additional damage.

You launch yourself across the battlefield using your boosted weapon. This energy pushes you 20 feet directly back from your target. This movement doesn't trigger reactions.

entities.name: Chat, Help!
entities.description: When you roll initiative, if you're Livestreaming, you can ask chat for some help. You Recall Knowledge about a creature you and your livestream audience can see, using a Performance check in place of the usual skill. For this action, you can't use any special abilities, reactions, or free actions that trigger when you Recall Knowledge.

entities.name: Critical Care
entities.description: When you administer a consumable that restores Hit Points to a creature, you can apply it to maximum effect, pinpointing vital parts of your patient's anatomy. When you do, instead of rolling dice, the consumable heals the maximum possible amount. The target is then temporarily immune to your Critical Care for 1 day.

entities.name: Deific Obedience
entities.description: You've dedicated yourself to a deity or pantheon. As long as you follow the edicts and anathema of that deity, you gain their granted 1st-rank spell as a divine innate spell you can cast once per day, heightened to 3rd rank; if you're legendary, the spell is heightened to 4th rank. If you repeatedly break your deity's edicts or perform anathemas, you lose this ability, and it can only be regained with an atone ritual.

Stats.Prerequisites: master in Religion, follower of a specific religion

entities.name: Fool the Camera
entities.description: You know how to fool security cameras and tech items that confer special senses, such as scopes. Whenever you use the Avoid Notice, Hide, or Sneak actions, you're always considered to be taking precautions against special senses from tech items. In addition, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Stealth DC to Avoid Notice by cameras and technological hazards.

entities.name: Predator's Eye
entities.description: Your eye magnifies distant targets as well as a scope. You can adjust your sight in that eye as a single action to Seek a specific creature with a +2 circumstance bonus to your Perception check, or Seek to search a 10-foot square up to 100 feet away for any undetected or Hidden creatures or objects. You don't take penalties for an object or creature being too far away unless you're more than 2 miles away.

entities.name: Push It
entities.description: Whenever you succeed at a Piloting check, the vehicle you're piloting gains a +10-foot circumstance bonus to all its Speeds until the end of your turn. If you critically succeed, this bonus increases to +15 feet.

entities.name: Religious Talisman
entities.description: You can construct and bless a religious symbol of your deity in 10 minutes. While such talismans are traditionally scraps of paper with a religious symbol drawn on them, they can take many forms, including body art, a sticker, or even a virtual emoji. You can create a talisman only for yourself and for the deity you worship. As long as you continue to engage in activities that match your deity's edicts you gain a +1 status bonus to initiative rolls. If you violate your deity's anathema, the talisman is destroyed, and you take a –1 status penalty to initiative rolls and Perception checks until you complete an Atone ritual.

Stats.Prerequisites: trained in Religion, follower of a specific religion

entities.name: Shameless Request
