**Effect** The war machine self-destructs, dealing 12d6 electricity |options:area-damage damage (DC 30 save) to all creatures in a 60-foot radius. For 1 minute after this ability is used, any creature that touches the war machine's remains is exposed to incredible radiation sickness.

**Reactive Strike.** 

**Thermal Shadow.** 10 feet. The war machine collects and reflects thermal energy to mask its presence. Any creatures targeting the war machine from outside the aura treats it as if it were Concealed unless they possess scent or a non-visual–based sense.

**Tentacle Flurry.** The war machine makes a tentacle Strike against up to four creatures in reach, rolling the attack and damage roll only once for all targets.

**Thoughtlance.** A creature touched by one of the war machine's tentacles must attempt a DC 30 save, becoming Slowed 1 on a failure (or Slowed 2 on a critical failure). Each time an affected creature ends its turn, its slowed valued decreases by 1.

entities.name: Biotech Ultimate War Machine
entities.description:
Only one member of the Stewards has ever encountered the biotechnical horror known as code name "moonflower" and lived to tell the tale—and only after they emerged from a months-long coma. According to her story, a single moonflower war machine was responsible for the massacre of Liavaran moon S-117, which used to house an entire Stewards deep space telescope array and planetary defense battery.

The incursion began with a series of probes detected by anacites on Aballon. Strange machines with blazing sensors and articulated tentacles appeared out of nowhere, ripping through infrastructure seemingly at random and collecting intelligence all around Pact Worlds space. Panic spread fast, but since the machines always vanished without a trace, or exploded when captured, the sightings couldn't be confirmed or identified. Rumors began to circulate that the machines were a form of biotech never encountered before. Soon the Stewards became formally involved, shuttering the incidents behind the adamantine partition of top security clearance.

In Sarenith of 325 ag, after dozens of military operations failed to engage the elusive probes, a wing of fighters dispatched from the Idari finally got lucky and disabled one of the machines before it could self-destruct. Coaxed into giving up some of its secrets by top Pact Worlds scientists, the biotech vessel became the prototype for the "home grown" remote war machines that are currently being tested for use in combat. The replicas aren't alive but are built using robotic construction templates since the core of the original biotech design has proven too complicated to reverse engineer with Pact technology.

Remote war machines are proxies that can be controlled from a great distance. The original biotech war machines connect to the pilot's mind through a psychic link or unknown radio frequency. Robotic remote war machines connect to a computer via data link, allowing the pilot to control their proxy using a keyboard, virtual reality rig, or even a vidgame controller.

Notes.Abilities:
**Constant Pulse Radar.** The war machine can detect all creatures and objects within 100 feet of itself, treating hidden, invisible, and unobserved creatures as Concealed.

**Interstellar Comms.** A remote war machine maintains a constant data link with its pilot, using its pilot's languages and skill modifiers for any unlisted skill. In addition, the pilot can speak through the data link using the remote war machine as a mouthpiece.

**Corpse Flower.** **Trigger** The war machine would be reduced to 0 Hit Points

**Effect** The war machine self-destructs, dealing 16d6 electricity |options:area-damage damage (DC 36 save) to all creatures in a 60-foot radius. For 1 minute after this ability is used, any creature that touches the war machine's remains is exposed to incredible radiation sickness.

**Psionic Flare.** **Trigger** A creature within 60 feet of the war machine Casts a Spell

**Effect** The war machine fires a focused lightning beam targeting only the triggering creature. If the creature fails its save, the spell becomes weakened. If the weakened spell requires a saving throw, the target uses the outcome one degree of success better than the result of its roll. If the weakened spell requires a spell attack, that attack roll takes a –4 circumstance penalty.

**Radio Silence.** 60 feet. Non-allied comm units and other computers don't function within the remote war machine's aura unless their operator succeeds at a  check against the war machine's Stealth DC as an Interact action.

**Reactive Strike.** 

**Swirling Shield.** 1 to 3

The remote war machine's tentacles surround it in defensive patterns. For 1 minute, it gains a number of reactions equal to the number of actions spent on Swirling Shield. These extra reactions can be used only for Psionic Flare or Reactive Strike.

**Tentacle Flurry.** The war machine makes a tentacle Strike against up to four creatures in reach, rolling the attack and damage roll only once for all targets.

**Thermal Camouflage.** The war machine becomes Invisible for 1 minute or until it attempts to make a Strike.

entities.name: Blight Drake
entities.description:
Blight drakes have a well-earned reputation among draconic creatures for stench and pollution. They corrupt the air around them with the sort of filth and decay commonly found in the worst kinds of industrialization. These solitary monstrosities resemble their swamp-dwelling draconic cousins but are often surrounded with a miasma of thick, choking smog. Blight drakes revel in befouling clean and verdant environments, leaving a permanent trail of filth in their wake.

Drakes resemble their larger draconic cousins in more than just scaled, monstrous acclaim. Ranging in size from the diminutive fey drake to the massive, ship-sized star drake, drakes share a dragons' winged reptilian form, long necks, and breath weapons. But where dragons often have forelimbs and wings, a drake typically only has one or the other. Their long, winding tails and sharp jaws more than make up for this lack, however.

Despite being more animalistic than dragons, drakes still possess a formidable cunning, and most share a dragon's ability to generate some form of breath weapon. However, their lack of intelligence makes drakes substantially easier to domesticate than other draconic creatures, and their familial nature makes them excellent pack hunters.

Notes.Abilities:
**Wing Deflection.** **Trigger** The blight drake is targeted with an attack from a creature they can see

**Effect** The blight drake raises their wing, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack. If the blight drake is flying, they descend 10 feet after the attack is complete.

**Draconic Frenzy.** The drake makes two jaws Strikes and one tail Strike in any order.

**Smokestack.** The blight drake blasts a thick, fetid smog from slits around their neck, creating a cloud of smoke in a 20-foot burst within 120 feet and that remains for 1d4 rounds. All creatures within the cloud become Concealed, and all creatures outside the cloud become concealed to creatures in it.

Each creature that begins its turn inside the cloud takes 5d6 poison |options:area-damage damage (DC 28 save). A creature that fails the save is also Sickened 1 (Sickened 2 on a critical failure).

**Toxic Breath.** The blight drake spews a fetid ball of polluted putrescence up to a range of 60 feet that explodes in a 15-foot burst. Creatures within the burst take 4d8 acid ,4d8 poison |options:area-damage damage (DC 28 save). The blight drake can't use Toxic Breath again for 1d4 rounds.

**Infrared Vision.** A bloodbrother can detect infrared radiation (such as that given off by warm-blooded creatures) as a precise sense at the listed range.

**Frigid Cold.** 10 feet. A bloodbrother's flesh radiates intense cold. A creature that starts its turn in the area must succeed at a DC 22 save or become Fatigued while it remains in the area. Creatures immune to environmental cold effects or with any cold resistance are immune.

**Drain Vital Fluids.** **Frequency** once per round

**Requirements** A creature is imprisoned in the bloodbrother's ribcage prison

**Effect** The bloodbrother drains the vital fluids from the imprisoned creature. The victim is Drained 1 (or increases its drained value by 1), and the bloodbrother regains 10 healing Hit Points, gaining any excess Hit Points as temporary Hit Points that last for 1 minute.

**Frigid Touch.** A creature that begins its turn Grabbed or Restrained by the bloodbrother takes 1d8 cold damage.

**Grisly Ambush.** **Trigger** The bloodbrother hits a creature in the first round of combat, and the bloodbrother was hidden from that creature at the start of combat

**Effect** Each enemy within 30 feet that witnesses the attack (including the target of the attack) must attempt a DC 25 save. On a failure, the creature is Frightened 2 (or Frightened 4 on a critical failure).

**Ice Passage.** A bloodbrother ignores difficult terrain from ice and snow and doesn't risk falling when crossing ice.

**Imprison.** **Requirements** The bloodbrother has a Large or smaller creature Grabbed or Restrained with their bone spur

**Effect** The bloodbrother tries to imprison the required creature in their ribcage prison. The bloodbrother attempts an  check against the creature's Reflex DC, imprisoning it on a success. The bloodbrother's bone spur is no longer grabbing or restraining the creature they've imprisoned, so the bloodbrother is free to use their bone spur Strike once again. The bloodbrother can't attack a creature they've imprisoned and can have only one creature imprisoned in their ribcage prison at a time. An imprisoned creature is restrained (escape dc=25) and temporarily immune to the bloodbrother's frigid touch while restrained.

entities.name: Botnib
entities.description:
The lowly botnib, also called a computer glitch gremlin, is intuitively tied with the computerized devices and networks of the modern age. These cavorting fey make it their mission to create as much havoc as they can by influencing computer systems and creating chaos in their wake. Known for their innate ability to communicate with digital devices, computer glitch gremlins routinely become infatuated with such systems, which they subvert like one might put together a fun puzzle.

Gremlins have plagued the Universe with cruel tricks since long before the Gap, and they've fully adapted to a galaxy filled with technology. Whether meddling with a comm unit, a starship, or an entire space station, gremlins delight in ruination and chaos.

Notes.Abilities:
**Digital Telepathy.** A botnib can communicate telepathically with digital devices and with other creatures that can do so (such as other botnibs). This allows the botnib to attempt Computers checks to access any computer within the telepathy's range.

**Techsense.** The botnib can sense items and creatures with the tech trait within 100 feet.

**Glitch Aura.** 20 feet. Creatures and items with the tech trait struggle to function reliably when near a botnib. Creatures with the tech trait, unattended items with the tech trait, or creatures holding equipment with the tech trait that start their turn in the aura must attempt a DC 16 save.

**Critical Success** No effect, and the creature or item is temporarily immune to the botnib's glitch aura for 1 minute.

**Success** The creature or items are unaffected.

**Failure** The creature, item, or all the creature's held items become Glitching 1.

**Critical Failure** As failure, but Glitching 2.
Notes.Spells: Delete, Electric Arc, Figment, Recharge Weapon, Thunderstrike

entities.name: Caypin
entities.description: Caypins are brawny predators with the agility of wolves and the scaly skin of crocodiles. Their most striking feature is a mass of wriggling, semi-sentient appendages that cover their heads. Each of these tentacle-like protuberances contains a bloodshot eyeball and a gaping mouth full of teeth, and the caypin—which has no eyes or mouth of its own—relies on these orifices to see and feed. Nutrients absorbed by the appendages are passed to the caypin via tiny receptive sockets in the beast's jaw, and caypins can detach these appendages into writhing clusters that independently move up to 100 feet from their bodies. In the wild, caypins use these clusters to ambush prey, and the creatures are known across the galaxy for their rapacious ability to consume half of their body weight in raw meat.

Notes.Abilities:
**Appendage Cluster.** A caypin's detached appendage cluster is a Small, mindless, semi-independent creature controlled by the caypin. It has the minion trait, darkvision, 30 healing Hit Points, a land Speed of 20 feet, and a swim Speed of 15 feet. It shares the caypin's AC, saving throw bonuses, and skill modifiers. The caypin can see what its appendage cluster sees and otherwise shares its senses with the cluster. Each round, the caypin can Command a Minion to grant an appendage cluster 2 actions. An appendage cluster can make jaws Strikes (**Melee** 1 jaws +14, **Damage** 2d4+3 piercing) and has the Cluster Onslaught ability.

If the caypin is killed, any detached appendage clusters are also killed. Any appendage cluster that moves more than 100 feet from the caypin dies instantly.

If both the caypin's detached appendage clusters are destroyed but the caypin still lives, the caypin is Blinded until it regrows at least one of its appendage clusters. A dead appendage cluster regrows in 3 days.

**Aquatic Ambush.** 40 feet

**Requirements** The monster is hiding in water and a creature that hasn't detected it is within the listed number of feet

**Effect** The monster moves up to its swim Speed + 10 feet toward the triggering creature, traveling on water and on land. Once the creature is in reach, the monster makes a Strike against it. The creature is Off-Guard against this Strike.

**Detach Cluster.** The caypin detaches half of its facial appendages into an Appendage Cluster that occupies a single adjacent square of its choice. A caypin can have up to two appendage clusters detached at a time, and if both clusters are detached, the caypin can't make jaws Strikes or Detach Cluster again until at least one cluster reattaches. An adjacent appendage cluster can reattach to the caypin with an Interact action.

entities.name: Cerebinite
entities.description:
The mineral cerebinium, also known as memory crystal, naturally appears in the broken region of space known as Kazmurg's Absurdity. Typically, these minerals develop in remote subterranean locations, where they grow based on the presence of thinking minds within a planetary range. The more active minds in a region, the faster these mineral formations grow. A major world of millions can easily create vast underground stores, and in these majestic caverns, cerebinites spontaneously emerge.

Cerebinites are essentially mindless creatures—save for the memories that power them—who have developed as an offshoot of cerebinium growth. Though possessing no intellect of their own, they act off the impulses provided by the memories stored within the crystals that constitute their forms. In many ways, a cerebinite is like the many oozes that lie in wait throughout the cosmos.

Encountering these active mineral deposits often requires a delicate approach, as cerebinites can engage up close or at a short range by hurling cerebinium spikes and blasts of cerebinium shards charged with memories drawn from their surroundings. Even in death, these masses of cerebinium explode in a destructive burst of psychic energy, affecting the minds of those nearby with jumbled visions of countless different lives. When multiple injured cerebinites gather near one another, this proximity can cause an especially destructive chain reaction due to cerebinites' own susceptibility to mental attacks.

Stats.Immunities: acid, bleed, critical-hits, precision, unconscious, visual

Notes.Abilities:
**Thoughtsense.** 

**Crystalline Ambush.** **Trigger** A non-mindless creature enters a space adjacent to a cerebinite

**Requirements** Initiative hasn't yet been rolled

**Effect** The cerebinite automatically notices the creature, makes a crystalline growth Strike against one creature adjacent to itself, then rolls initiative.

**Mind-Shattering Demise.** When the cerebinite dies, it explodes in a blast fueled by the memories stored in its crystalline body, affecting all creatures in a 30-foot. Each creature in the area (including other cerebinites) must succeed at a DC 22 save or take 2d8 mental |options:area-damage damage and become Stunned 1 (or double damage and Stunned 2 on a critical failure).

**Constrict.** 1d8 bludgeoning ,1d6 mental, DC 22

entities.name: Civusdaemon
entities.description:
Born from infospheres and digital networks, the civusdaemon is a force of malign intent who bends online spaces to torment mortals. Representing death through oppression and hate from social media, these daemons act in the shadows, tormenting their foes to such a ruinous extent that they often take their own life.

Hailing from the plane of Abaddon, daemons are utterly devoted to the destruction of all life. Their existence is based around specific means of death, and they seek the death of all things in service to their lords: the Apocalypse Riders. Each daemon represents a different way to die, and they use their specific powers to further that means of death.

Advents in technology have only created new means of death and torment, so new types of daemons enter existence with regularity, each created once a sufficient mass of new deaths occurs to spawn them. These new advent daemons often prefer to spend their time in the galaxy rather than Abaddon, as they can better spread their torments to the mortals of creation.

Notes.Abilities:
**Telepathy.** 100 feet

**Eyes on the Infosphere.** A civusdaemon knows the presence of any creatures connected to any local infospheres it has access to. A creature who is connected to an infosphere is visible to the civusdaemon as a precise sense. Disconnected creatures who've been active on an infosphere within the past day leave enough residual trace that a civusdaemon can sense them as an imprecise sense.

**+1 Status to All Saves vs. Mental.** 

**Profile Picture.** A civusdaemon appears as a strangely two-dimensional version of a creature of their choice. Creatures targeting the civusdaemon must succeed at a DC 5 to do so, as if the civusdaemon were Concealed. A creature who succeeds at this check automatically succeeds at further such flat checks for 1 round.

**Well, Actually.** **Frequency** once per day

**Trigger** An enemy critically hits the civusdaemon or the civusdaemon critically fails a save against an enemy's effect

**Effect** The attack becomes a hit instead of a critical hit, or the critical failure on the save becomes a failure instead.

**Character Assassination.** The civusdaemon targets the online reputation of a creature it's aware of on a shared infosphere. After 1 day of downtime, the civusdaemon attempts a  check against the target's Computers DC.

If successful, the target takes a –2 circumstance penalty to all checks made on that infosphere because of damage to their reputation. The civusdaemon can maintain this effect each day by spending another day of downtime without needing to attempt an additional check.

If the civusdaemon maintains this for a week or more, the penalty increases to –4. The creature or an ally of the creature can spend a day of downtime to attempt a DC 26, DC 26 or DC 26 check to counter the character attack.

On a success, the civusdaemon's efforts end, and the target becomes immune to this ability for 1 month.

On a critical success, the target or ally also identifies a specific location that the civusdaemon operates out of, such as one where it frequently connects to the infosphere.
Notes.Spells: Nightmare, Suggestion, Clairaudience, Mind Reading, Selective Invisibility (At Will), Share Pain, Detect Thoughts, Doom Scroll (At Will), Analyze Target, Detect Magic, Injury Echo

entities.name: Clangit
entities.description:
Clangits, or space station gremlins, know everything about the inner workings of their home stations and enjoy punishing or pranking the station's larger inhabitants who know less than they do. "Haunted" space stations and ships with mysterious power flickers, doors that randomly open and shut, equipment that malfunctions at just the wrong time, and frequent unexplainable accidents are probably the home of one or more clangits.

When they aren't playing pranks, some clangits monitor and repair the sensitive machinery keeping many older space stations afloat—a fact that has probably saved them from eradication on larger settlements like Absalom Station. Most clangits stand about 2 feet tall and weigh around 7 pounds—the perfect size for slipping through vents and squeezing down maintenance tunnels.

Gremlins have plagued the Universe with cruel tricks since long before the Gap, and they've fully adapted to a galaxy filled with technology. Whether meddling with a comm unit, a starship, or an entire space station, gremlins delight in ruination and chaos.

Notes.Abilities:
**Mechanical Trickery.** When a clangit has spent at least 1 hour exploring a ship or space station, the gremlin gains an innate sense of its inner workings and can remotely control mechanical infrastructure within 60 feet, performing simple actions such as opening and shutting airlocks and doors, opening heat vents, activating alarms, turning lights on and off, or tampering with gravity controls.

**Tech Travel.** The clangit enters adjacent mechanical infrastructure, such as a control panel or pipe network, and instantly emerges from another within 100 feet.
Notes.Spells: Invisibility, Adhere, Electric Arc, Figment, Illusory Object, Overheat, Recharge Weapon

entities.name: Cloud Ray
entities.description: Enormous cloud rays are apex predators on gas giants such as Bretheda and Liavara. Cloud rays are incredibly maneuverable and can fly through the atmosphere at speeds few can match, rendering them nearly inescapable when on the hunt.

Notes.Abilities:
**Explosive Death.** If a cloud ray dies due to fire or electricity damage, its internal reservoirs of explosive gases and combustible fluids detonate in a 20-foot emanation that deals 11d8 fire |options:area-damage damage (DC 30 save).

**Engulf.** DC 30, 3d8+8 bludgeoning damage, escape dc=30, Rupture 25

**Lash Out.** The cloud ray makes two consecutive tail lash Strikes at a –2 penalty against any targets within reach. These attacks count toward the cloud ray's multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after it makes all its attacks.

**Natural Thruster.** **Frequency** once per hour

**Effect** Until the beginning of its next turn, the cloud ray gains a +80-foot status bonus to its fly Speed and deals an additional 1d10 slashing damage with its tail Strikes.

**Stunning Lash.** A creature that takes electricity damage from a cloud ray's tail Strike is Stunned 1 (Stunned 2 on a critical hit), then becomes temporarily immune to stunning lash for 1 minute. Creatures with a weakness to electricity don't become temporarily immune.

entities.name: Cloud Skate
entities.description: Cloud skates are skittish creatures that avoid settlements whenever possible. They travel in large packs when in their docile periods and remain in small groups even during their aggressive hunting cycles, making them dangerous to travelers. They navigate through the clouds using three powerful tails, trapping prey with huge, baleen-filled mouths that span the full width of their single-segmented bodies.

Notes.Abilities:
**Explosive Death.** If a cloud skate dies due to fire or electricity damage, its internal reservoirs of explosive gases and combustible fluids detonate in a 20-foot emanation that deals 6d8 fire |options:area-damage damage (DC 21 save).

**Engulf.** DC 21, 2d6+3 bludgeoning damage, escape dc=21, Rupture 12

**Natural Thruster.** **Frequency** once per hour

**Effect** Until the beginning of its next turn, the cloud skate gains a +75-foot status bonus to its fly Speed and deals an additional 1d10 slashing damage with its tail Strikes.

entities.name: Coposirix
entities.description: The rapid and careless industrialization of Tabrid Minor ruined the planet, particularly ravaging the population of copi—the coral that's the ancestor of the native copaxi people. In areas where the copi's magical connection to gravity was strongest, however, the rampant pollution instead mutated it into grotesque new forms. In a twisted mockery of copaxi evolution, clusters of copi fused together to form coposirixes, shambling mounds of mutated copi fused with a partial shell of crystallized waste that crackles and creaks as it moves. The form of a coposirix constantly changes, sometimes even taking on hauntingly humanoid features that melt away just as quickly.

Notes.Abilities:
**Seep In.** **Trigger** The coposirix takes damage

**Effect** The coposirix's body absorbs some of what damaged it until the end of its next turn, the material seeping into its constituent copi and changing its composition. The effects of this change depends on the nature of the damage.

- **Energy Damage** The coposirix's attacks deal an additional 2d6 damage of the same type as the energy damage dealt to it.

- **Physical Damage** The coposirix gains resistance 6 to physical damage. If the damage was dealt by a weapon made of a special material, such as silver, the coposirix's battering sludge Strike counts as that same material for the duration of the effect.

**Falling Rush.** The coposirix bends gravity around itself, causing it to fall toward its target. The coposirix Strides up to twice its Speed in a straight line in any direction. If it ends this movement within melee reach of at least one enemy, it can make a battering sludge Strike against that target. After this attack, the coposirix falls if it isn't on a solid surface, taking half the normal amount of damage for the distance fallen and not falling Prone. If the coposirix passes within 10 feet of another creature at any point during this movement, that creature is affected by the fluctuating gravity and must attempt a DC 25 save.

**Critical Success** The creature can use the fluctuating gravity to its advantage to reposition itself. It can Step as a free action.

**Success** No effect.

**Failure** The creature is pulled 5 feet in the direction of the coposirix's travel. This follows the rules for forced movement. If at the end of this movement the creature is unsupported, it falls and lands prone, taking fall damage as normal.

**Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature is pulled 10 feet and falls prone even if supported.

entities.name: Corchaaz
entities.description:
The crab-like corchaazes of Tabrid Minor build their shells from copi, a coral-like polyp that also constitutes the bodies of humanoid copaxis. Copi contain hollows that collapse matter into dense stores, creating pressurized chambers that emulate black holes. Corchaazes break down copi with their claws and add the material to their shells, creating gravity wells on their bodies. Corchaazes are effectively immortal unless they die of injury or illness. Legend has it their shells continue to grow as they age—copaxi folk tales describe corchaazes as big as islands.

A coastal shelf collapse on Tabrid Minor in 322 ag destroyed the planet's major corchaaz spawning ground, but this wasn't the end for this hardy species. In 324 ag, a team of scientists in a nearby star system noticed wildly fluctuating gravimetric readings. Following the weird readings, the scientists discovered and tracked a group of corchaazes traveling along a local Drift lane. Corchaaz migrations were new, and many scientists were eager to study rafts, as the migratory groups were called. More corchaaz rafts showed up the following year in other systems, including the Ghavaniska and Pact Systems.

Notes.Abilities:
**Gravity Well.** 20 feet. The corchaaz's body pulls nearby creatures toward it with dense gravitational forces. A creature that ends it turn within the aura must succeed at a DC 20 save or be pulled 10 feet toward the corchaaz (also landing Prone on a critical failure).

**Interstellar Raft.** A corchaaz can combine its gravitational forces with other willing corchaazes into an interstellar raft as an exploration activity that takes 10 minutes. While part of an interstellar raft, the corchaazes must remain within 100 feet of each other. Additionally, the raft members gain a 40-foot fly Speed and the cosmic trait (both of which they keep for 1 hour after this ability ends). An individual corchaaz can Dismiss the raft, which detaches all combined corchaazes. If half or more of the raft members die, the interstellar raft ends.

Effect: Interstellar Raft

**Aquatic Ambush.** 40 feet

**Copi Concealment.** The corchaaz raises a gravitational barrier around its copi shell and gains Concealment against all creatures for 1 round.

**Graviton Grip.** The corchaaz attempts to lock a creature within 40 feet into place with gravitational forces. The target must attempt a DC 20 save.

**Critical Success** The target is unaffected.

**Success** The target takes a –5-foot status penalty to its Speeds until the end of its next turn.

**Failure** The target becomes Stunned 1.

**Critical Failure** The target is Paralyzed for 1 round.

**Rend.** Claw

entities.name: Corpse Fleet Infantry
entities.description:
The Corpse Fleet's rank and file infantry are trained to work as a unit.

The Corpse Fleet is an army made up of undead supremacists who refuse to bow to the will of the living. Founded by defectors from the Eoxian navy, the Corpse Fleet aims to shatter Pact Worlds unity and liberate Eox from the influence of the living and those bone sages who sided with them. Unyielding and utterly ruthless, the Corpse Fleet deals in death and destruction, feeding on the living and exploiting the dead.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, unconscious

Notes.Abilities:
**Coordinated Shuffle.** **Trigger** An adjacent ally moves away from the Corpse Fleet infantry

**Effect** The Corpse Fleet infantry Strides up to half their Speed. They must move in the same direction as the triggering ally.

**Void Healing.** 

**Fusillade.** The Corpse Fleet infantry's ranged Strikes deal an additional 1d4 precision damage when the Corpse Fleet infantry is within the first range increment of at least one other member of the Corpse Fleet wielding a ranged weapon.

entities.name: Corpse Fleet Officer
entities.description:
A Corpse Fleet officer is a bold combat leader who bolsters their undead allies and has trained to destroy the living.

The Corpse Fleet is an army made up of undead supremacists who refuse to bow to the will of the living. Founded by defectors from the Eoxian navy, the Corpse Fleet aims to shatter Pact Worlds unity and liberate Eox from the influence of the living and those bone sages who sided with them. Unyielding and utterly ruthless, the Corpse Fleet deals in death and destruction, feeding on the living and exploiting the dead.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, unconscious

Notes.Abilities:
**Bolstering Aura.** 20 feet. Undead that begin their turn in the aura (including the Corpse Fleet officer) gain 8 temporary Hit Points for 1 hour, then become temporarily immune to bolstering aura for 1 hour.

Effect: Bolstering Aura

**Reactive Strike.** 

**Void Healing.** 

**Decimate the Living.** The Corpse Fleet officer has trained to decimate the living. Their Strikes deal an additional 1d6 void damage.

**Lead Salvo.** The Corpse Fleet officer makes a ranged or melee Strike against a creature. Each undead within 100 feet of the officer can immediately use a reaction and expend ammunition from a ranged weapon they're wielding equal to its expend value to increase the damage of Lead Salvo by 1d4 void damage for each undead ally, to a maximum of an additional 4d4 void damage.

**Tireless Flurry.** The Corpse Fleet officer makes one ranged Strike and one melee Strike in any order. These attacks count toward their multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until after both attacks are made.

entities.name: Corpse Fleet Recruiter
entities.description:
Corpse Fleet recruiters are powerful necromancers capable of maintaining control of mindless undead, creating new undead, and turning their magic against the living.

The Corpse Fleet is an army made up of undead supremacists who refuse to bow to the will of the living. Founded by defectors from the Eoxian navy, the Corpse Fleet aims to shatter Pact Worlds unity and liberate Eox from the influence of the living and those bone sages who sided with them. Unyielding and utterly ruthless, the Corpse Fleet deals in death and destruction, feeding on the living and exploiting the dead.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, unconscious

Notes.Skills: Acrobatics +15, Arcana +17, Intimidation +14, Piloting +15, Religion +14, Society +17
Notes.Abilities:
**Seize Control.** 20 feet. Mindless undead that begin their turn in the area must attempt a DC 22 save; on a failure, the Corpse Fleet recruiter seizes control of that undead. It gains the minion trait.

**Void Healing.** 

**Corpse Bomb.** The Corpse Fleet recruiter detonates one mindless undead minion under their control, causing it to explode in a 15-foot-radius burst, dealing 4d6 slashing damage and 4d6 void damage to creatures in the area (DC 25 save).

**Efficient Commands.** The Corpse Fleet recruiter Sustains each spell they cast to create minions and Commands any number of their minions.

**Rapid Recruitment.** **Frequency** once per day

**Requirements** A formerly living creature that died within the last round is within 10 feet

**Effect** The Corpse Fleet recruiter immediately performs the Create Undead ritual, as if it were a spell with a casting time of 2 actions and the Corpse Fleet recruiter rolled a critical success on the ritual.
Notes.Spells: Bind Undead, Entropy Strike, Irradiate, Vampiric Feast, Create Undead (doesn't require secondary casters), Darkness, Resist Energy, Caustic Blast, Detect Magic, Electric Arc, Grim Tendrils, Harm, Read Aura, Summon Undead, Summon Undead, Void Warp

entities.name: Corzad
entities.description:
Packs of wolflike corzads act as the eyes and mouths of the corzadai fungal colony.

Corzadais spawned from the broken remains of Aucturn. Explosively launched into space, these fungal colonies are held together by mysterious forces. Their strange fruiting bodies have taken on numerous shapes, of which two have been more commonly seen in the Pact Worlds than others: corzads and corzadors.

Notes.Abilities:
**Fungal Symbiosis.** A corzad's Strikes deal an extra 1d4 damage to targets within 20 feet of at least two of the corzad's allies.

**Spore Tide.** The corzad dissolves into a mass of slimy spores and Strides twice, ignoring difficult terrain and other creatures. This movement doesn't trigger reactions. Any creature in the corzad's path must succeed at a DC 15 save or become Sickened 1. The corzad re-forms at the end of this movement.

entities.name: Corzador
entities.description:
Vaguely humanoid corzadors herd corzad packs as they carry out their grim tasks.

Corzadais spawned from the broken remains of Aucturn. Explosively launched into space, these fungal colonies are held together by mysterious forces. Their strange fruiting bodies have taken on numerous shapes, of which two have been more commonly seen in the Pact Worlds than others: corzads and corzadors.

Notes.Abilities:
**Follicle Germination.** Hundreds of wirelike nerve endings erupt from the corzador's head in a 30-foot emanation. Each non-corzadai in the area must succeed at a DC 18 save or be instantly observed by all corzadais within 100 feet. Corzadais in the area gain a +1 circumstance bonus to attack and damage rolls against the detected creatures as long as the targets remain in the emanation. The corzador's emanation remains in effect until it takes a move action to leave its current space.

Effect: Follicle Germination

**Shrieking Utricle.** **Trigger** A non-corzadai creature moves within the corzador's active Follicle Germination

**Effect** The corzador emits a high-pitched shriek. All non-corzadai creatures within the corzador's Follicle Emanation take 2d8 sonic |options:area-damage damage with a DC 18 save.

entities.name: Cosmic Dragon (Adult, Spellcaster)
entities.description: These majestic dragons embody the stellar forces that underly and balance all that exists in the universe. Cosmic dragons are wise, social, and patient beings, accepting of all whom they come across; they see all creatures as equal components of the universe and are just as likely to be found discussing astrophysics in the company of scholars as they are to be found lamenting the twists and turns of fate in the company of the downtrodden. Most cosmic dragons can change their shape, though they usually only do so to make other creatures comfortable. They detest deception and always introduce themselves as dragons even while in another form.

Notes.Abilities:
**+2 status to all saves vs. divine.** 

**Attunement Aura.** 60 feet. All allied creatures in the aura gain a +5-foot status bonus to Speeds (if the dragon is photon-attuned), or all enemies take a –5-foot status penalty to Speeds (if the dragon is graviton-attuned).

**Reactive Strike.** 

**Cosmic Attunement.** The cosmic dragon is always attuned to an underlying stellar force: either photons or gravitons. They can swap attunement as a free action once at the start of their turn in combat and is otherwise attuned to whichever force they choose at any time outside of combat. The dragon's melee Strikes deal an additional 2d6 fire damage while they're photon-attuned and an additional 1d6 bludgeoning damage plus Knockdown while they're graviton-attuned. The damage of their cosmic blast Strike is likewise determined by their current attunement, as are the effects of some of their other abilities. The dragon can choose to exclude any creatures from any effect of the aura or action that uses the aura.

The dragon can always sense the distance and direction to the nearest *Drift beacon* and to the *Starstone* on Absalom Station.

**Stellar Breath.** The dragon unleashes divine power like that from the core of a star or black hole, dealing 10d10 spirit |options:area-damage damage in a 40-foot cone (DC 34 save). The dragon can't use Stellar Breath for 1d4 rounds.

**Stellar Mote.** The dragon conjures a mote of stellar energy that shares their current attunement. They direct the mote to a square within 90 feet. While the mote is deployed, the dragon's attunement aura also emanates from that square, with the same emanation radius. The dragon can Sustain to move the mote up to 90 feet or to recall the mote from any distance. The mote is made of cosmic energy, doesn't occupy a space, and can't be targeted or destroyed by any effect.

**Stellar Pulse.** The dragon imposes an effect on creatures within their attunement aura. The effect is based on the dragon's current attunement. The dragon can't use Stellar Pulse again for 1d4 rounds.

- **Graviton** Each creature must succeed at a DC 34 save or be Immobilized for 1 round.
- **Photon** Each creature becomes Quickened and can use the extra action only to Stride or Strike.
Notes.Spells: Eclipse Burst, Sunburst, Repulsion, Truesight, X-Ray Vision, Banishment, Sending, Sending, Truespeech (constant), Planar Tether, Heroism, Life Seal (at will), Calm, Cleanse Affliction, Clear Mind, Environmental Endurance, Resist Energy, See the Unseen, Status, Translate, Detect Magic, Forbidding Ward, Guidance, Heal, Infuse Vitality, Reorient, Sanctuary, Spirit Link, Stabilize

entities.name: Crest-Eater Necrograft Zombie
entities.description:
Necrograft zombies are animated by necrografts created from the body parts and internal organs of undead creatures. On Eox, it's common to augment animals and beasts with necrografts to ensure their survival on the dead planet. After death, many of these creatures return as true undead to continue serving their creators.

Technological zombies are created when a dead creature is reanimated (or otherwise kept moving) by an internal or integrated technological item—usually an augmentation. Despite the vast differences in form and hardware between different tech zombies, they do have similarities—they're mindless undead driven to harm the living, with technological components and weaknesses that can be leveraged.

Stats.Immunities: death-effects, disease, mental, paralyzed, poison, unconscious

Notes.Abilities:
**Necrograft.** A necrograft zombie's necrografts can be disabled for 1 hour by a creature that succeeds at a DC 22 check. Attempting to do so can typically be done only while within reach of the zombie, and is a 2-action activity that has the manipulate trait. A necrograft zombie with disabled necrografts is Slowed 1 and can't use any reactions.

**Rapid Decomposition.** A necrograft zombie must use this reaction unless its necrograft is disabled

**Trigger** The zombie is reduced to 0 Hit Points

**Effect** The zombie rapidly decomposes into a heap of rotting biomass, dealing 2d8 poison ,2d8 void |options:area-damage damage in a 15-foot emanation (DC 22 save) and making that area hazardous terrain for 1 minute (1d4 void |options:area-damage damage). This ability destroys any organic items on the zombie (including necrografts).

**Stench.** 10 feet. DC 22

**Void Healing.** 

**Constrict.** 1d8+9 bludgeoning, DC 22

**Scree Strider.** The crest-eater necrograft zombie ignores difficult terrain caused by rubble, sand, and uneven ground made of earth and stone.

entities.name: Crest-Eater
entities.description:
Crest-eaters are large four-legged beasts with traits of both reptiles and mammals. Originating from the distant world of Kasath, they've spread throughout the cosmos, accompanying numerous kasathas and even having a small enclave aboard the Idari worldship in the Pact Worlds. A crest-eater is a predator known for consuming the bones of their prey. They use a highly corrosive acidic venom that eats through minerals with ease. Their name comes from their history of tracking down kasathas and cracking open their prey's elongated skulls to feed on the "bony crests" within. As crest-eaters consume bones and other substances, they produce large mineral protrusions across their bodies. Crest-eaters are social creatures and often form prides to hunt together or join with other nearby species if they're accepted—it's not uncommon to find a starship crew or local raider gang with one or more crest-eaters they've adopted. Tamers who have hunted with crest-eaters for generations craft a ceremonial cestus from their comrade's body after a crest-eater passes, a tradition still practiced to this day despite the high value and demand for crest-eater bones.

Most crest-eaters can grow as long as 14 feet and about 6 feet tall (not including their noticeable mineral protrusions). Thanks to their mineral-laden composition, they often weigh in excess of 1,000 pounds, somewhat hampering their mobility in environments that can't support their girth. Young and mature crest-eaters tend to stay together in small prides, though some act as solitary hunters in environments where food sources are scarce. Especially large males frequently become increasingly aggressive as they age, and they're often driven away by the rest of the pride for both their hostility and gluttonous appetites. If these solitary beasts survive long enough, they can become unpredictable and dangerous threats that attempt to establish territory and find food by attacking desert settlements. Many kasathan epics feature one or more brave warriors defending their village against an ancient male crest-eater. Whether dispatched by local legends or eventually dying off in secret, these oversized crest-eaters can leave behind a valuable cache of minerals for enterprising adventurers.

Notes.Abilities:
**Bone Tracker.** A crest-eater can use its scent as a precise sense at the listed range against creatures that have taken damage from crest-eater venom in the past hour.

**Reactive Strike.** 

**Crest-Eater Venom.** **Saving Throw** DC 21

**Max Duration** 4 rounds

**Stage 1** 1d6 acid damage and Enfeebled 1 (1 round)

**Stage 2** 1d8 acid damage and Enfeebled 2 (1 round)

**Stage 3** 1d10 acid damage, Drained 1, and enfeebled 2 (1 round)

**Scree Strider.** Crest-eaters ignore difficult terrain caused by rubble, sand, and uneven ground made of earth and stone.

entities.name: Cyanoscum Bloom
entities.description:
While these wood elementals bear the adorable appearance of a rodent, their main bodies are unfortunately composed of toxin-producing algae. Cyanoscums thrive in any warm, wet environment. Cyanoscum blooms are easy to spot; from a distance, they look like blue-green meadows floating atop still waters or clusters of fuzzy, teal moss clinging to plants and rocks. An explorer moved by this majestic sight might venture too close to the water's edge or reach out to touch the soft, resplendent moss—inviting contact with these beautiful but poisonous creatures.

Elementals are energetic intrusions from the primal planes of existence. They take many forms, from mindless eddies in the wind or water to complex entities capable of wielding primal magic. The advent of space travel and the progress of technology have allowed even more living embodiments of the elements to manifest in the Universe.

Natural events like wildfires, solar storms, and floods can unleash hordes of unruly elementals on a planet or into a region of space. Sometimes, a gathering of powerful elementals causes a natural disaster on an epic scale, like an off-the-charts solar flare that fries a planet's power grid or a ceaseless storm swirling in a gas giant's atmosphere.

Notes.Abilities:
**Water Sense.** A cyanoscum can sense the presence of water within 60 feet as an imprecise sense.

**Regeneration 5 (Deactivated by Fire).** 

**Toxic Exposure.** Creatures inside the cyanoscum bloom's space are exposed to cyanoscum toxin. A creature can't reduce the poison below stage 1 while it shares a space with the cyanoscum bloom.

**Cyanoscum Toxin.** **Saving Throw** DC 18

**Maximum Duration** 6 rounds

**Stage 1** 1d4 poison damage and Slowed 1 (1 round)

**Stage 2** 1d6 poison damage and Slowed 2 (1 round)

**Stage 3** 1d8 poison damage and Paralyzed (1 round)

**Frenzied Scratching.** Each enemy in the cyanoscum bloom's space takes 3d6 piercing |options:area-damage damage (DC 18 save).

**Squish.** A cyanoscum bloom can Squeeze through spaces that aren't airtight at half its Speed per round.

entities.description:

**Self-Destruct.** A cybernetic zombie must use this reaction unless its cybernetics are disabled

**Trigger** The cybernetic zombie is reduced to 0 Hit Points

**Effect** The zombie's damaged cybernetics explode, dealing 1d8 electricity |options:area-damage damage in a 10-foot emanation (DC 15 save). This ability destroys the zombie's integrated items and any tech items on the zombie of 1st level or lower.

**Void Healing.**

entities.name: Daipex
entities.description:
Daipexes are formed from souls of sinful mortals whose lives were consumed by rage and indiscriminate violence. Their hulking figures consist primarily of a pair of chain guns merged into the flesh of their large arms. By comparison, their legs are disproportionately small and incapable of bracing completely against the force of their attacks. Daipexes only use their legs when necessary and otherwise rely on their arms to move about to reduce the strain on their leg muscles.

Daipexes carry about the entrails of their prey, sometimes dangling loops of intestines from their necks or simply dragging it along the ground. They feed these organs into their arms and, by flexing their muscles there, condense the putrid flesh into ammunition that can then be fired directly from their bodies. While they often have enough ammunition to fire off their arm weapons for hours, in the rare instances that they run out of ammunition mid-combat, they either retrieve more from corpses on the battlefield or sacrifice their own flesh in the name of victory.

All mortal creatures have souls that are usually judged in the Boneyard after their demise. The souls of individuals who lived sinful lives—usually by hurting others or acting selfishly—are sent to the Outer Rifts, where they eventually coalesce into demons. These fiends care for nothing but the corruption of mortal life to ensure that the ranks of their fellow demons never wane.

Notes.Abilities:
**Arm Cannon.** A daipex's powerful arms can be fused into one or more cannons. These arm cannons also can't be Disarmed or Released. The daipex takes a –4 circumstance penalty to any action that requires fine motor control.

**Char Miasma.** 5 feet. The heat from a daipex's arm cannons burns the intestines fed into the grafted weapons as ammunition. A creature that enters or begins its turn in the aura must succeed at a DC 23 save or be Sickened 1.

**Misfire Vulnerability.** A daipex is full of unceasing rage and despises it when they can't deal damage. When a daipex critically fails a Strike or when a creature critically succeeds at its save against Hail of Bullets, the daipex takes 3d6 mental damage.

**Hail of Bullets.** The daipex fires a 30-foot cone of bullets, dealing 6d10 piercing |options:area-damage damage (DC 26 save) to creatures in the area. The daipex is pushed 10 feet in the opposite direction and can't use Hail of Bullets again for 1d4 rounds.

**Rain of Bullets.** **Frequency** once per round

**Effect** The daipex makes two arm cannon Strikes against a single target. The daipex's multiple attack penalty is applied normally. If both Strikes hit, combine their damage for the purpose of resistances and weaknesses.

**Recoil.** A daipex's relatively small legs can't withstand their arm cannon's kickback. When a daipex makes an arm cannon Strike, they're pushed 5 feet in the opposite direction of the Strike's target. The daipex can take a –2 circumstance penalty to the Strike to avoid this forced movement.
Notes.Spells: Demonic Pact

entities.name: Deh-Nolo
entities.description:
Deh-nolos are the Dominion's foremost engineers, seamlessly and deviously merging technology and biological systems to create any device imaginable, from sinister weapons to massive starships to shipmind oozes. These creations are grown, not built, but they're neither cybernetics nor biotech—rather, something in between. Deh-nolos seek to understand all technology they encounter, and they believe it's their right to consume the brain of anyone they think might help them better understand an unfamiliar device. Then again, deh-nolos have no qualms about consuming brains for nearly any reason, seeing all forms of life outside the Dominion as lesser beings.

While mostly organic, deh-nolos can concentrate their shimmering liquid metal secretions into foul crystals that they can use as projectiles or mechanical components for their twisted inventions. A casual onlooker might assume these creations are biotechnological in nature, as they often look like atrophied organs and mutated body parts held together by seemingly crude or incomplete circuitry. Those who attempt to incorporate deh-nolo technology into their bodies as augmentations typically experience terrible pain and grisly deaths, even if they somehow manage to isolate or drain the toxins naturally produced by a deh-nolo's alien flesh. Even less intrusive experiments with deh-nolo technology are unpredictable and dangerous, and the results of a "successful" outcome are disturbing at best.

Notes.Skills: Acrobatics +25, Arcana +28, Athletics +25, Computers +28, Medicine +25, Occultism +28, Stealth +25
Notes.Abilities:
**Thoughtsense.** The deh-nolo senses a creature's mental essence as a precise sense with the listed range; they can't sense mindless creatures with thoughtsense.

**+1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic.** 

**Brain Loss.** If a deh-nolo takes 60 damage from a critical hit or takes 50 mental damage, they must succeed at a DC 34 save (DC 34 for critical damage or DC 34 for mental damage) or one of their brain sacs is destroyed.

**Brain Sacs.** A deh-nolo snatcher has four brain sacs that they use to store harvested brains. A deh-nolo knows one additional language for each brain they have stored in a brain sac, chosen from the languages that the creature knew when its brain was harvested. A deh-nolo without all four sacs full is Stupefied with a value equal to the number of empty sacs.

**Open Pustules.** When the deh-nolo takes damage, pustules on their body burst, spraying foul poison. Each adjacent creature is exposed to *dominion bile*.

**Dominion Bile.** **Saving Throw** DC 34

**Maximum Duration** 6 rounds

**Stage 1** 4d6 poison damage and Enfeebled 1 (1 round)

**Stage 2** 4d6 poison damage, enfeebled 1, and Slowed 1 (1 round)

**Stage 3** 6d6 poison damage, Enfeebled 2, and Slowed 2 (1 round)

**Stage 4** death

**Harvest Brain.** The deh-nolo harvests the brain of a creature that's been dead for no more than 1 minute. They can then use an Interact action to secure the brain in one of their empty brain sacs.
Notes.Spells: Corrosive Haze, Promession, Overload Systems, Synaptic Pulse, Translocate (at will), Discharge (at will), Instant Virus (at will)

entities.name: Demolition-Class Assassin Robot
entities.description:
Named for their tendency toward extreme violence and aggressiveness, demolition robots nevertheless start their mission with stealth being a priority. Outwardly, these robots conceal their true nature with an outer casing resembling that of industrial, civic, or even domestic robots and drones.

Once the target has been detected, all stealth flies out the window as these killer machines unfurl their weapons and sensory suite from hidden panels and rush toward the mark at full speed. With their encyclopedic data banks on the stress points and emergency release mechanisms of most doors, only the most solid barriers can hold them at bay for long.

In some societies, machines automate many processes. It only makes sense, then, that some would attempt to automate the act of murder. Most manufacturers would never admit to creating such designs, forcing wealthy figures to go through hidden channels to acquire units from secret facilities or unscrupulous manufacturers. Regardless of their origins, these robots can be programmed with a target and set loose, the owner assured that either their target will be dead or will be unable to prove who tried to kill them thanks to the unit's fried circuitry.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, doomed, drained, fatigued, healing, mental, nonlethal-attacks, paralyzed, poison, sickened, spirit, unconscious, void, vitality

Notes.Abilities:
**Burn Protocol.** The circuitry of an assassin robot self-destructs upon the robot's destruction, making tracing its owner extremely difficult. Add 10 to the DC of a Computers check to recover data from a destroyed assassin robot.

**Breaching Rush.** The demolition-class assassin robot attempts to close the distance between it and its target, removing all obstacles in its way. The robot makes a ranged Strike with its breaching gun against the Force Open DC of a door or other obstacle. If successful, the obstacle gains the broken condition. The robot then Strides twice toward (and even through) the obstacle, but if the obstacle still bars the robot's movement, it stops adjacent to the obstacle and attempts an Athletics check to force-open the obstacle with a +4 circumstance bonus.

**Disguise Shell.** The demolition-class assassin robot enters or leaves its disguised form. While in its disguised form, it loses the ability to make Strikes or use its Breaching Rush ability, but it becomes indistinguishable from a noncombatant robot or drone model that it's based on; it gets an automatic result of 33 on Deception checks and DCs to pass as a robot of that model. Damage to the robot can prevent this disguise from being effective at the GM's discretion.

**Sneak Attack.** The demolition-class assassin robot's Strikes deal an additional 2d6 precision damage to Off-Guard creatures.

**Target Tracking.** The demolition-class assassin robot establishes a target lock on a creature it can see within 120 feet. The creature can't become Concealed against the robot or create-a-diversion against the robot. This ability lasts until the robot loses line of sight with the target or the target otherwise becomes Hidden.

entities.name: Deprimogon
entities.description:
Deprimogons stalk hidden tunnels, shadowed alleys, and looming towers of settlements whose governments have made infernal pacts as they silently monitor citizens for any signs of sedition. Agitators or freedom fighters are harassed or chased down and trapped by these devils before disappearing forever. Deprimogons hide their faces behind sleek metallic masks that suppress their own emotions, blocking out any pleas, threats, or bargaining that might dissuade them from their mission. Deprimogons delight in summoning diabolic creatures from eras long forgotten to torment their prisoners.

In the shadows of space stations, halls of courtrooms, and offices of corporations, devils tempt mortals with promises of power and lay the groundwork for their conquest. A devil's pacts can vary from elaborate contracts to quick promises, but they all end the same way: a mortal soul condemned, and Hell's forces bolstered. From the open rule of Malfane, the unseen control of Embroi, and hidden pacts with souls across the galaxy, devils continue their relentless work to spread tyranny and force the universe to resemble the hellish bureaucracy of their home.

Notes.Abilities:
**Masked Emotions.** The deprimogon loses their immunity to emotion and mental effects if they aren't wearing a mask. In addition, an unmasked silencer devil uses the outcome one degree of success worse than they roll on saving throws against mental effects. A deprimogon's mask can be Disarmed as if it were a held item.

**Evoke Paranoia.** The deprimogon infuses their weapons with paranoia and mistrust, instilling doubt in their victims with every attack. A creature damaged by a deprimogon's Strikes must attempt a DC 27 save.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected and temporarily immune to the deprimogon's evoke paranoia for 1 minute.

**Success** The creature is unaffected and temporarily immune to the deprimogon's evoke paranoia for 1 round.

**Failure** Until the beginning of the deprimogon's next turn, the creature believes everyone it sees is a potential threat. It becomes unfriendly to all creatures to which it wasn't already hostile, even those who were previously allies. It treats no one as an ally.

**Critical Failure** As failure, except the target believes that everyone it sees is a mortal enemy. It uses its reactions and free actions against everyone, regardless of whether they were previously its allies, as determined by the GM. It otherwise acts as rationally as it normally does and likely prefers to attack creatures that are actively attacking or hindering it over those leaving it alone.

**Infernal Disgrace.** The deprimogon's Strikes count as magical and unholy.

**Silent Prison.** The deprimogon casts a 6th-rank Wall of Force that dampens sound. Any creature that moves and begins its turn adjacent to the wall must attempt a DC 27 save. On a failure, the creature can't speak and can't use any actions and effects with the sonic or auditory traits while adjacent to the wall; this also prevents the creature from casting spells, with the exception of subtle spells.
Notes.Spells: Diabolic Pact (DC 27)

entities.name: Diaspora Worm Sage
entities.description:
Diaspora worms that survive for centuries grow significantly in size, power, and intelligence. They mostly protect their ancestral home, preserving bioelectric coral records and directing the actions of younger worms.

"Space worm" is a nonscientific term for a xenobiologically complex clade of invertebrate animals and beasts that make their home in the vastness of space. Some, like the diaspora and dust worms, show signs of intelligence and are directly related to each other. Others, like the surnoch, evolved separately, with their origins completely unknown to science.

Notes.Abilities:
**Electrocommunication.** Diaspora worms communicate by shaping and reading electromagnetic fields. This functions like telepathy with creatures that share this ability.

**Electromagnetic Sight.** Diaspora worms sense their surroundings by reading electromagnetic fields, including disruptions caused by creatures or objects. This is a precise sense within the listed range. Intense fields, such as areas emitting radiation or auras of electricity, make creatures within them Concealed to the diaspora worm.

**Electromagnetic Blindness.** Diaspora worms that take electricity damage must attempt a DC 23 save.

**Critical Success** The worm is unaffected.

**Success** The worm is Dazzled for 1 round.

**Failure** The worm is Blinded for 1 round.

**Critical Failure** The worm is blinded for 1 round, then dazzled for 1 round.

**Darkwater Veil.** **Requirements** The diaspora worm is in water

**Effect** The worm alters the structure of water within a 20-foot emanation, forming light-absorbing nanotubes. This field moves with the worm and lasts for 1 minute. The emanation deactivates non-magical light sources and automatically attempts to counteract magical light (counteract rank 9, counteract modifier +38). This field also provides cover for creatures inside of it from those outside, and vice versa.

**Darkwater Vortex.** The diaspora worm sage stirs up a 40-foot-tall cylinder of water with a 20-foot radius within 300 feet. If the area isn't already filled with water, this ability fails. The vortex buffets all creatures, dealing 5d10 bludgeoning |options:area-damage damage (DC 35 save). Creatures that fail the save are pulled 5 feet toward the center of the vortex (or 10 feet on a critical failure).

**Electromagnetic Surge.** The diaspora worm sage emits a concentrated wave of electromagnetism in a 50-foot cone. Each creature in the area must attempt a DC 35 save. A creature with the tech trait uses the outcome one degree of success worse than the result of its roll.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected and becomes immune to Electromagnetic Surge for 1 hour.

**Success** The creature's items with the tech trait become Glitching 1 for 1 round.

**Failure** The creature becomes Stunned 1, and its items with the tech trait become Glitching 2 for 1 minute. A creature with the tech trait also gains this glitching condition.

**Critical Failure** The creature becomes Paralyzed for 1 round, and its items with the tech trait become Glitching 3 for 10 minutes. A creature with the tech trait also gains this glitching condition.

**Swallow Whole.** Large, 6d10+6 bludgeoning, Rupture 32

**Tongue Grab.** A creature hit by the diaspora worm's tongue becomes Grabbed. A creature can sever the tongue with a Strike against AC 37 that deals at least 32 slashing damage. This prevents the worm from using its tongue Strike until it regrows its tongue, which takes 1 day.

**Tongue Reel.** **Requirements** The diaspora worm has Grabbed a creature with its tongue

**Effect** The diaspora worm attempts to reposition the grabbed creature toward the worm. If the grabbed creature is brought to within 10 feet or less of the worm, the worm can attempt to Swallow Whole the creature.

entities.name: Diaspora Worm
entities.description:
Resembling fanged eels with manes of tendrils instead of eyes, diaspora worms originally ruled the inky depths of the ocean that later became the icy planetoid Nisis. The worms' hostility toward trespassers and lack of observable speech lead most people to consider them mere beasts, but xenobiologists know the worms' tendrils respond to electromagnetic waves, which they manipulate to see, communicate, and interact with their surroundings. Bioelectric radiation from coral samples recovered from the worms' home reef documents millennia of worm culture and history from even before the Diaspora's formation.

Juvenile members of this species are sleek, sinuous, and nimble despite their size. Their electromagnetic manipulation lets them briefly change the molecular structure of water, making it murky like their original depths. Young worms tend to commit brazen attacks, requiring decades of experience to value more complex strategies.

"Space worm" is a nonscientific term for a xenobiologically complex clade of invertebrate animals and beasts that make their home in the vastness of space. Some, like the diaspora and dust worms, show signs of intelligence and are directly related to each other. Others, like the surnoch, evolved separately, with their origins completely unknown to science.

Notes.Abilities:
**Electrocommunication.** Diaspora worms communicate by shaping and reading electromagnetic fields. This functions like telepathy with creatures that share this ability.

**Electromagnetic Sight.** Diaspora worms sense their surroundings by reading electromagnetic fields, including disruptions caused by creatures or objects. This is a precise sense within the listed range. Intense fields, such as areas emitting radiation or auras of electricity, make creatures within them Concealed to the diaspora worm.

**Electromagnetic Blindness.** Diaspora worms that take electricity damage must attempt a DC 23 save.

**Critical Success** The worm is unaffected.

**Success** The worm is Dazzled for 1 round.

**Failure** The worm is Blinded for 1 round.

**Critical Failure** The worm is blinded for 1 round, then dazzled for 1 round.

**Darkwater Veil.** **Requirements** The diaspora worm is in water

**Effect** The worm alters the structure of water within a 10-foot emanation, forming light-absorbing nanotubes. This field moves with the worm and lasts for 1 minute. The emanation deactivates non-magical light sources and automatically attempts to counteract magical light (counteract rank 4, counteract modifier +17). This field also provides cover for creatures inside of it from those outside, and vice versa.

**Swallow Whole.** Medium, 1d10+8 bludgeoning, Rupture 12

**Tongue Grab.** A creature hit by the diaspora worm's tongue becomes Grabbed. A creature can sever the tongue with a Strike against AC 19 that deals at least 12 slashing damage. This prevents the worm from using its tongue Strike until it regrows its tongue, which takes 1 day.

**Tongue Reel.** **Requirements** The diaspora worm has Grabbed a creature with its tongue

**Effect** The diaspora worm attempts to reposition the grabbed creature toward the worm. If the grabbed creature is brought to within 10 feet or less of the worm, the worm can attempt to Swallow Whole the creature.

entities.name: Diatha
entities.description:
Often called "boom bugs" or "exploding slugs," diathas are invertebrates that store nutrients as hydrocarbon chains rather than fat deposits. Threatened diathas secrete hormones that prime their energy stores to combust, detonating themselves to drive off or kill predators. Even if several diathas sacrifice themselves this way, their hive rarely suffers thanks to their rapid reproductive cycle.

Diathas are hardy scavengers that can convert almost any carbon-based molecules into energy. Originally, diathas consumed biowaste in underground warrens, but their appetite for hydrocarbon-based fuels and industrial runoff drew them into contact with modernized civilizations, where they quickly adapted to urban environments. Though some entrepreneurs try to use these creatures as an organic means of converting plastic waste into petrol products, most see diathas as vermin that do far more harm than good when allowed to propagate.

Diathas can easily stow away in the nooks and crannies of starships, and interstellar travelers often don't notice them until it's too late. Because they can digest almost any carbon-containing matter, diathas that colonize new worlds can adapt to a wide range of biomes and persist as a threat to native species for generations. Efforts to eradicate invasive diathas carry substantial risks to the exterminators and the environment they're trying to protect, as the explosive vermin use literal scorched earth tactics to protect their hives. To make matters worse, diathas are hermaphroditic and can grow new hives from a single organism if they have sufficient food sources to multiply. As a result, the Pact Worlds and Veskarium maintain strict quarantine measures for vessels suspected of carrying diatha infestations.

As diathas age, their stored internal gases allow them to become buoyant. These "elder" diathas instinctively take prominent roles as scouts and guards for other diathas. To create an elder diatha, apply the aerial and elite adjustments to a diatha, or increase its level using the guidelines from GM Core.

Notes.Abilities:
**Detonate.** **Trigger** The diatha takes acid, electricity, fire, piercing, slashing, or sonic damage

**Requirements** The diatha has 5 or fewer Hit Points

**Effect** The diatha dies, its body combusting in a flash of flame. All creatures in a 5-foot take 1d6 fire |options:area-damage damage (DC 16 save).

**Hydrocarbon Slick.** If a diatha dies before it can detonate, its body rapidly decomposes into a slick of highly volatile hydrocarbons. Any effect that deals acid, electricity, or fire damage in an area that includes the square where the diatha died, or targets a creature in that square, causes a small explosion and consumes the slick.

All creatures in the square and in a 5-foot emanation take 1d6 fire |options:area-damage damage (DC 16 save). The slick evaporates after 10 minutes if it isn't ignited.

**Explosive Charge.** **Requirements** The diatha has 5 or fewer Hit Points

**Effect** The diatha Strides twice and makes a melee Strike at the end of that movement. After the Strike, the diatha uses Detonate.

entities.name: Digital Ghost Vidgamer
entities.description:
Some vidgamers are so terminally online that they can manifest as a digital ghost.

Digital ghosts are data constructs crafted from forgotten user accounts and metadata that are gathered and formatted into a simulacrum of the source user.

Notes.Abilities:
**Techsense (Imprecise) 30 feet.** A digital ghost senses creatures and items with the tech trait at the listed range.

**Backup.** An offline copy of the digital ghost is stored in a device. When an active digital ghost is destroyed, it reforms after 2d4 days within the device that the copy is stored in, fully healed, but with no memory of what destroyed them. A digital ghost can be permanently removed from that device by attempting a DC 24 check against the digital ghost's Will DC.

On a success, the copy of the digital ghost is purged from the device, and no new copies will be generated. On a critical success, any active copies are also purged.

**Device Bound.** A digital ghost can stray only a short distance from the device where they're stored. A typical limit is 120 feet.

**Malware Infection.** **Frequency** once per day

**Effect** The digital ghost attempts to infect an item with the tech trait being held or used by a creature within 30 feet. The bearer can attempt a DC 21 save.

**Critical Success** The item is unaffected, and the digital ghost can't use Malware Infection for 1 week.

**Success** The item is unaffected.

**Failure** The item becomes glitching 2.

**Critical Failure** The item becomes glitching 2, and an offline digital ghost based on the bearer is created on the device in 2d4 days.

**Virtual Arms.** A digital ghost's weapons deal mental damage, have the ghost killer upgrade, and disappear if dropped.

entities.name: Draiclipsed
entities.description:
Draiclipsed are the undead heralds of the Insatiable Eclipse, an ancient and terrifying tzitzimitl warlord buried when the Blackmoon fell on Eox and recently awakened by the Newborn. The Insatiable Eclipse amasses its forces, including legions of draiclipsed, to retake Eox, a world he feels has fallen to decadence and frivolity, whose disgraceful leaders have made the blasphemous decision to ally with the living.

Draiclipsed are canny skeletal undead whose pitch-black bones absorb light, allowing them to cast deep shadows. They can also consume magical light, using the absorbed photons to obscure their form before unleashing it in a blast of electromagnetic energy. Utterly loyal to their creator and liege, draiclipsed are trained for open warfare and even more dangerous when fighting alongside one another.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, cold, death-effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, unconscious

Notes.Abilities:
**Infrared Vision.** A draiclipsed can detect infrared radiation (such as that given off by warm-blooded creatures) as an imprecise sense at the listed range.

**Eclipse Shroud.** 15 feet. A draiclipsed absorbs light and is perpetually surrounded by shifting shadows and lengthening darkness. Light in the area decreases by one step (for example, bright light becomes dim light).

**Void Healing.** 

**Consume Light.** The draiclipsed opens their mouth and sucks in a magical light, consuming it to fuel their own powers. The draiclipsed attempts a counteract check against one magical light effect within 60 feet (+15 counteract modifier). If successful, the draiclipsed becomes ringed in diffuse light, becoming photonic for the next 24 hours. While a draiclipsed is photonic, they're Concealed.

**Cull the Betrayers.** Whenever a draiclipsed would deal void damage to an undead or other creature with void healing, that void damage becomes cold damage instead.

**Darkness Falls.** **Requirements** The draiclipsed is photonic

**Effect** The draiclipsed releases the light they've consumed in a blast of corrupted electromagnetic energy, dealing 3d8 electricity ,3d8 void |options:area-damage damage in a 30-foot cone (DC 24 save). The draiclipsed is no longer photonic.

**Gathering Darkness.** If at least one other draiclipsed is within the draiclipsed's eclipse shroud, the draiclipsed's Strikes deal an additional 1d8 void damage.

entities.name: Dread Empathnid
entities.description:
Dread empathnids are deadly hunters native to jungle planets. They thrive on populated worlds, and their preferred prey are intelligent humanoids. Drawn to negative emotions, dread empathnids absorb the terror of their dying victims and infuse their webbing with these horrific experiences.

Empathnids have tremendous empathy for other creatures. The fact that the 8-inch spidery creatures come in a variety of colors and have a lifesaving venom likely explains why they're frequently used as companions or pets across the Pact Worlds.

Notes.Abilities:
**Emotionsense.** This is a precise sense against creatures under an emotion effect or in the grips of overwhelming emotions (at the GM's discretion). Against other creatures, this is an imprecise sense. Creatures immune to emotion or mental effects or under the effects of a Calm spell are undetectable by emotionsense.

**Dread Venom.** **Saving Throw** DC 18

**Maximum Duration** 6 rounds

**Stage 1** 1d6 mental damage and Frightened 1 (1 round)

**Stage 2** 2d6 mental damage and Frightened 2 (1 round)

**Stage 3** As stage 2, plus Doomed 1 (1 round)

**Mental Mire.** A non-flying creature damaged by the dread empathnid's psychic web Strike or psychic burst is Immobilized, stuck to the ground or nearest adjacent surface until it Escapes. A flying creature must instead succeed at a DC 18 save or fall 20 feet (or 40 feet on a critical failure).

entities.name: Dreamer
entities.description:
Dancing between Liavara's peach-colored clouds are the Dreamers, the psychically gifted cousins of barathus. Not native to Liavara, the Dreamers were originally barathu explorers. They arrived by sailing one of the first living oma-ships long before the Gap. What exactly transformed them is still unknown to this day, though barathus as a people have been extremely protective of their prophetic cousins ever since.

The Dreamers lack barathus' ability to combine consciousnesses as well as their collectivist culture. That said, the Dreamers often dance through the skies of Liavara in flotillas together. To most of the Pact Worlds, they're a curiosity. To barathus, they're charges to be protected. The Dreamers themselves seem unconcerned with any such attention, giving neither care nor notice as to what's going on around them.

Notes.Abilities:
**Atavistic Rage.** **Trigger** The Dreamer is reduced to half or less than half their total Hit Points

**Effect** The injured Dreamer erupts into a terrifying state of psychic fury, requiring all non-Dreamers in a 30-foot emanation to attempt a DC 24 save. The Dreamer gains a +2 status bonus to attack and damage rolls for 1 minute but can't use their innate spells. After they stop raging, a Dreamer can't enter an Atavistic Rage again for 1 minute.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Success** The creature is Frightened 1.

**Failure** The creature is Frightened 2 and Stunned 1.

**Critical Failure** The creature becomes Frightened 3 and Fleeing for 1 round.

**Sluggish Mind.** Any creature that uses an emotion or mental effect on a Dreamer must succeed at a DC 24 save or become Slowed 1 for the next 1d4 rounds as fragments of prophetic songs fill its mind.

**Synesthetic Shock.** Any creature struck by a Dreamer's tentacle must attempt a DC 24 save to resist a wave of sensory overstimulation. The creature is then temporarily immune to all synesthetic shocks for 1 minute.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Success** The creature is Suppressed and Stupefied 1 until the end of its next turn.

**Failure** As success, but the creature is also Dazzled until the end of its next turn.

**Critical Failure** As failure, but with a duration of 2 rounds, and the creature is also Stunned 2.
Notes.Spells: Confusion, Eldritch Wrath, Mind Reading, Slow, Time's Edge, Void Whispers, Augury, Detect Thoughts, Sift the Sphere, Vibe Check, Akashic Download, Daze, Dream of Home, Eldritch Lance, Mind Skewer, Mindlink, Shield

entities.name: Dredgelit
entities.description:
Dredgelits linger as flickers on the silver screen or neon silhouettes glimpsed backstage. They seethe in shortwave static and stare out from fading gravure tableaux. Dredgelits are the undead specters of deceased media megastars who haunt the venues of their former glories and crave the attention of forgetful fans.

Most dredgelits live in a fantasy version of their former lives, but once their delusions are shattered, a burning desire to recapture their lost fame drives them. At this point, they become unpredictable, and even the smallest perceived slight can lead to a murderous fit of rage.

Dredgelits embody their former stage personas. These decaying debutantes ensnare admirers into their eternal fan clubs, blissfully unaware of the life-draining consequences they have upon new admirers. Dredgelit seek sacrificial fans, luring in the unwary and draining their vitality to stay famous and fabulous forever.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, precision, unconscious

Notes.Abilities:
