entities.name: Glass Serpent
entities.description:
The great glass serpents of the barren planet of Eox are one of the Pact Worlds' most notorious apex predators. With an average length of almost 60 feet and a weight of about 5,000 pounds, the size and grace of glass serpents are only part of what makes them such efficient killers. Thanks to an innate invisibility provided by their unique scales, glass serpents remain outside of the visual spectrum of most creatures, allowing them to silently approach unsuspecting prey. Having evolved through Eox's numerous cataclysms, these serpents find sustenance from the rare bands of living creatures who visit the world, and in an odd turn, while they're consuming the living is when glass serpents are at their most vulnerable. The combination of acids and digestive fluids used in consuming a living creature also deprives the serpents of their invisibility, and canny glass serpent hunters actively tempt their quarry with animals to consume before attacking in force.

Glass serpents have made their way well beyond the confines of Eox, and some have even found an accepting ecosystem in the Diaspora's strange waterway, the River Between. The local sarcesians blame Eox for intentionally polluting their waterways with predators, though Eox denies all accusations of intentional meddling. Such debates have only intensified since the Diaspora was granted provisional Pact World status under the sarcesians' stewardship.

Notes.Abilities:
**Ambush.** **Trigger** A creature passes within 20 feet of the glass serpent and hasn't detected it

**Effect** The glass serpent lunges out of hiding. It Strides directly toward the triggering creature and makes a jaws Strike against it. The target creature is Off-Guard to this attack.

**Ravenous Invisibility.** The glass serpent is naturally invisible. When a glass serpent takes a hostile action of any kind, it is hidden instead of undetected until the start of its next turn, as parts of its body become momentarily tangible. A glass serpent that has swallowed a creature becomes visible for the next day as its meal is being digested. If the swallowed creature escapes or is otherwise removed, the glass serpent immediately returns to being invisible.

**Concealing Coil.** **Requirements** The glass serpent's last action was a successful tail whip Strike

**Effect** The creature the glass serpent hit is Concealed from all creatures except the glass serpent until that creature moves out of the glass serpent's reach or until the start of the glass serpent's next turn.

**Swallow Whole.** Large, 2d8+6 bludgeoning, Rupture 12

entities.name: Gnackle
entities.description:
Many poor souls who encounter a gnackle don't realize until it's too late. These gremlins relish watching other creatures suffer humiliating failure and often spend weeks or longer selecting and grooming a victim into bringing out their own downfall. After reading their target's mind to learn what they want most, gnackles then magically disguise themselves, presenting to their target as a fairy godmother or similar granter of wishes and convincing their victims of some great destiny. They offer a magical "gift" and encourage the target toward acts of greater and greater ambition. However, once gnackles deem their victims in a suitably embarrassing or dangerous situation, they twist the gift into a terrible curse.

Gremlins have plagued the Universe with cruel tricks since long before the Gap, and they've fully adapted to a galaxy filled with technology. Whether meddling with a comm unit, a starship, or an entire space station, gremlins delight in ruination and chaos.

Notes.Abilities:
**False Confidence Aura.** 30 feet. Non-gremlin creatures that enter the aura must attempt a DC 18 save. On a failure, the creature gains a +1 status bonus to attack rolls and skill checks while in the aura, but if it misses an attack roll or fails a skill check while in the aura, it loses that bonus and instead takes a –2 status penalty to all attack rolls and skill checks for 1 minute. After 1 minute has elapsed, or if a creature succeeds at its save, the creature becomes temporarily immune to that gnackle's aura for 24 hours.

**Gremlin's Gift.** A gnackle can imbue a willing creature with a magical gift of talent for 24 hours, imparting a +2 status bonus to checks with a specific skill, chosen when this ability is used. The gnackle always knows when the creature attempts checks with the chosen skill and, at any time, can choose to invert the gift to instead immediately impart a –4 status penalty to all checks attempted with that skill for 1 minute, after which the creature is no longer affected by this ability.

Effect: Gremlin's Gift

Effect: Gremlin's Inverted Gift
Notes.Spells: Mind Reading, Cellular Stimulant, Daze, Glow Up, Illusory Disguise, Ricochet

entities.name: Gubbin
entities.description:
Gubbins—also known as data gremlins—are spontaneously born from corrupted data, especially as a result of errors in artificial intelligence programs. While gubbins aren't particularly powerful, they're notoriously hard to hit due to the way their bodies flicker and jolt through space as if slightly out of sync with the rest of the world. Gubbins are most easily set apart from other gremlins by their fingers, which vary in number from moment to moment and sprout from illogical locations on their hands, such as the backs or palms. While lacking in fine mobility, their warped hands are disturbing to observe in motion, a fact they delightfully use to their advantage.

Due to being weaponized in corporate espionage efforts and later multiplying out of control, gubbins are one of the most ubiquitous types of gremlin on heavily computerized planets. While not as malevolent as other gremlins, gubbins delight in irrevocably corrupting computer data, which they do for their own amusement as well as to create more gubbins. Gubbins are often found where large amounts of data are stored, accompanied by corrupted technological constructs such as hardlight life-forms or robots.

Gremlins have plagued the Universe with cruel tricks since long before the Gap, and they've fully adapted to a galaxy filled with technology. Whether meddling with a comm unit, a starship, or an entire space station, gremlins delight in ruination and chaos.

Notes.Abilities:
**Unsettling Appearance.** 20 feet. A non-gremlin creature that enters the aura must succeed at a DC 17 save or become Frightened 1 (or Frightened 2 on a critical failure) and is then temporarily immune to unsettling appearance for 1 minute. If the gubbin used any action with the manipulate trait, an Interact action, or a claw Strike since the start of their last turn, creatures take a –4 status penalty to their saves against this effect.

**Not Really There.** **Trigger** A creature targets the gubbin with an attack or area effect, and the gubbin is aware of the attacker

**Effect** The gubbin teleports 10 feet. If this puts the gubbin out of the range or area of the attack, the attack misses. If not, the gubbin gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC and Reflex saves against the attack.

**Scramble.** Gubbins can spread their glitchiness to others. Creatures damaged by the gubbin's claw or glitchy beam Strikes must succeed at a DC 17 save or become Sickened 1 (Sickened 2 on a critical hit). If the target has the tech trait, it becomes glitching instead of sickened.
Notes.Spells: Instant Virus, Delete (at will), Implant Data

entities.name: Gwereiad Queen
entities.description:
The rarest of nymphs, gwereiad queens form within supermassive black holes, either from a weaker gwereiad's ascension or created spontaneously amid the black hole's powerful energies. They tend to be even more detached than the typical gwereiad, speaking only in peculiar metaphors blending science and mysticism.

Nymphs are beautiful fey who appear as humanoids with elven features. They generally take female forms, but nymphs of all genders and presentations exist. While many nymphs live on planets and act as protectors of natural ponds, forests, caves, and cliffsides, other nymphs—often called space nymphs—are known for their association with celestial bodies. Like their planet-bound kin, space nymphs guard their bonded territories from exploitation or harm.

As admirers of the arts, nymphs are especially friendly toward creatives, and offering to depict a nymph in story, picture, or song is a sure way to win their favor—unless the nymph doesn't like the final result and lashes out at the artist for insulting them with a mediocre product. Vidcasting and livestreaming are popular pastimes among more sociable nymphs, whether to show off their remote environments or find audiences for performances. Some nymphs entice movie crews to film in their territories, with two provisos: first, that the production not damage the environment, and second, that the nymph receive a prominent role in the film.

Unless their territories are threatened, most space nymphs are friendly or indifferent to mortals, but they have long memories. Anyone visiting a space nymph's territory would be wise to research that nymph's grudges, past encounters with mortals, or any recent events in the area that might color the nymph's perspective of those traveling near their home.

A mortal who demonstrates the right attitude and abilities, such as by protecting a stellar body from destruction or creating an especially beautiful work of art, might draw a space nymph's attention. From time to time, space nymphs will offer their services as mentors to solarians or mystics, though they seldom seek pupils on their own. Space nymphs rarely enter into more than one such arrangement at a time and typically only make commitments that promise to last decades or centuries, so they're extremely selective in their choice of mentee.

Notes.Abilities:
**Sense Transponder.** While on their bonded celestial body, a nymph can sense approaching starships within a day's travel from the celestial body. This doesn't give them any information about the ship, its occupants, or its exact position. The nymph can send a message to the ship as if using a personal comm unit.

**Astronomical Ties.** A nymph queen is intrinsically tied to a specific celestial body, such as a supergiant star for a heliad queen.

As long as the queen is healthy, her territory thrives, and she can attempt to 1d20+32 #Counteract counteract spells and rituals that alter its physical properties with a counteract rank of 10.

If a nymph queen is injured or unhealthy, however, her celestial body also weakens: asteroids wobble out of orbit, stars dim, and the gravity of black holes diminishes. Restoring the nymph queen returns her celestial body to its equilibrium.

**Singularity Field.** 60 feet. The area around a gwereiad inexorably draws things toward its center. Creatures entering or starting their turns inside the aura must succeed at a DC 40 save or be pulled 5 feet toward the gwereiad (10 feet on a critical failure).

**Broadcast Allure.** The nymph queen magically superimposes her image on all technological items capable of displaying it, such as datapads or comm units, within planetary range. Alternatively, she can send this image to any comm address or addresses that she knows.

Each creature that can see the image must succeed at a DC 40 or have their attitude toward her improve by one step (two steps on a critical failure).

Affected creatures' attitudes revert to their previous level if the nymph queen uses a hostile action against them or their allies.

**Celestial Step.** A nymph queen can traverse her celestial body near-instantaneously. A nymph queen can use Celestial Step to teleport to any area on or within her territory, vanishing into its surface and reemerging at her intended destination.

**Change Shape.** Nymph queens can transform between their original form, which looks much like a typical nymph of their kind, and any Small or Medium humanoid form, typically choosing a version of their natural form with the appearance of the chosen species.

**Fan Mail.** A nymph queen can inspire a single intelligent creature by sending them a motivational video or text message. As long as the creature keeps the message saved and remains in good standing with the nymph queen, they gain a +1 status bonus to all Crafting, Performance, and Lore checks related to art or performance.

As a 1-action Interact action, the creature can play or view the message to bolster their spirits. Doing so allows the creature to attempt a 1d20+26 #Counteract counteract check against a single emotion effect affecting them.

When the nymph queen's message is used in this way, it becomes a mundane video or text afterward.

**Gravitic Crush.** The gwereiad summons a gravitational collapse around a creature within 30 feet, dealing 5d12 bludgeoning damage. The affected creature must attempt a DC 40 save.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Success** The creature's body crumples under the gravity, and it takes half damage.

**Failure** The creature takes full damage and is Immobilized by the gravitational collapse. It takes 2d6 persistent,bludgeoning damage until it Escapes.

**Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature takes double damage and the persistent damage is 4d6.
Notes.Spells: Event Horizon, Call Cosmos, Implosion, Telekinetic Tantrum, Gravity Field, Singularity Seed, Eclipse Burst, Execute, Void Scour, Mislead, Pocket Vacuum, Promession, Wave of Warning, Cairn Form, Clairvoyance, Electrotether, Haste, Personal Gravity (Constant), Time's Edge, Darkness, Charm, Command, Detect Magic, Fear, Glow Up, Guidance, Prestidigitation, Scan Environment, Seek the Stars, Stumble

entities.name: Gwereiad
entities.description:
Gwereiads are aloof and enigmatic nymphs who keep to themselves, nestling deep inside the phenomena known as black holes. Whether their solitary nature is an active preference or simply a consequence of their homes is up for debate, as few creatures can brave the gravitational forces of a black hole long enough to make contact with gwereiads. They're rarely hostile unless provoked and occasionally even rescue starships at risk of being devoured by their homes.

Gwereiads adore art and music, though their tastes tend toward the strange and avant-garde. While most nymphs aren't overtly religious, gwereiads devote themselves to esoteric spirituality focused on space-time.

This doesn't give them any information about the ship, its occupants, or its exact position. The nymph can send a message to the ship as if using a personal comm unit.

**Constant Spells.** 

**Black Hole-Dependent.** A gwereiad is mystically bonded to a single black hole. If they're away from their bonded black hole for more than 24 hours, they become Drained 1 and must succeed at a DC 29 save each additional 24 hours or increase their drained value by 1. A gwereiad can perform a 24-hour ritual to bond themself to a new black hole.

**Singularity Field.** 30 feet. The area around a gwereiad inexorably draws things toward its center. Creatures entering or starting their turns inside the aura must succeed at a DC 29 save or be pulled 5 feet toward the gwereiad (10 feet on a critical failure).

**Gravitic Crush.** The gwereiad summons a gravitational collapse around a creature within 30 feet, dealing 6d6 bludgeoning damage. The affected creature must attempt a DC 29 save.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Success** The creature's body crumples under the gravity, and it takes half damage.

**Failure** The creature takes full damage and is Immobilized by the gravitational collapse. It takes 2d6 persistent,bludgeoning damage until it Escapes.

**Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature takes double damage and the persistent damage is 4d6.
Notes.Spells: Gravity Field, Electrotether, Personal Gravity (Constant), Fear, Glow Up, Stumble

entities.name: Haeshi-Shaa (Haeshi Form)
entities.description:
A haeshi-shaa in their haeshi form is aggressive and persistent, unlikely to back down from an argument or a fight unless their life is in danger. While aggressive, haeshis are far from foolish; they prepare carefully for any encounter and often have dozens of nested contingencies to fall back on should any situation evolve beyond their control.

Haeshi-shaas are relatively new members of the Dominion of the Black. These long-lived creatures shift unpredictably between a liquid and a gaseous form in a mysterious cycle that lasts their entire lives. In their liquid haeshi form, they're a churning, chunky fluid, while in their vaporous shaa form, they're more akin to hazy brown fog. Regardless of their form, they hum with atonal harmonies that cause great discomfort in others.

Haeshi-shaas serve as a sort of priest caste for the Dominion of the Black, each form preaching a doctrine of entropy and annihilation, though with slightly different nuances between each form. Haeshis tend toward assertive, aggressive practices, while shaas are meditative, often spending many months or years in contemplation. Haeshi-shaas believe that the most perfect and divine state of any object or being is complete separation into its most basic, individual particles. They claim (dubiously) that they can see, even predict, the journey of all things as they travel toward this ultimate entropic end.

In truth, haeshi-shaas can't even predict when they'll shift into their alternate form. Some have tried to catalyze the change by seeking out specific types of life experience or knowledge, but despite the many claims to the contrary, there are no verified instances of a haeshi-shaa forcing the change. Most choose to simply await their next transformation, during which time they have many centuries to spread the Dominion's disturbing doctrines and pursue their inscrutable agendas.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, critical-hits, disease, paralyze, precision, unconscious, visual

Notes.Abilities:
**+1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic.** 

**Fast Healing 5.** 

**Frenetic Death.** When killed, a haeshi explodes in a wave of psychic energy, dealing 13d6 mental |options:area-damage damage to all creatures in a 20-foot burst (DC 29 save).

**No Breath.** 

**Stench.** 30 feet. DC 29

**Compression.** A haeshi can move through a gap at least 2 feet wide without Squeezing and can Squeeze through a gap at least 1 foot wide.

**Viral Vapor.** **Saving Throw** DC 32

**Stage 1** carrier (1 day)

**Stage 2** the creature becomes partially vaporous and treats all other creatures as Concealed (1 day)

**Stage 3** the creature is incorporeal and Unconscious (1 day)

**Stage 4** the creature dies, and its body dissipates into fine particles
Notes.Spells: Fear, Force Barrage (at will), Mind Skewer

entities.name: Haeshi-Shaa (Shaa Form)
entities.description:
While demonstrably more powerful while in shaa form, haeshi-shaas tend to spend this portion of their lives in careful contemplation. A shaa interrupted in their contemplation is a vengeful enemy indeed.

Haeshi-shaas are relatively new members of the Dominion of the Black. These long-lived creatures shift unpredictably between a liquid and a gaseous form in a mysterious cycle that lasts their entire lives. In their liquid haeshi form, they're a churning, chunky fluid, while in their vaporous shaa form, they're more akin to hazy brown fog. Regardless of their form, they hum with atonal harmonies that cause great discomfort in others.

Haeshi-shaas serve as a sort of priest caste for the Dominion of the Black, each form preaching a doctrine of entropy and annihilation, though with slightly different nuances between each form. Haeshis tend toward assertive, aggressive practices, while shaas are meditative, often spending many months or years in contemplation. Haeshi-shaas believe that the most perfect and divine state of any object or being is complete separation into its most basic, individual particles. They claim (dubiously) that they can see, even predict, the journey of all things as they travel toward this ultimate entropic end.

In truth, haeshi-shaas can't even predict when they'll shift into their alternate form. Some have tried to catalyze the change by seeking out specific types of life experience or knowledge, but despite the many claims to the contrary, there are no verified instances of a haeshi-shaa forcing the change. Most choose to simply await their next transformation, during which time they have many centuries to spread the Dominion's disturbing doctrines and pursue their inscrutable agendas.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, critical-hits, disease, poison, precision, unconscious, visual, paralyzed

Notes.Abilities:
**+1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic.** 

**Fast Healing 10.** 

**No Breath.** 

**Stench.** 30 feet. DC 34

**Expand.** The shaa spreads their matter thin, becoming Gargantuan and gaining a space and reach of 20 feet. The shaa can take only purely mental actions or use Thicken while in this state. A shaa can return to their normal size by spending a single action, which has the concentrate trait.

**Thicken.** The shaa agitates their molecules and becomes semitransparent and virtually impenetrable for 1 minute. In this form, the shaa isn't incorporeal, gains resistance 25 to all damage, and gains 150 temporary Hit Points for 1 minute. They can take no actions and are immovable. The shaa reverts to their natural form at the end of the duration.

**Viral Vapor.** **Saving Throw** DC 37

**Stage 1** carrier (1 day)

**Stage 2** the creature becomes partially vaporous and treats all other creatures as Concealed (1 day)

**Stage 3** the creature is incorporeal and Unconscious (1 day)

**Stage 4** the creature dies, and its body dissipates into fine particles
Notes.Spells: Phantasmal Fleet, Truesight, Mind Probe (at will), Synaptic Pulse, Cleanse Affliction, Fear (at will), Heal

entities.name: Hardlight Havoc
entities.description:
This hardlight life-form is unstable, displaying stuck frames and erratic movements.

Unlike normal holograms, hardlight life-forms are tangible, living entities.

Notes.Abilities:
**Error State.** Before the hardlight havoc begins its turn in combat, it gains one of the following error states at random, losing any previous error state.

**Change Character** The hardlight havoc regains 2d8 healing |options:area-damage Hit Points.

**Pixelation** The hardlight havoc is Concealed from all creatures.

**Power Leak** The hardlight havoc is Stunned 1. At the end of its turn, it deals 4d6 electricity |options:area-damage damage to creatures in a 10-foot emanation (DC 22 save).

**Surge** The hardlight havoc is Quickened until the end of its turn and can use the extra action to Stride or Strike.

**Tethered 120 feet.** A hardlight life-form can't travel more than the indicated number of feet from its projector. A hardlight life-form reduced to 0 HP vanishes, though its projector reconstructs it in 1d4 hours. The only way to permanently destroy a hardlight life-form is to find its projector and either repair or destroy it.

**Flicker.** The hardlight havoc teleports up to 40 feet. If the destination is within melee reach of an enemy, it can make a melee Strike against that enemy. If it teleports to a square without a surface to stand on, it falls after attempting a Strike and takes no damage from falling.

**Tethered 90 feet.** A hardlight life-form can't travel more than the indicated number of feet from its projector. A hardlight life-form reduced to 0 HP vanishes, though its projector reconstructs it in 1d4 hours. The only way to permanently destroy a hardlight life-form is to find its projector and either repair or destroy it.

**Arcade Leap.** The hardlight mascot can make a special Leap up to 15 feet vertically and up to 20 feet horizontally without a check.

**Stomp.** The hardlight mascot Leaps adjacent to a Medium or smaller creature, then makes a kick Strike against it. On a successful attack, it deals kick damage plus an additional 1d8 force damage. On a critical hit, the target is also knocked Prone.

**Taunt.** The hardlight mascot sings a jingle to a creature within 60 feet, dealing 4d6 mental damage (DC 19 save).

entities.name: Hardlight Scamp
entities.description:
These creatures typically resemble the ad or media they were born from, though they often also resemble bat-like elemental scamps, thus earning their name.

Unlike normal holograms, hardlight life-forms are tangible, living entities.

Notes.Abilities:
**Tethered 100 feet.** A hardlight life-form can't travel more than the indicated number of feet from its projector. A hardlight life-form reduced to 0 HP vanishes, though its projector reconstructs it in 1d4 hours. The only way to permanently destroy a hardlight life-form is to find its projector and either repair or destroy it.

**Freeze.** The hardlight scamp holds perfectly still so it appears as a normal hologram and becomes hidden. A hardlight scamp can Freeze even while being observed and counts as being Concealed.

**Holospark.** The hardlight scamp shoots sparks at a creature within 60 feet. The target must succeed at a DC 17 save or be Dazzled for 1 round (1 minute on a critical failure).
Notes.Spells: Blur, Figment, Ricochet

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, doomed, drained, fatigued, healing, nonlethal-attacks, paralyzed, poison, sickened, spirit, unconscious, vitality, void

Notes.Abilities:
**Tethered 200 feet.** A hardlight life-form can't travel more than the indicated number of feet from its projector. A hardlight life-form reduced to 0 HP vanishes, though its projector reconstructs it in 1d4 hours. The only way to permanently destroy a hardlight life-form is to find its projector and either repair or destroy it.

**Digital Reality.** 60 feet. Within the aura, everything looks digitalized. Visible creatures in the aura can't be Concealed, and invisible creatures are concealed rather than undetected.

**Constrict.** 2d8+6 bludgeoning, DC 26

**Virtual Roadblocks.** The hardlight weaver creates a stationary medium (1), large (2), or huge (3) hardlight obstacle, the center of which must be within its digital reality aura. These obstacles are difficult and hazardous terrain for non-hardlight life-forms, dealing 9 force damage. The Virtual Roadblocks remain until the hardlight weaver uses this ability again or until its aura moves out of range, whichever comes first.

entities.name: Heliad Queen
entities.description:
Heliad queens live on the largest dwarf stars, mature stars, and supergiants. They take great pride in the luminosity of their stars, often bedecking themselves in clothing specially designed to refract light to show off their home's brilliance.

Nymphs are beautiful fey who appear as humanoids with elven features. They generally take female forms, but nymphs of all genders and presentations exist. While many nymphs live on planets and act as protectors of natural ponds, forests, caves, and cliffsides, other nymphs—often called space nymphs—are known for their association with celestial bodies. Like their planet-bound kin, space nymphs guard their bonded territories from exploitation or harm.

As admirers of the arts, nymphs are especially friendly toward creatives, and offering to depict a nymph in story, picture, or song is a sure way to win their favor—unless the nymph doesn't like the final result and lashes out at the artist for insulting them with a mediocre product. Vidcasting and livestreaming are popular pastimes among more sociable nymphs, whether to show off their remote environments or find audiences for performances. Some nymphs entice movie crews to film in their territories, with two provisos: first, that the production not damage the environment, and second, that the nymph receive a prominent role in the film.

Unless their territories are threatened, most space nymphs are friendly or indifferent to mortals, but they have long memories. Anyone visiting a space nymph's territory would be wise to research that nymph's grudges, past encounters with mortals, or any recent events in the area that might color the nymph's perspective of those traveling near their home.

A mortal who demonstrates the right attitude and abilities, such as by protecting a stellar body from destruction or creating an especially beautiful work of art, might draw a space nymph's attention. From time to time, space nymphs will offer their services as mentors to solarians or mystics, though they seldom seek pupils on their own. Space nymphs rarely enter into more than one such arrangement at a time and typically only make commitments that promise to last decades or centuries, so they're extremely selective in their choice of mentee.

Notes.Skills: Acrobatics +27, Deception +28, Diplomacy +28, Intimidation +26, Nature +24, Performance +31
Notes.Abilities:
**Sense Transponder.** While on their bonded celestial body, a nymph can sense approaching starships within a day's travel from the celestial body. This doesn't give them any information about the ship, its occupants, or its exact position. The nymph can send a message to the ship as if using a personal comm unit.

**Astronomical Ties.** A nymph queen is intrinsically tied to a specific celestial body, such as a supergiant star for a heliad queen.

As long as the queen is healthy, her territory thrives, and she can attempt to 1d20+26 #Counteract counteract spells and rituals that alter its physical properties with a counteract rank of 7.

If a nymph queen is injured or unhealthy, however, her celestial body also weakens: asteroids wobble out of orbit, stars dim, and the gravity of black holes diminishes. Restoring the nymph queen returns her celestial body to its equilibrium.

**Radiant Gaze.** 60 feet. A heliad's eyes blaze like a sun. When a creature enters or starts its turn in the aura, it must attempt a DC 34 save. The heliad can deactivate or activate this aura by using a single action, which has the concentrate trait.

**Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Failure** The creature is Dazzled until the start of its next turn.

**Critical Failure** The creature is Blinded until the start of its next turn.

**Supernova.** **Trigger** The heliad queen dies

**Effect** The heliad's body explodes into brilliant, luminous flame. Each creature in a 10-foot emanation takes 12d8 fire |options:area-damage damage (DC 34 save). Creatures that critically fail are Blinded for 1 minute.

**Broadcast Allure.** The nymph queen magically superimposes her image on all technological items capable of displaying it, such as datapads or comm units, within planetary range. Alternatively, she can send this image to any comm address or addresses that she knows.

Each creature that can see the image must succeed at a DC 34 or have their attitude toward her improve by one step (two steps on a critical failure).

Affected creatures' attitudes revert to their previous level if the nymph queen uses a hostile action against them or their allies.

**Celestial Step.** A nymph queen can traverse her celestial body near-instantaneously. A nymph queen can use Celestial Step to teleport to any area on or within her territory, vanishing into its surface and reemerging at her intended destination.

**Change Shape.** Nymph queens can transform between their original form, which looks much like a typical nymph of their kind, and any Small or Medium humanoid form, typically choosing a version of their natural form with the appearance of the chosen species.

**Fan Mail.** A nymph queen can inspire a single intelligent creature by sending them a motivational video or text message. As long as the creature keeps the message saved and remains in good standing with the nymph queen, they gain a +1 status bonus to all Crafting, Performance, and Lore checks related to art or performance.

As a 1-action Interact action, the creature can play or view the message to bolster their spirits. Doing so allows the creature to attempt a 1d20+26 #Counteract counteract check against a single emotion effect affecting them.

When the nymph queen's message is used in this way, it becomes a mundane video or text afterward.
Notes.Spells: Energy Aegis, Sunburst, Field of Life, Wall of Plasma, Elemental Form, Creation, Fire Shield, Wall of Fire, Wall of Fire, Electrotether, Enthrall, Fireball, Fireball, Irradiate, Blazing Bolt, Everlight, Soul Surge, Breathe Fire, Charm, Glow Up, Guidance, Ignition, Light, Light, Overheat, Prestidigitation

entities.name: Heliad
entities.description:

Heliads reside among still-coalescing protostars or smaller dwarf stars. Many heliads take a keen interest in their star's entire system, eagerly following news, gossip, and activities of its planets' residents, if any, or travelers passing through. They view the arrival of visitors with excitement and frequently broadcast messages offering hospitality to those who venture near their stars. To host such visitors, heliads often build lodgings within special protective bubbles for creatures who couldn't otherwise survive the environment.

Notes.Skills: Acrobatics +14, Deception +15, Diplomacy +15, Intimidation +13, Nature +13, Performance +17
Notes.Abilities:

This doesn't give them any information about the ship, its occupants, or its exact position. The nymph can send a message to the ship as if using a personal comm unit.

**Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Failure** The creature is Dazzled until the start of its next turn.

**Critical Failure** The creature is Blinded until the start of its next turn.

**Solar-Dependent.** A heliad is mystically bonded to a single protostar or small dwarf star. If they're away from their bonded star for more than 24 hours, they become Drained 1 and must succeed at a DC 24 save each additional 24 hours or increase their drained value by 1. A heliad can perform a 24-hour ritual to bond themself to a new star.

**Supernova.** **Trigger** The heliad dies

**Effect** The heliad's body explodes into brilliant, luminous flame. Each creature in a 10-foot emanation takes 6d8 fire |options:area-damage damage (DC 24 save). Creatures that critically fail are Blinded for 1 minute.
Notes.Spells: Wall of Plasma, Fire Shield, Fireball, Blazing Bolt, Charm, Glow Up, Light, Overheat

entities.name: Hellknight Armiger
entities.description:
Hellknight armigers are the lowest-ranked Hellknights, though attaining this rank requires them to spend six years as an initiate and then pass the Hellknight Test, during which they must summon, combat, and defeat a fiend of Hell.

Hellknights are infernal knights, and while they once ruled entire nations on Lost Golarion, the Hellknights of the Pact Worlds enforce law and order more holistically, traveling in massive citadel starships to spread their influence rather than remaining in any one place. In battle, Hellknights are orderly, unrelenting, and deadly.

Notes.Abilities:
**Forged in Hellfire.** **Trigger** The armiger takes fire damage

**Effect** The armiger absorbs a fraction of the fire to empower their attacks. Until the end of their next turn, their Strikes deal an additional 1d6 fire damage.

**Four-Armed.** You have four arms, which allows you to wield and hold up to four hands' worth of weapons and equipment. At any time, one pair of hands is designated as your active hands. You can change this designation from one pair of hands to another by taking the Switch Hands action, which is a single action. You can wield items only with your active hands.

**Rapid Bombardment.** The armiger draws two grenades, then Area Fires both grenades. Creatures in the area of both grenades take a –1 circumstance penalty to their saving throws against both grenades.

entities.name: Hellknight Degradant
entities.description:
Hellknights most often study the forces of Hell to inspire their fighting styles and magic, but they might also learn to attune to the forces of the cosmos to become solarians.

Hellknights are infernal knights, and while they once ruled entire nations on Lost Golarion, the Hellknights of the Pact Worlds enforce law and order more holistically, traveling in massive citadel starships to spread their influence rather than remaining in any one place. In battle, Hellknights are orderly, unrelenting, and deadly.

Notes.Skills: Acrobatics +14, Athletics +17, Intimidation +14, Nature +14, Piloting +14, Stealth +14
Notes.Abilities:
**Reactive Strike.** 

**Black Hole.** The degradant deals 9d6 bludgeoning damage to each enemy creature within 30 feet with a DC 26 save. The degradant can't use Black Hole again for 1d4 rounds.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Success** The creature takes half damage and is pulled 5 feet toward the degradant.

**Failure** The creature takes full damage and is pulled 10 feet toward the degradant.

**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage, is pulled 30 feet toward the degradant, and is knocked Prone.

**Crush.** The degradant uses gravity to crush an enemy within 100 feet, dealing 4d6 bludgeoning damage (DC 26 save); on a critical failure, the creature takes an additional 1d6 persistent,bleed damage.

**Graviton Glaive.** A degradant wields a solar glaive formed of solidified gravitons. They can conjure and dismiss this weapon as a single action that has the concentrate trait. Whenever they successfully Strike a creature using their graviton glaive, the creature treats all squares adjacent to the square in which it was struck as difficult terrain until the end of the creature's next turn.

**Stellar Rush.** The degradant Strides twice, gaining a +10-foot circumstance bonus to their Speed during these moves. When they complete these Strides, all enemies within 15 feet of the degradant are pulled 15 feet closer to the degradant unless they succeed at a DC 26 save.

entities.name: Hellknight Signifer
entities.description:
A Hellknight who displays prowess, scholarly discipline, and magical acumen might attain the rank of signifer.

Hellknights are infernal knights, and while they once ruled entire nations on Lost Golarion, the Hellknights of the Pact Worlds enforce law and order more holistically, traveling in massive citadel starships to spread their influence rather than remaining in any one place. In battle, Hellknights are orderly, unrelenting, and deadly.

Notes.Abilities:
**Burn the Unworthy.** 10 feet. Magical wards cause a signifer's surrounding foes to catch flame. An enemy creature that starts its turn in the area must succeed at a DC 19 save or take 1d4 persistent,fire damage. A signifer can activate and deactivate this aura as a single action that has the concentrate trait. Regardless of the result of the save, the creature is immune to the aura for 1 minute.

**Proclamation of Guilt.** **Frequency** once per round

**Effect** The signifer accuses a target within 60 feet of misdeeds, then attempts an Intimidation check to demoralize them. As long as the target is frightened due to Proclamation of Guilt, it's also Suppressed.

**Reach Spell.** If the next action the signifer uses is to Cast a Spell that has a range, increase that spell's range by 30 feet.
Notes.Spells: Holy Light, Share Pain, Dispel Magic, Noise Blast, Resist Energy, Bless, Detect Magic, Diabolic Pact (DC 22, Doesn't Require Secondary Casters), Enfeeble, Harm, Heal, Heal, Ignition, Light, Ricochet, Shield, Wisp Ally

entities.name: Hesper
entities.description: These nuclear fey make their homes in reactors and embody the rapidly changing nature of their radioactive homes. They shift colors to reflect their moods, which can sometimes be used to predict their dangerous bouts of boredom. Hespers never intend malice, but they rarely consider the consequences of their actions.

Notes.Abilities:
**Radiation Sense.** A hesper can sense radiation sources, such as reactors and power cores, as an imprecise sense at the listed range.

**Energy Ray.** A hesper can change the damage type of its energy ray as a free action.

**Merge.** **Requirements** The hesper has spent at least 1 hour in contact with a reactor or other large power source

**Effect** The hesper Strides into the reactor, passing through its exterior and gaining fast healing 5 while inside. The hesper is aware of but can't physically interact with their surroundings and is protected from those outside. If the reactor is broken, the hesper takes 2d10 force damage and is immediately expelled from it. If the reactor is destroyed while the hesper is inside, the hesper must succeed at a DC 15 save or be slain instantly.

**Mutating Touch.** A hesper can deliver an enormous, mutating dose of radiation with a touch. Creatures struck by a hesper's fist Strike must attempt a DC 18 save. On a failure, the creature gains a random mutation from the table below for 1 hour (or 24 hours on a critical failure).

1d8Mutation

1**Extra eyes:** Target is dazzled in bright light and gains a +2 status bonus to sight-based Perception checks.

2**Bioelectric cells:** Tech items held by the target regain all spent charges at the end of the creature's turn. Tech items are glitching 1 for as long as the target holds them. If the target is a creature with the tech trait, it becomes glitching 1, and its melee Strikes deal an additional 1d6 electricity damage.

3**Spikes:** Target gains an unarmed melee attack that deals 1d4 piercing damage. It takes a –2 status penalty to attack rolls with two-handed weapons.

4**Glowing Tumors:** Target sheds light as a flashlight and takes a –2 status penalty to Stealth checks.

5**Gills:** Target gains the amphibious trait and takes a –1 status penalty to Fortitude saves.

6**Musk gland:** Target gains a 30-foot stench aura with a DC equal to their class DC.

7**Protective growths:** Target gains a +1 status bonus to AC and takes a –2 status penalty to Dexterity-based checks.

8**Cellular alteration:** The target is Sickened for the duration and gains Fast Healing with a value equal to half its level (rounded up).
Notes.Spells: Cellular Stimulant, Charm, Light, Mending, Prestidigitation, Thunderstrike

entities.name: Host Dragon (Adult, Spellcaster)
entities.description: Innumerable insects follow these lumbering, ravenous dragons wherever they roam, swarming around them and living in the countless orifices along the host dragon's body. The dragon is both a part of the swarm itself and a part of the swarm's ecosystem—the swarm feeds on their body, and the dragon feeds on the swarm in a grotesque, centuries-long cycle that somehow results in the host dragon growing larger and more powerful even if they feed on no other substance in their lifetime. Host dragons draw their power from the primal instincts of insects and, despite their intelligence, often behave like the insects they gather to them. Host dragons despise answering questions and violently defy all attempts others make to understand their nature.

Notes.Skills: Acrobatics +18, Athletics +24, Intimidation +24, Nature +22, Stealth +20, Survival +22
Notes.Abilities:
**Covered in Bugs.** **Trigger** The dragon critically fails a saving throw

**Effect** Swarming insects interfere with the effect, sacrificing themselves to protect their host's body and mind. The dragon attempts a DC 17. On a success, the dragon fails the saving throw instead of critically failing.

**Frightful Presence.** 90 feet. DC 30

**+2 status to all saves vs. mental.** 

**Excruciating Bites.** A creature that takes damage from a host dragon's jaws Strike or is swallowed by the dragon is also bitten by hundreds of tiny insects; the creature must succeed at a DC 28 save or be Enfeebled 2 for 1 round.

**One with Swarms.** The host dragon is immune to any attack made by a swarm of insects or similar creature (at the GM's discretion).

**Swallow Whole.** Large, 3d10+7 bludgeoning plus excruciating bites, Rupture 26

**Swarm Breath.** The dragon disgorges a swarm of biting insects that deals 9d8 piercing |options:area-damage damage in a 40-foot cone (DC 30 save). They can't use Swarm Breath again for 1d4 rounds.

**Swarm Shape.** The dragon transforms into an insect swarm. They drop all held, worn, and carried items. While in this form, they can't use attack actions (except Swarming Bites and Swarm Breath) and can't cast spells, but they can move through areas small enough for their individual insects to fit without having to Squeeze. They can use the same action to coalesce back into their normal form.

**Swarming Bites.** **Requirements** The dragon is a swarm

**Effect** Each enemy in the swarm's space takes 8d6 piercing damage (DC 30 save). A creature that fails its save is also Enfeebled 1 for 1 round.

entities.name: Host Dragon (Ancient, Spellcaster)
entities.description: Innumerable insects follow these lumbering, ravenous dragons wherever they roam, swarming around them and living in the countless orifices along the host dragon's body. The dragon is both a part of the swarm itself and a part of the swarm's ecosystem—the swarm feeds on their body, and the dragon feeds on the swarm in a grotesque, centuries-long cycle that somehow results in the host dragon growing larger and more powerful even if they feed on no other substance in their lifetime. Host dragons draw their power from the primal instincts of insects and, despite their intelligence, often behave like the insects they gather to them. Host dragons despise answering questions and violently defy all attempts others make to understand their nature.

Notes.Skills: Acrobatics +26, Athletics +32, Intimidation +29, Nature +28, Stealth +29, Survival +28
Notes.Abilities:
**Covered in Bugs.** **Trigger** The dragon critically fails a saving throw

**Effect** Swarming insects interfere with the effect, sacrificing themselves to protect their host's body and mind. The dragon attempts a DC 17. On a success, the dragon fails the saving throw instead of critically failing.

**Frightful Presence.** 90 feet. DC 37

**+2 status to all saves vs. mental.** 

**Excruciating Bites.** A creature that takes damage from a host dragon's jaws Strike or is swallowed by the dragon is also bitten by hundreds of tiny insects; the creature must succeed at a DC 34 save or be Enfeebled 2 for 1 round.

**Fast Swallow.** **Trigger** The dragon Grabs a creature

**Effect** The dragon uses Swallow Whole.

**One with Swarms.** The host dragon is immune to any attack made by a swarm of insects or similar creature (at the GM's discretion).

**Swallow Whole.** Large, 3d10+7 bludgeoning plus excruciating bites, Rupture 26

**Swarm Breath.** The dragon disgorges a swarm of biting insects that deals 12d8 piercing ,2d6 persistent,piercing |options:area-damage damage in a 50-foot cone (DC 37 save). They can't use Swarm Breath again for 1d4 rounds.

**Swarm Shape.** The dragon transforms into an insect swarm. They drop all held, worn, and carried items. While in this form, they can't use attack actions (except Swarming Bites and Swarm Breath) and can't cast spells, but they can move through areas small enough for their individual insects to fit without having to Squeeze. They can use the same action to coalesce back into their normal form.

**Swarming Bites.** **Requirements** The dragon is a swarm

**Effect** Each enemy in the swarm's space takes 12d6 piercing damage (DC 37 save). A creature that fails its save is also Enfeebled 1 for 1 round.
Notes.Spells: Energy Aegis, Regenerate, Root of all Pain, Field of Life, Carcinization, Toxic Cloud, Wall of Stone, Unfettered Movement, Earthbind, Life Seal, Wall of Wind, Entangling Flora, Environmental Endurance, Speak with Animals, Water Breathing, Ant Haul, Caustic Blast, Detect Magic, Detect Poison, Fear, Seek the Stars, Stumble, Tangle Vine

entities.name: Ichor Lord
entities.description:
Orocoran ichor lords are blessed by the Newborn—ichor flows through their veins, and they can conjure short-lived fonts of ichor. Most gather desperate orocorans around them, controlling their brethren through access to ichor.

Native to the now-destroyed planet of Aucturn, orocorans are foul and desperate creatures, cast adrift in space as they yearn to consume once more the essence of the Newborn god or fragments of the womb it gestated within. They're irritable, violent, and utterly anguished.

While some orocorans have broken free of their addiction and regained their clarity of mind and sense of self, the orocorans presented here are those who still rely on Aucturn's eldritch fluids.

Notes.Skills: Acrobatics +18, Deception +21, Intimidation +21, Occultism +15, Religion +15, Stealth +18, Survival +17
Notes.Abilities:
**Ichor Spray.** **Trigger** The ichor lord is dealt piercing or slashing damage

**Effect** Hallucinogenic ichor spurts from the ichor lord's wound, dealing 1d6 mental |options:area-damage damage to non-orocoran creatures in a 10-foot emanation centered on the ichor lord (DC 28 save).

**Hallucinate.** An orocoran's stomach fluids are laced with hallucinogens due to their consumption of the ichor-like birthing fluids expelled by Aucturn during the hatching of the Newborn.

A creature hit with the projectile vomit must succeed at a DC 28 save or be Confused for 1 round (1d4 rounds on a critical failure).

**Ichor Wellspring.** **Requirements** The ichor lord is touching solid ground

**Frequency** once per hour

**Effect** With a psychic cry to the Newborn, the ichor lord tears open the earth, causing a geyser of hallucinogenic ichor to burst from the ground within 100 feet. This geyser occupies a 50-foot-tall cylinder with a 10-foot radius base. The base of this geyser must be on the ground or a similar solid surface, and the geyser must be oriented vertically. Each creature in the area takes 4d6 bludgeoning damage and 4d6 mental damage, with a DC 28 save. A creature pushed into the air by the geyser can't be pushed beyond the top of the geyser. After being pushed into the air, a creature falls unless it's flying, is in zero gravity, or has some other means of staying aloft in its current environment, taking falling damage as normal.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Success** The creature takes half damage and isn't pushed into the air.

**Failure** The creature takes full damage and is pushed 20 feet into the air.

**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage and is pushed 40 feet into the air. The geyser continues to flow for 1 minute, gently raining ichor in a 30-foot emanation centered on the geyser's base. An orocoran in the area of this rain can drink the ichor once per round as a single action with the manipulate trait; if they do, they become invigorated, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to damage rolls and resistance 5 to physical damage until the beginning of their next turn.

**Lick Wounds.** **Frequency** once per round

**Requirements** A creature within reach of the orocoran's proboscis is taking persistent bleed damage

**Effect** The orocoran flicks out their proboscis and sups on the flowing blood of their enemy. The orocoran regains Hit Points equal to the target's persistent bleed value.
Notes.Spells: Read Omens, Entropy Strike, Personal Gravity, Share Pain, Void Whispers, Augury, Augury, Blur, Detect Thoughts, See the Unseen (Constant), Bane, Daze, Detect Magic, Eldritch Lance, Enfeeble, Fear, Mind Skewer, Telekinetic Hand, Void Warp

entities.name: Ignurso
entities.description:
Adventurers exploring active geothermal areas might encounter one of the extreme habitat's most unique creatures: ignursos. These ursine burrowers are partially armored with scales and a fearsome horn. They're sedentary by nature, but when disturbed, their rage combines the ferocity of a bear mauling with the heat of a pyroclastic flow.

Ignursos are specially adapted to survive in extremely hot climates but thrive anywhere warm. Those that inhabit less hospitable planets tend to stay underground and hibernate during the coldest parts of the year.

Scavengers by nature, ignursos can't take their next meal for granted. However, these clever creatures can manipulate their environment to trap prey. Ignursos have been observed creating large networks of burrows right before volcanic eruptions, seemingly because they understand lava flows will follow this path of least resistance. These tunnels turn to rivers of red-hot lava perfectly positioned to strand fleeing wildlife. Ignursos then return for their spoils after the worst of the eruption has passed.

Ignursos have a significant impact on volcanic ecosystems. Burrowing ignursos break up solid rock—often freshly deposited after an eruption—kick-starting the process of soil formation that's necessary for the return of plants. Some dig too close to underground magma chambers, turning their tunnels into volcanic vents that release lava and gases. In this way, they make explosive, damaging eruptions much less likely and provide a moderating force on a harsh environment.

Notes.Abilities:
**Smoke Vision.** The ignurso ignores the Concealed condition from smoke.

**Lavaproof.** The ignurso is immune environmental fire damage and fatigue from to heat and lava

**Reactive Strike.** 

**Thermal Venting.** 20 feet. The ignurso is shrouded in a cloud of smoke and ash. Creatures within the aura are Concealed, and creatures outside it are concealed to creatures within. The ignurso can deactivate or activate this aura as a single action, which has the concentrate trait.

**Mauler.** The ignurso gains a +3 circumstance bonus to damage rolls against creatures it has Grabbed or Restrained.

**Rend.** Claw

**Spew Lava.** The ignurso expels lava in a 30-foot cone, dealing 6d6 fire |options:area-damage damage (DC 20 save). A creature that fails its save also takes 1d6 persistent,fire |options:area-damage damage. The ignurso can't Spew Lava again for 1d4 rounds.

entities.name: Illumantula
entities.description:
Though it only recently appeared in the shattered red deserts of the planet Akiton, the so-called illumantula has already become the stuff of local legend and folklore. Emerging shortly after the crash of the mysterious First Ones vessel now only known as the Wreck of the Returned, the illumantula was so named by the shobhad desert guides who first encountered the creature and compared it to the deadly spiders of the Akitonian glaciers. Other Pact Worlds citizens have taken to the name, as the closest descriptive title for the being has simply been "a spider made of light."

Content—for now—to spend its days wandering the Wreck of the Returned and the immediately surrounding area, the illumantula has only had a handful of meaningful engagements since its appearance. The first was against a group of Hellknights of the Order of the Eclipse, where the illumantula systematically unmade 80 of their best-trained troops in under two minutes. Only weeks after the engagement, a group of Stewards attempting to enter the Wreck of the Returned were discovered and engaged at the periphery of the illumantula's patrol path. Only two of 12 commandos managed to escape, and their accounts of the illumantula and its powers are contradictory, leaving the Stewards unable to make effective plans for further encounters.

A strict quarantine has been set up to match the illumantula's patrol path, as calculated by the meticulous anacites of Investigation Site **A01**. The Aballonian constructs know the being to be related to the First Ones and dedicate their time to finding a means of communicating with the swarm of technological bits that patrol the outer wastes of the crashed starship. So far, they've had no success, and they've sent out an urgent call for linguistics and computers experts from across the Pact Worlds to travel to Akiton and aid their research.

Where the anacites continue their experiments, scholars of Eloritu have uncovered a disturbing connection between the illumantula and the concept of alternate realities. Somehow, the actions of the illumantula produce fixed points in reality, where the unique powers of creatures with greater connections to the multiverse are somehow stymied or forced to adhere to the illumantula's will. The reason for this phenomenon remains a mystery, though one the anacites seem blissfully ignorant to explore.

The appearance of the illumantula has led to the belief that it's a protector for the ancient technology of the mysterious First Ones. Similarities between the illumantula's technological bits and extracted data from Aballon have all but confirmed this theory. However, the association begs the question: is there just one illumantula, or is it merely one of many such highly advanced guardian constructs for the First Ones, a species who might be beyond anything the Pact Worlds could contend with?

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, doomed, drained, fatigued, mental, nonlethal-attacks, paralyzed, poison, precision, prone, restrained, sickened, unconscious, grabbed
Stats.Resistances: acid 10, cold 10, electricity 20, fire 20, physical 20, sonic 10

Notes.Skills: Acrobatics +40, Athletics +40, Computers +38, Intimidation +46, Occultism +49, Stealth +40
Notes.Abilities:
**Telepathy.** 300 feet

**Mutable Form.** The illumantula is a grouping of tiny tech bits that project energy between themselves, though the illumantula functions as single creature. The illumantula's size gives its space while being fully dispersed, though it can take actions to change its size. The illumantula can occupy the same space as other creatures and must do so to use some of its actions.

**Reactive Unmaking.** **Trigger** A creature moves within the illumantula's space or uses a manipulate action, move action, or ranged attack within 100 feet of the illumantula

**Effect** The illumantula attempts a ranged Strike against the triggering creature. If the attack is a critical hit and the trigger was a manipulate action, the illumantula disrupts that action. This Strike doesn't count toward the illumantula's multiple attack penalty, and its multiple attack penalty doesn't apply to this Strike.

**Relativity Field.** Creatures sharing a space with the illumantula can't use any actions or abilities with the fortune trait. A creature beginning its turn within the illumantula's space can't use actions or ability with the fortune trait until the end of their turn. The illumantula has weakness 10 against any ability or action affected by the fortune trait that successfully damages it.

**Energy Bombardment.** The illumantula releases coordinated blasts from each of its constituent bits at creatures within its form. Each enemy in the illumantula's space takes 12d8 electricity damage (DC 49 save). A creature that fails its save is also Blinded for 1 round (or 1 minute on a critical failure). The blinding is a visual effect.

**Reform.** **Frequency** once per round

**Effect** The illumantula changes its size to either Huge, Large or Medium as desired. When changing size in this manner, the illumantula can determine what direction its new space takes up or what portion of its existing space is removed. This movement doesn't trigger reactions.

**Unreality Engine.** When the illumantula scores a critical hit with a transreality beam Strike, the target becomes Doomed 1, or increases its doomed value by 1 if it was already doomed.
Notes.Spells: Event Horizon, Atomic Blast, Call Cosmos, Promession (at will), Slice Reality (at will), Truesight (constant), Control Machine (at will), Unfettered Movement (constant), Electrotether (at will), Dispel Magic (at will), Analyze Target, Detect Magic, Implant Data, Read Aura, Seek the Stars

entities.name: Iridia
entities.description:
When mortals encounter spectra outside the drift, that encounter is usually with an iridia. These opalescent, bipedal ambassadors travel the cosmos as messengers and agents of the Drift, extolling the benefits of new and emergent technologies. They champion growth and improvement in all aspects of life but especially focus on the advancement of new technologies. Their goals often put them at odds with those who forswear controversial and dangerous tech or who approach new and untested discoveries with caution.

Iridias are known to visit remote worlds in the Vast, far away from Absalom Station and the Drift lanes where Triune's original signal and the secrets of Drift travel were suppressed, lost, or misunderstood. They bring the people of these isolated worlds instructions to achieve interstellar travel and a second chance to join the galactic community.

In the Great Beyond, time is measured not in hundreds, thousands, or millions of years, but rather in eons—in iterations of reality itself. Only rising to prominence within the last three centuries alongside the advent and proliferation of Drift technology, spectra have thrived in a burgeoning niche of the otherwise stagnant zeitgeist of the Great Beyond.

Though their origins and objectives remain shrouded in mystery, encounters with spectra revolve around new technological discoveries, sharing the knowledge of faster-than-light travel, and protecting the Drift. No one knows if spectra existed before the Drift, but their connection to the hyperspace plane is indisputable. Prominent metaphysicians believe spectra were created as amalgams of raw quintessence pulled into the Drift, just as the Drift itself grows from pieces of the Multiverse. If this is true, spectra's interest in the proliferation of Drift technology takes a subtle sinister turn, as each new Drift engine serves to harvest the Great Beyond and all its denizens for the growth of the Drift and spectra themselves.

Notes.Skills: Acrobatics +16, Computers +18, Deception +14, Diplomacy +16, Occultism +14, Piloting +14
Notes.Abilities:
**Arc Network.** The iridia can communicate through items and creatures with the tech trait, projecting sound from and speaking through the item or creature's voice, speakers, or other audio output. In addition, the excuba can use any item or creature with the tech trait within their digital telepathy aura as the point of origin for their spells and abilities when calculating range, distance, line of effect, and area of effect.

**Slip Drive.** An iridia has an internal biomechanical Drift engine, allowing them to function as a Drift engine for a starship or vehicle they pilot as a 1-minute activity. An excuba can enter or exit the Drift themself as a 1-minute activity. When an excuba gets a critical failure on a Piloting check to Navigate or Plot a Course through the Drift, they get a failure instead.

**Techsense.** The iridia senses creatures and objects with the tech trait as a precise sense within the listed range.

**Digital Telepathy.** 100 feet. An iridia can communicate telepathically with any item or creature with the tech trait within their aura as well as with other technologically telepathic creatures (such as those with shortwave and similar abilities). This ability also allows the spectra to remotely attempt Computers checks within their aura.

**Reactive Strike.** 

**Shift Dimensionality.** **Frequency** once per round

**Trigger** The iridia is targeted by a ranged Strike

**Effect** A rainbow of visual distortion cascades across the iridia. They desynchronize from reality and are briefly replaced by a two-dimensional rendering, gaining concealment against the triggering Strike.

**Change Shape.** The excuba can take on the appearance of any Small or Medium humanoid.
Notes.Spells: Truespeech (constant), Translocate (at will), Holographic Memory, Caustic Conversion, Detect Thoughts, Inject Nanobots, Skim Data (at will), Delete, Implant Data, Mending, Seek the Stars, Wisp Ally

entities.name: Irradiated Undead Charger
entities.description:
Chargers, known by as many different names as their planets of origin, usually spawn from the irradiated corpses of beasts slain by natural or manufactured nuclear disasters. These quadrupedal, animalistic undead are so named for their mighty charge attack.

To survive in the unforgiving expanse of space, creatures must be naturally adapted or take protective measures. While the dead rarely need such precautions against these threats, sometimes radiation can animate a corpse (or several) to a state of undeath!

Scientists and religious scholars alike debate whether a specific type of radiation is to blame for this phenomenon that spontaneously triggers unlife, but all agree on the dangers such irradiated creatures pose. Many types of radiation could be the cause: intense bursts of cosmic radiation emitted by the stars, magically enhanced radioactive isotopes found in a planet's or moon's crust, or even the advent of new energy sources in a society (or its radioactive waste) contaminating the land. Regardless of their specific origin, irradiated undead all pose the same threat—they emit ionizing radiation that ravages everything around them.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, mental, paralyzed, poison, radiation, unconscious

Notes.Abilities:
**Meltdown.** **Trigger** The irradiated undead plant is reduced to 0 Hit Points by energy damage of any kind

**Effect** The energy acts as a catalyst for a nuclear reaction, causing the plant to explode and dealing 9d6 poison |options:area-damage damage to all creatures in a 20-foot emanation with a DC 24 save.

**Radioactive Remains.** 20 feet. A creature entering or starting its turn inside the aura is exposed to extreme radiation.

**Void Healing.** 

**Charged Burst.** The irradiated charger triggers a localized radioactive reaction as it charges. It Strides once and then Strikes. A creature damaged by this attack takes 1 additional point of void damage for every space the charger moved prior to making its Strike. On a critical hit, the creature is also knocked Prone.

**Trample.** Medium or smaller, Tusk, DC 24

entities.name: Irradiated Undead Flyer
entities.description:

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, mental, paralyzed, poison, radiation, unconscious

Notes.Abilities:
**Meltdown.** **Trigger** The irradiated undead plant is reduced to 0 Hit Points by energy damage of any kind

**Effect** The energy acts as a catalyst for a nuclear reaction, causing the plant to explode and dealing 5d6 poison |options:area-damage damage to all creatures in a 20-foot emanation with a DC 19 save.

**Radioactive Remains.** 20 feet. A creature entering or starting its turn inside the aura is exposed to severe radiation.

**Void Healing.** 

**Strafing Snap.** The irradiated undead flyer Strides twice up to its Speed in a straight line, making a single wing slash Strike against all creatures whose spaces it flies adjacent to. All creatures damaged by the Strafing Snap are considered to be within the flyer's aura at the start of their next turn. The flyer can't use Strafing Snap again for 1d4 rounds.

**Wing Spasm.** **Frequency** once per minute

**Effect** The irradiated undead flyer channels energy into its wings, forcing all creatures in a 10-foot emanation to attempt a DC 19 save.

**Critical Success** No effect.

**Success** The creature takes 1d8 void |options:area-damage damage.

**Failure** The creature takes 2d8 void |options:area-damage damage and is pushed back 5 feet.

**Critical Failure** The creature takes 4d8 void |options:area-damage damage and is pushed back 10 feet.

entities.name: Irradiated Undead Plant
entities.description:
Flora are often the first victims of industrialization, dying petal by petal and blade of grass at a time before anybody even notices a loss of habitat. When nuclear fallout corrupts the hardiest species of vegetation, sometimes their irradiated seeds inexplicably bloom into new, unliving specimens.

To survive in the unforgiving expanse of space, creatures must be naturally adapted or take protective measures. While the dead rarely need such precautions against these threats, sometimes radiation can animate a corpse (or several) to a state of undeath!

Scientists and religious scholars alike debate whether a specific type of radiation is to blame for this phenomenon that spontaneously triggers unlife, but all agree on the dangers such irradiated creatures pose. Many types of radiation could be the cause: intense bursts of cosmic radiation emitted by the stars, magically enhanced radioactive isotopes found in a planet's or moon's crust, or even the advent of new energy sources in a society (or its radioactive waste) contaminating the land. Regardless of their specific origin, irradiated undead all pose the same threat—they emit ionizing radiation that ravages everything around them.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, mental, paralyzed, poison, radiation, unconscious

Notes.Abilities:
**Meltdown.** **Trigger** The irradiated undead plant is reduced to 0 Hit Points by energy damage of any kind

**Effect** The energy acts as a catalyst for a nuclear reaction, causing the plant to explode and dealing 3d6 poison |options:area-damage damage to all creatures in a 20-foot emanation with a DC 16 save.

**Void Healing.** 

**Radioactive Remains.** 20 feet. A creature entering or starting its turn inside the aura is exposed to mild radiation.

**Seedpod.** When a irradiated undead plant Strikes a creature, some of its contaminated seeds stick to the target. The irradiated undead plant gains the Sprout action. An affected creature can remove this seedpod as an Interact action.

**Sprout.** **Requirements** One or more creatures within 60 feet of the irradiated undead plant are currently host to at least one seedpod

**Effect** The irradiated undead plant pulses with energy, causing the seedpods to sprout vines. Creatures hosting a seedpod must attempt a DC 16 save.

**Critical Success** No effect.

**Success** The creature takes 1d6 piercing |options:area-damage damage.

**Failure** The creature takes 2d6 piercing |options:area-damage damage and is Slowed 2 for 1 round.

**Critical Failure** The creature takes 2d6 piercing |options:area-damage damage, is slowed 2 for 1 round, and is Immobilized until it Escapes. Until it Escapes, the creature is a new source of the irradiated undead plant's radioactive remains aura with a 5-foot emanation.

entities.name: Jinchori Endling
entities.description:
Jinchoris were sinuous quadrupedal reptiles that dug tunnel systems through the desert world of Priori-8. Their iridescent scales grew into dense armored plates, protecting them from the hunters who sought their brilliant frills as fashion accessories. Poachers started flooding jinchori tunnels with poison gas in a method that proved all too effective and wiped the species out. Years after, visitors to Priori-8 spy gleaming wyrms stalking them through caves and tunnels, and poachers die choking on spectral poison.

Every species follows a natural arc as it emerges and evolves: rising, thriving, declining, and falling into extinction. When extremely unnatural ends to these paths occur—when unexpected predation, industrialization, or alien pathogens wipe out a population—endlings are born. These spectral members of extinct species typically develop as "answers" to their eradication. Xenobiologists differ on what creates endlings, unable to confirm whether the creatures are a species' last collective sorrow made manifest or just vengeful individual spirits—the last lights to go out.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, precision, unconscious

Notes.Abilities:
**Huntersight.** A jinchori can sense the presence of any creature wielding weapons as a precise sense at the listed range.

**Reactive Strike.** 

**Rejuvenation.** When an endling is destroyed, it reforms after 2d4 days within the area where it first emerged, fully healed. An endling can be permanently destroyed only if someone determines the reason for its existence and sets right whatever prevents the spirit from resting, such as an act of decolonization, ecological restoration, or curing the disease responsible for its extinction.

**Void Healing.** 

**Noxious Breath.** The jinchori endling floods the air with toxic fumes, dealing 4d12 poison |options:area-damage damage in a 30-foot cone (DC 22 save). A creature that fails its save is also Sickened 1 (or Sickened 2 on a critical failure). The jinchori can't use Noxious Breath again for 1d4 rounds.

entities.name: Jinsul Pontiff
entities.description:
Pontiffs rally jinsuls to a near suicidal frenzy in the throes of combat. Part magic wielder and part orator, they act as inspirational battlefield leaders. Each serves one of the major jinsul hierarchs, who in turn act as the leaders of the overall Jinsul Hierocracy.

Jinsuls are a warlike species scattered across the Vast. Six-legged creatures with a bulbous body covered in eyes, jinsuls have notable segments of chitin along with a set of upper forelimbs for using equipment. They long ago lived in the region of space known as the Scoured Stars but eventually departed and settled on the harsh world of Rax. In recent years, the divine herald Dhurus unified the jinsuls into a cohesive force known as the Jinsul Hierocracy, which briefly retook the Scoured Stars. A joint alliance between several species and members of the Starfinder Society defeated Dhurus and scattered the jinsuls back into the Vast.

With countless bases and fleets operating in deep space, jinsuls mostly act as raiders, scavenging for equipment and testing their mettle against other species. Indoctrinated to view themselves as a superior species, with only other inhabitants of the Scoured Stars having any value, jinsuls prefer to engage in short-ranged combat with their foes.

Jinsuls aren't numerous enough to fill every need on the many ships and starbases they control across the galaxy. Instead, they rely on robots and automated computer systems (always commanded by at least one jinsul officer) to keep their space stations running efficiently. These systems are programmed to be just as deadly and ruthless as jinsuls themselves; even the most innocuous automated system or robot, like a garbage collector, might wield deadly weapons or contain vicious technomagical countermeasures.

Notes.Abilities:
**All-Around Vision.** 

**Vitality Network.** A jinsul pontiff can channel vitality to up to four bonded allies as though they were a mystic. This network stores up to 20 healing Hit Points and begins combat full.

**Fill Vitality.** **Frequency** once per round

**Effect** The jinsul pontiff restores 6 healing Hit Points to their vitality network, up to its maximum.

**Strider Leap.** The jinsul Strides and then performs a long-jump. They can Stride less than 10 feet and not automatically fail their check to Long Jump.

**Transfer Vitality.** The jinsul pontiff transfers any number of Hit Points from their vitality network to a visible bonded target.
Notes.Spells: Selective Invisibility, Share Pain, Void Whispers, Blur, Bless, Mind Skewer, Overheat, Shifting Surge, Soothe, Soothe

entities.name: Jinsul Trooper
entities.description:
The lowest ranked jinsuls in a warband are the subordinate troopers. These jinsuls prove themselves by hurtling toward the enemy, discharging weapons, and closing with their vicious leg blades. Those troopers who survive long enough are recognized and promoted through the harsh jinsul military lifestyle.

entities.name: Jinsul Warblooded
entities.description:
Warblooded are jinsuls who have survived at least a half-dozen engagements in service to the Jinsul Hierocracy. They take on roles of minor leadership or as elite sharpshooters and commandos in a unit of other jinsuls. Warblooded often elect to sit out of engagements that they deem "beneath" them, opting to train up or observe fights from a distance unless they need to step in as reinforcements. These jinsuls often use their extra training time to learn how to pick out critical foes in a battle.

Notes.Skills: Athletics +8, Deception +11, Intimidation +8, Occultism +13, Piloting +10, Religion +16, Survival +8
Notes.Abilities:
**All-Around Vision.** 

**Aim.** The jinsul aims with their melee or ranged weapon against a target within 60 feet. For the rest of their turn, successful Strikes made with that weapon deal an additional 1d4 precision damage and reduce the target's cover bonus to AC by 1.

**Strider Leap.** The jinsul Strides and then performs a long-jump. They can Stride less than 10 feet and not automatically fail their check to Long Jump.

entities.name: Juvenile Nyssholora
entities.description:
Despite their age, juvenile nyssholoras remain dangerous and formidable predators.

Incredibly ferocious, nyssholoras are dinosaur-like creatures that number among the most dangerous and feared apex predators on the planet of Castrovel. These walking weapons brandish lethal biology: a massive maw lined with twin rows of razor-sharp teeth, scythe-shaped phasic blade forearms that vibrate at ultrasonic speeds, and a scourge-like tail capable of absorbing electricity from the surrounding atmosphere. Yet, nyssholoras are also cunning and perceptive—a frill of tentacles that crowns their head detect telepathic signals, making it impossible for the local formians and lashuntas to escape their notice. Their phasic blades can cut through walls and vehicles as easily as underbrush, ensuring prey have nowhere safe to hide.

Notes.Abilities:
**Telepathy Sense.** A nyssholora senses all creatures that have telepathy, limited telepathy, or a similar ability, such as a mystic's bond, as an imprecise sense at the listed range. This sense works through walls and other obstacles.

**Crunch.** **Frequency** once per round

**Requirements** A creature is Grabbed in the nyssholora's jaws

**Effect** The nyssholora chomps down on the creature, dealing 1d8+7 piercing damage.

**Discordant Bellow.** The nyssholora unleashes a blast of discordant sound that deal 5d6 sonic |options:area-damage damage in a 30-foot cone (DC 21 save). Objects and constructs in the area are treated as if they had half as much Hardness as usual. Creatures that critically fail their saving throw are also Slowed 1 for 1 round. The nyssholora can't use Discordant Bellow again for 1d4 rounds.

**Phasic Strike.** A nyssholora's phasic blade Strike treats any object or construct it hits as if the target had half as much Hardness as usual.

entities.name: Jygyk
entities.description:
Jygyks embody remorseless revenge, stalking mortals and slaying them at great distances. Three legs create the unflinching stability needed for their sniper shots, and lenslike eyes scope out their prey up to 2 miles away.

Jygyks become obsessed with their intended victims and have the capacity to nurse intense grudges against dozens of mortals at once. A fresh jygyk might begin by targeting people they hated in their mortal life or seek victims who match a certain profile.

Jygyks move cautiously, typically stalking their targets for weeks, memorizing movement patterns and noting routines, to pinpoint the ideal time and place to strike. Close-range combat can prove disastrous for them, so they prioritize fleeing if confronted in close quarters.

All mortal creatures have souls that are usually judged in the Boneyard after their demise. The souls of individuals who lived sinful lives—usually by hurting others or acting selfishly—are sent to the Outer Rifts, where they eventually coalesce into demons. These fiends care for nothing but the corruption of mortal life to ensure that the ranks of their fellow demons never wane.

Notes.Abilities:
**Mental Fragility.** While a jygyk embodies remorseless vengeance, they can't fathom being attacked in kind. If a creature critically hits a jygyk who damaged it on the jygyk's previous turn, the jygyk takes 3d6 mental damage.
