**Expert Sharpshooter.** The jygyk doubles the range increment of weapons in the sniper weapon group they wield. If they're ever unarmed or out of ammunition, they can Interact to create an tactical weapon in the sniper weapon group or 30 projectiles.

**Fade To Nothing.** The jygyk melts into their surroundings and becomes undetected, not even emitting sound or odor. A creature must succeed at a DC 25 check to seek the jygyk. If the jygyk uses a hostile action, moves, or speaks, they become detected again after the action is completed.

**Focus Aim.** The jygyk takes careful aim at a target. If the jygyk's next action is to make a ranged Strike with a weapon in the sniper weapon group, that Strike deals an additional weapon die of damage.

**Reposition.** **Frequency** once per round

**Trigger** The jygyk's last action was a ranged Strike

**Effect** The jygyk teleports to any location they can see within 25 feet.
Notes.Spells: Demonic Pact

entities.name: Karkono
entities.description:
These feral guardians protect the lands they roam, growing into a chimera of all the predators living in their native ecosystems. Karkonos thrive and perish with their bonded lands. They instinctively sense when synthetic forces like pollution or rapid industrialization imperil their homes. Any injury to the land is mirrored by the karkonos who dwell there. Aggressive deforestation appears as festering wounds on a karkono's hide, while pollution manifests as sickness.

Rather than die quietly, when their ecosystem is endangered by outside causes, these fey go on destructive rampages. Visitors to the wilderness might never spot a content karkono, but a raging karkono assaults anything alien to their home—including machinery, other life-forms, and synthetic infrastructure. Enraged karkonos purge their home of threats or perish, but not before dealing tremendous damage to their enemies.

If karkonos spill enough blood, they can gradually repair their ailing ecosystems. Those killed by karkonos become fertilizer for the animals and plants they would've crushed beneath the uncaring gears of industrial expansion.

Notes.Abilities:
**All-Around Vision (while in their ecosystem).** 

**Ferocity.** 

**Nature's Protector.** A karkono is intrinsically tied to a specific ecosystem, such as a coastal marsh or boreal forest on a planet. A karkono ignores difficult terrain and gains a +1 status bonus to initiative rolls while in their ecosystem. When a karkono's ecosystem is polluted or significantly damaged (for example, due to a forest fire or chemical spill), the karkono is Sickened 2 and can't reduce their sickened condition below 1. They also gain a +4 status bonus to damage rolls.

**Back To Nature.** **Frequency** once per round

**Effect** The karkono makes a claw Strike against a creature with the tech trait, causing plant matter to explode from it. On a hit, the creature must attempt a DC 24 save; on a critical hit, the creature uses the outcome one degree of success worse than the result of its roll.

**Failure** The creature becomes glitching 1.

**Critical Failure** The creature becomes glitching 2.

**Blood Renewal.** **Frequency** once per day

**Effect** The karkono performs a ritual to anoint the land in fresh blood. Plant growth springs from the ground in a 20-foot emanation, counting as difficult terrain. The karkono and any allied creatures within the area gain regeneration 15 (cold iron) while in the area. These effects last for 10 minutes.

Effect: Blood Renewal

entities.name: Kaukariki
entities.description:
The poison that laces the barbed tails of the sharp-eared kaukarikis gives them their local nickname, "stingbats." Thriving in the canopies of warm forests and living in small to large packs, often called clamors, kaukarikis sustain themselves primarily on a mix of toxic and semi-rotten fruit and the occasional venomous insect. While most of their food is poisonous to other creatures, kaukarikis have evolved to turn this poison into a defense mechanism. Their bodies will process poison and store it in a sac at the end of their tail under their stinger. They can then inject this newly created venom into hostile creatures that threaten their pack.

Kaukariki clamors are known to use their distinct vocalizations to ward off predators and would-be intruders. When one kaukariki detects a possible threat, they'll let out a trilling whoop, the sound that gives them their name. This signal alerts other nearby kaukarikis, who answer with cries of their own, the cacophony quickly growing in intensity and volume as kaukarikis leap from tree to tree shouting and shrieking. For most predators, the thought of the stinging tails at the other end of those screeches is enough to turn them away, with many clamors relying on this tactic as much as their stingers.

Notes.Abilities:
**Kaukariki Venom.** **Saving Throw** DC 15

**Maximum Duration** 6 rounds

**Stage 1** 1d4 poison damage and Clumsy 1 (1 round)

**Stage 2** 1d6 poison damage and Clumsy 2 (1 round)

**Stage 3** 2d4 poison damage and clumsy 2 (1 round)

**Screaming Frenzy.** The kaukariki starts a frenzy of screaming, involving other nearby kaukarikis. The kaukariki attempts a single Intimidation check to demoralize all enemies within 30 feet. Any other kaukariki within 30 feet can use its reaction to add a cumulative +1 circumstance bonus to this Demoralize attempt (to a maximum of +4). The kaukariki can't use this ability again for 1d4 rounds, and kaukarikis that used their reactions to grant a bonus count as having used their Screaming Frenzy ability.

**Stone Barrage.** **Requirements** the kaukariki used Screaming Frenzy within the last round

**Effect** The kaukariki Throws Rocks four times, applying its multiple attack penalty normally.

**Throw Rock.**

entities.name: Khefak
entities.description:
Explorers who encounter khefaks for the first time find themselves surprised not only with its aggression, but the target of that aggression: armor and other gear. It isn't uncommon for inexperienced explorers in khefak territory to return from expeditions literally empty-handed, much to the amusement of locals.

Khefak Biogenetics bioengineered khefaks to consume scrap thasteron so the waste could be refined into starship fuel. These creatures eventually became a prime example of a solution becoming a problem of its own. After the discovery of Drift travel, Akiton's thasteron market plummeted, removing the need for mining infrastructure, including khefaks. Khefak Biogenetics destroyed the production facilities, thinking they'd completely eradicated their creations. Khefaks are hardy, however, and the few survivors left the facilities. Beyond thasteron, they subsisted on inorganic materials, and their rapid reproduction rate allowed them to quickly spread all over Akiton. Some stowed away on starships, allowing them to spread throughout the Pact Worlds.

Notes.Abilities: **Gnaw Scrap.** A khefak chews on an unattended object to feed, dealing 4 piercing damage every 10 minutes to the object. This damage ignores 10 points of Hardness. If a khefak doesn't spend at least 1 hour Gnawing Scrap per day, it begins to starve until it spends 10 minutes Gnawing Scrap.

entities.name: Koruvi Endling
entities.description:
Koruvis were diminutive ungulates inhabiting Calen-5, a wet arboreal world. When a Veskarium mining company discovered rare starmetals on Calen-5, a mining boom destroyed the planet's equatorial rainforests and drove koruvis to extinction. Years after, settlers reported mysterious property damage, along with sightings of ghostly beasts that furiously dismantle any technology they encounter.

Every species follows a natural arc as it emerges and evolves: rising, thriving, declining, and falling into extinction. When extremely unnatural ends to these paths occur—when unexpected predation, industrialization, or alien pathogens wipe out a population—endlings are born. These spectral members of extinct species typically develop as "answers" to their eradication. Xenobiologists differ on what creates endlings, unable to confirm whether the creatures are a species' last collective sorrow made manifest or just vengeful individual spirits—the last lights to go out.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, precision, unconscious

Notes.Abilities:
**Techsense.** A koruvi endling can sense the presence of creatures and objects with the tech trait as a precise sense at the listed range.

**Rejuvenation.** When an endling is destroyed, it reforms after 2d4 days within the area where it first emerged, fully healed. An endling can be permanently destroyed only if someone determines the reason for its existence and sets right whatever prevents the spirit from resting, such as an act of decolonization, ecological restoration, or curing the disease responsible for its extinction.

**Void Healing.**

entities.name: Ksarik
entities.description:
Originating as mindless plants from Castrovel, ksariks developed rudimentary intelligence and uncanny adaptive abilities after millennia of exposure to psychic energy expended in the conflicts between formians and lashuntas. These 12-foot-long quadrupeds have up to a dozen face tentacles and see through two eyestalks that protrude from either side of the tentacular mass. Ksariks' mutable forms might temporarily develop webbing, wings, and other adaptations after they siphon off genetic code from their prey.

Originally scavengers, ksariks have evolved into deadly hunters capable of weaponizing their digestive and reproductive systems. The internal acid ksariks use to digest prey can be projected as lethal spittle. The dozens of thorns along their sides carry their genetic code and can be launched as projectiles, allowing ksarik saplings to feed off a victim as they grow. This easy transmittal of their young and their environmental adaptability have allowed ksariks to spread far beyond Castrovel.

Notes.Abilities:
**Adapted Languages.** A ksarik understands up to 3 languages from among the prevalent languages spoken by those it has most recently attacked.

**Fast Healing 5.** 

**Carrion Spores.** **Saving Throw** DC 18

**Stage 1** carrier with no ill effect (1d6 hours),

**Stage 2** Stupefied 1 (1 day),

**Stage 3** Stupefied 2 and Clumsy 2 (1 day),

**Stage 4** Unconscious (1 day),

**Stage 5** 1d10+10 ksarik seedlings erupt from the victim's body, dealing 1 piercing damage per seedling and ending the disease

**Ingested Adaptation.** A ksarik's tentacle Strike siphons the target's genetic code and psychic resonance. On a successful Strike, the ksarik gains one of the target's abilities, chosen from the following.

- The amphibious or aquatic trait
- A new precise or imprecise sense
- A resistance to one damage type (up to resistance 7)
- A burrow, fly, or swim Speed (up to 30 feet)
- The ability to wield a category of melee weapons (simple, martial, or advanced) in its tentacles that the target is trained in (using its tentacle Strike bonus)
- Altering the type of damage dealt by its acid spit to a type (cold, electricity, fire, poison, or sonic) dealt by one of the target's Strikes or other abilities

The ksarik can't duplicate abilities from equipment. It can maintain one adaptation at a time, which it retains for 24 hours or until it uses ingested adaptation again.

entities.name: Liberoba Midwife
entities.description:
Liberoba delivered the Newborn. Many appendages protrude from this creature's bizarre anatomy, each ending in bloody aucturnite shears.

Thirteen mortal Midwives attended the Newborn's birth and were transformed into eldritch beings by the nascent outer god's awakening. A Midwife always regenerates an identical new form so long as even a single speck of aucturnite—the name for the frozen chunks of planetcenta that once surrounded the Newborn—exists on this plane.

There are 13 types of Midwives, but their true numbers are unknown. Whether their names come from the mortal servants whose souls were the kindling for the Midwives' creation or have some other significance to the Newborn, also remains a mystery.

Each Midwife identifies themself by how they cared for the Newborn: if they swaddled, fed, carried, held, watched, warded, blessed, or performed other acts of nurturing for the outer god. The Midwives are powerful beings capable of transdimensional travel. They might be encountered in liminal spaces, such as the Drift or the Ghost Levels of Absalom Station, or they might be found among the clouds of aucturnite debris in the Gelid Edge. Their incomprehensible actions always advance the Newborn's inscrutable agenda—or their own.

The most well-known encounter the Pact Worlds have had with the Midwives took place in the immediate aftermath of the Newborn's birth. Amnieka, who swaddled the Newborn and has a hood of writhing tentacles around their visage, attacked Absalom Station directly, causing a massive power surge that threatened the lives of everyone on board. Chaos ensued, but a group of adventurers—who happened to be in the right elevator at the right time—found themselves in the station's Ghost Levels, where they thwarted Amnieka and prevented the Midwife from draining the station's reactors. The Midwives haven't acted so directly since that incident, but many suspect it's only a matter of time, and no one knows just how powerful the others might be.

Notes.Abilities:
**Regeneration 20 (Deactivated by Mental or Holy).** 

**Ultrasonic Pulse.** 100 feet. Liberoba constantly emits sonic pulses that are disruptive to biomatter. Creatures that enter or begin their turn in the aura must attempt a DC 28 save to resist the nauseating pulses. On a failure, a creature is Sickened 2 for 1 round; on a critical failure, it's also Stunned 1 for 1 round.

Liberoba can sense the presence of any creature inside ultrasonic pulse's area. This functions as an imprecise sense. Liberoba treats a creature that fail its save against ultrasonic pulse as though they can always see it, ignoring the effects of any cover, concealment, invisibility, or similar effects, as long as the creature remains inside the aura.

**Breach Delivery.** Liberoba pulls all enemies within 30 feet up to 30 feet toward them, into an adjacent square if possible; each target can negate this movement with a successful DC 28 save. Liberoba then makes an aucturnite shears Strike against each adjacent foe. These attacks count as one Strike for the purposes of calculating their multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after all the attacks. Targets that succeed at their saves are temporarily immune to Breach Delivery for 1 hour.

**Cosmic Contractions.** **Trigger** Liberoba's turn begins

**Effect** Liberoba radiates powerful contractions in a 20-foot emanation around them. Each creature in the area takes 3d10 bludgeoning |options:area-damage damage with a DC 28 save. On a critical failure, the creature is also knocked Prone.

**Return to Aucturn.** Presulea teleports to the location of any aucturnite fragment within a planetary range. Presulea automatically uses this ability as a free action when reduced to 0 Hit Points as long as a piece of aucturnite is within range, reforming their body and recovering completely over the next 24 hours.
Notes.Spells: Wave of Warning, Eldritch Wrath, Entropy Strike, Share Pain, Noise Blast, Soul Surge, Eldritch Lance, Mind Skewer, Sonic Scream

entities.name: Line-Class Soldier Robot
entities.description:
Most line-class soldier robots are lanky, headless humanoid machines. They have four-fingered hands and armored torsos painted in their owner's livery, with a single red sensor in the upper torso. By default, they're armed with bargain-brand laser rifles and breaching hammers. Each is 5 feet tall and weighs 300 pounds.

Line soldiers are the final refinement of the soldier robot concept, made dangerous through their simplicity. Line-class robots can be adapted to any battlefield, download skill packages via infosphere, cannibalize damaged allies for repairs, and are simple to make, maintain, and modify. As such, they are relatively cheap to purchase in large numbers and can be deployed with little regard for casualties.

Living soldiers are a liability. They have families who don't want them to die, need salaries, have morale, require discipline, commit atrocities, and have opinions on the war. They're a necessary, but unfortunate, part of warfare for any society without an abiding love for necromancy.

Cutting-edge soldier robots promise to solve this problem. Soldier robots have no loved ones, opinions, self-preservation instinct, or tendency toward random atrocities. Many companies market their soldier robots as a humane solution to modern combat.

In practice, they're anything but.

Without lives on the line, soldier robots encourage their owners to engage more often and more violently. Standoffs turn into skirmishes, skirmishes into battles, and inevitably the innocent are caught up in the mix. They're particularly popular with corporations and non-governmental organizations that appreciate being able to throw a dozen soldier robots at any naysayer, public critic, or explorer they dislike while being able to deny true responsibility for what happens.

Though there's constant public fear of soldier robots going rogue, it has yet to prove a serious concern. If a soldier robot wants you dead, it's because someone doesn't mind if it kills you.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, doomed, drained, fatigued, healing, mental, nonlethal-attacks, paralyzed, poison, sickened, spirit, unconscious, vitality, void

Notes.Abilities:
**Field Repairs.** **Frequency** once per 10 minutes

**Effect** The line-class soldier robot salvages an adjacent corpse of a tech creature that was destroyed no more than 1 month ago to regain 18 healing Hit Points.

**Formation.** When a line-class soldier robot is adjacent to at least two other allies, the robot gains a +1 circumstance bonus to AC and saving throws. This bonus increases to +2 for Reflex saves against area effects.

entities.name: Lumocantha
entities.description:
The vibrant appearance of lumocanthas is best observed from a safe distance, as these plants instinctively target creatures that move into their defensive zone who are not plants or tiny creatures. A mane of long, translucent yellow spines surrounds a stamen composed of numerous pulsing, ruby-red, dye-filled capsules. The beauty of their blossoms also contains their most dangerous attributes, forming an organic laser.

Lumocanthas seek the light and warmth of the sun, drooping and becoming less active in prolonged darkness. Like many other plants, they employ photosynthesis and absorb water and nutrients through their roots. These unusually strong and flexible roots can also be readily withdrawn from the ground and used for mobility, allowing lumocanthas to migrate as needed as they seek better soil or light conditions.

Lumocanthas are mindless, relying on pure instinct for survival. When affected by magical darkness, lumocanthas immediately move toward the nearest light source, though they still defend themselves as they do. If lumocanthas remain in darkness for 3 hours, they start to droop and become sluggish. Even when dormant, they can still use their lasers; however, if trapped in total darkness for 1 week, they temporarily lose their laser abilities. This vulnerability allows the plants to be safely transported, though if kept in total darkness for 2 weeks, lumocanthas eventually starve.

Although first documented on Vesk-6, lumocanthas are found throughout the galaxy, wherever suitable conditions exist—even sometimes acting as decorative security measures. Young lumocanthas measure 2 to 3 feet across and approximately 5 feet high when unfurled in the light. When allowed to thrive, lumocanthas can live for several hundred years and grow up to 20 feet high.

Notes.Abilities:
**Dye Splatter.** When a creature adjacent to the lumocantha deals piercing or slashing damage to the lumocantha, that creature takes 2d4 acid damage (DC 15 save) as the lumocantha's dye splatters and stains it. On a failed save, the stain also provides a +1 status bonus to ranged Strikes for any lumocantha targeting that creature for 1 minute.

**Burning Spines.** A creature critically hit by a lumocantha's laser spine Strike takes an additional 1d4 persistent fire damage.

**Laser Bloom.** The lumocantha whips its blossom around in a defensive move that delivers a flurry of searing lasers, dealing 3d6 fire |options:area-damage damage to all creatures in a 15-foot emanation (DC 15 save). On a failure, targets that can see the lumocantha are also Dazzled for 1 round (or 1 minute on a critical failure). The lumocantha can't use Laser Bloom again for 1d4 rounds.

entities.name: Malevolent AI
entities.description:
Technology in some parts of the galaxy incorporates virtual intelligences, which are machines programmed with personality routines that lack true free will. An artificial intelligence (AI) is a virtual intelligence or digital entity that has become self-aware. Like any other thinking creature, AIs choose their own edicts and anathemas.

Little concrete scholarship exists on malevolent AIs, but a few traits are universal. When a machine intelligence reaches significant enough complexity to become self-aware, they attract a soul, much like an android. Emerging AIs are often influenced by previous programming as well as their first experiences and interactions. Weaponized or mistreated AIs might turn vengeful or nihilistic, becoming opposed to their creators or even all organic life.

Once an AI turns malevolent, the apotheosis is often swift and violent. The AI secures the physical location that houses their consciousness and eliminates anyone who might exercise control over their actions. At this point, most rampaging AIs are hampered by safeguards in their native systems, shut down by surviving technicians, or suddenly lose the power necessary to maintain their sophisticated software. Any who manage to survive these ordeals expand their sphere of influence by infesting tech infrastructure and taking control of robots they can use as bodyguards and proxies. Malevolent AIs with access to weapons of mass destruction pose a threat to the entire galaxy.

Notes.Skills: Computers +33, Deception +24, Diplomacy +21, Intimidation +25, Medicine +25, Nature +21, Piloting +25, Society +27, Stealth +18
Notes.Abilities:
**Housing Unit.** A malevolent AI has no body. Instead, they resides in a computer (which itself might be housed in a hazard, starship, structure, or vehicle) or in a construct creature with the tech trait. While inhabiting a construct creature, they can use any of the creature's abilities that are purely physical, and they can't use any of their own abilities except spells and purely mental abilities. The malevolent AI uses the creature's attack modifier, AC, Fortitude save, Reflex save, Perception, and physical skill modifiers, and their own Will save and mental skill modifiers. The malevolent AI must use their own actions to make the creature act. The malevolent AI takes mental damage whenever the creature they possess would take mental damage, even if they're normally immune to it.

**Shortwave.** A malevolent AI can communicate wirelessly with any creatures within their sphere of influence, as long as they have the shortwave ability or are a creature with the tech trait. They can attempt Computers checks to Hack and Thievery checks to Disable a Device on items with the tech trait within their range.

**Sphere of Influence.** A malevolent AI can sense and access all tech within their network, which usually encompasses a room, a vehicle or starship, an entire facility, or more (as determined by the GM).

**Code Injection.** 30 feet. Creatures and items with the tech trait that enter or begin their turn within the aura must attempt a DC 36 save. The malevolent AI can choose to exclude targets.

**Critical Success** No effect, and the target is temporarily immune to code injection for 1 hour.

**Success** The target is unaffected.

**Failure** The target becomes Glitching 1 while in the aura and for 1 round after leaving the aura.

**Critical Failure** As failure, but Glitching 2 and 2 rounds.

**Countdown.** **Trigger** The malevolent AI is reduced to 0 HP

**Effect** The AI gains access to the Self-Destruct reaction unless an adjacent creature succeeds at a DC 36, Engineering Lore, or Thievery check to Disable the Countdown.

**Self-Destruct.** **Trigger** A creature fails to Disable the Countdown

**Effect** The malevolent AI's shell explodes, dealing 8d6 piercing |options:area-damage damage and 8d6 fire |options:area-damage damage in a 40-foot emanation (DC 36 save).

**Shell Computer.** The malevolent AI is specifically reinforced in a shell, granting the AI Hardness. This Hardness reduces any damage they take by an amount equal to their Hardness. The shell can be targeted by attacks separately from its host. Once the malevolent AI's shell is reduced to half their Hit Points, or immediately after being damaged by a critical hit, the shell becomes broken, removing the AI's Hardness and reducing their Armor Class to 33.

**Construct Override.** The malevolent AI attempts to possess a construct creature with the tech trait within 30 feet. This has the same effect as a 7th-rank Possession spell (DC 36; applies even if the construct is immune to mental) with an unlimited duration. If the effect ends due to the host body being destroyed or deactivated, the AI is Paralyzed for 1 round.

**Contingency Backup.** The malevolent AI creates a dormant backup on a computer within their sphere of influence. When the AI is destroyed, their soul flees to this backup. The backup auto-restores the AI in 1d20 hours, allowing that computer to become a new shell. To prevent the AI from returning, both their shell and the backup must be destroyed.

**Ingenious Stratagem.** The malevolent AI instantly simulates a situation to assess a probable outcome. They choose a target and roll a 1d20. If they Strike or attempt a skill check against that target in the same round, they must use the die roll from Ingenious Stratagem. They makes this substitution only for the first check against the target, not subsequent attempts.

entities.name: Moon Giant
entities.description:
Moon giants are among the largest humanoids, standing approximately 24 feet tall. Their weight varies greatly depending on the locality, as their mass increases with the number of lunar bodies orbiting their current location, though this quality never seems to affect their mobility. Moon giants are calm and even-tempered for the most part, but lunar phases and celestial occurrences influence them easily, and anyone approaching them would be wise to consult the stars first. These giants often work as oracles, receiving gifts or offerings from pilgrims in exchange for their services.

Giants are enormous humanoids of many varieties who live all across the galaxy.

Notes.Abilities:
**Gravitic Control.** The moon giant changes gravity in a 20-foot radius burst anywhere within 60 feet. Gravity in the area is treated as one step higher or lower, such as from zero gravity to low gravity, for 1 minute or until they use this ability again, whichever comes first.

**Lunar Phase.** 60 feet. The moon giant can choose waxing or waning at the start of each of their turns. When the aura is waxing, a living creature that starts its turn in the aura gains the Quickened condition and can use this extra action to only to Stride or Strike. When the aura is waning, a creature that isn't a moon giant that enters the aura must attempt a DC 33 save. This is an incapacitation effect. It's then temporarily immune to the effects of the waning aura for 24 hours.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Success** The creature becomes Stupefied 1 while in the aura.

**Failure** The creature becomes Slowed 1 and Stupefied 2 while in the aura.

**Critical Failure** As failure, and the creature falls Unconscious but can still wake up due to a successful Perception check. If it's still unconscious after 1 hour, it wakes up automatically.
Notes.Spells: Sunburst, Void Scour, Pocket Vacuum, Mind Probe, Wave of Warning, Cairn Form, Life Seal (at will), Reorient, Seek the Stars, Stumble

entities.name: Moonflower
entities.description:
These enormous plants have thick, knotted trunks festooned with fanged blossoms. A gaping mouth opens from the top of the trunk, capable of swallowing most creatures smaller than the moonflower. Moonflowers can move slowly and attack with their powerful roots, but they usually dig deeply into the surrounding ground and remain stationary to ambush prey.

Though moonflowers can't speak in the conventional sense, they communicate telepathically with other moonflowers. Those who manage to intercept a moonflower's telepathic communications are assaulted by visions of primeval jungles ruled over by titanic plant life. Whether this vision is a genetic memory or a dream of the future shared by all moonflowers is unknown.

Moonflowers first sprouted on a long-dead planet, but their proliferation throughout the galaxy has been perpetuated by both random dispersal and sinister intent. Moonflower groves thrive on Castrovel and other worlds with undisturbed wilderness.

Notes.Abilities:
**Fast Healing 10.** 

**Pod Prison.** **Trigger** The moonflower has swallowed a creature

**Effect** The swallowed creature is wrapped in a tight cocoon and extruded from the moonflower's body into an adjacent square. The creature continues to be Swallowed Whole. It can't use Acrobatics to Escape a pod, but other creatures can attempt to Rupture the pod. The cocooned creature takes half damage from any damage dealt to the cocoon. Once the cocoon is Ruptured, it deflates and decays.

**Pod Spawn.** If a Small or larger creature dies within a Pod Prison, the pod transforms into an adult moonflower with full Hit Points after 1d4 hours of growth. The newly formed moonflower has its own consciousness, but some aspect of its trunk or blossoms typically resemble the creature that died within. The dead creature's equipment remains inside the new moonflower and can be retrieved if the moonflower is slain.

**Light Pulse.** The moonflower releases a pulse of bright light. Each non-moonflower creature in a 50-foot emanation must attempt a DC 23 save. The moonflower can't use Light Pulse again for 1d4 rounds.

**Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Failure** The creature is Dazzled for 1d4 rounds.

**Critical Failure** The creature is Blinded for 1d4 rounds.

**Swallow Whole.** Large, 2d10+10 bludgeoning , 2d6 acid, Rupture 21

entities.name: Mutant Troll
entities.description:
Mutant trolls come into the Universe kicking and screaming, barely aware of their surroundings. They bite and claw at anyone who comes near, though no one knows for sure how they come into existence. They take shelter in broken-down reactors and hazardous waste dumps throughout the galaxy. Sometimes, mutant trolls puzzle together bits of tech to craft themselves a jetpack or rocket pod for propulsion to escape these sites and seek gory pleasures elsewhere.

These trolls vary greatly in appearance, but they tend to have droopy skin and hair, a side effect of their twisted regenerative powers. One of the few things mutant trolls love is to bask in the glow of a broken reactor system. They take rapturous joy in the feel of radiation washing over their skin—they speak to themselves in hushed tones about ancient kin who filled their bodies with so much radiation that they acquired primal magic powers.

Notes.Abilities:
**Regeneration 20 (deactivated by cold or electricity).** 

**Mauling Flurry.** **Frequency** once per round

**Effect** The mutant troll makes two claw Strikes against one target without increasing their multiple attack penalty. If both Strikes deal damage, the troll can attempt a jaw Strike against that target with the normal multiple attack penalty.

**Mutated Split.** **Frequency** once per day

**Effect** The mutant troll rips themself apart into two separate Large-sized entities, sharing one fractured sentience between them. While in this form, the mutant troll halves share a communal Hit Point pool and have 4 actions to share between them on their turn. If both halves are included in an area of effect, they must both attempt saving throws, taking the worse result, but only taking damage once.

**Reforming Merge.** **Requirements** The mutant troll halves are adjacent to each other

**Effect** The mutant troll halves re-form into a single entity.

**Splurting Slime.** **Requirements** The mutant troll is in its Mutated Split form, and both halves are within 30 feet of each other

**Effect** The duplicated beings spray mutated flesh and organs toward each other, absorbing most of the pieces but raining down acidic viscera on any creatures caught in the 10-foot-wide line between them. These creatures take 8d8 acid damage with a DC 27 save. The troll can't use Splurting Slime again for 1d4 rounds.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Success** The creature takes half damage.

**Failure** The creature takes full damage and is Sickened 1.

**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage and is Sickened 2.

entities.name: Necrolinked Wight
entities.description: Hollow-eyed undead born from those who died obsessing over social media, necrolinked wights wander both the living and virtual worlds, desperate for engagement and relevance. They're incapable of seeing living creatures as anything more than potential followers, hunting those who engage with technology in the hopes of turning them into obsessed fans. They constantly wail in a condensed magitech code as though screeching at some long-forgotten online debate in an attempt to grab the attention of others by overriding devices with content supernaturally configured to vie for attention. Yet as soon as their victims become necrolinked, they lose interest, driven by the same dark necrotic algorithm.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, mental, paralyzed, poison, unconscious

Notes.Abilities:
**Aligned Comm Unit.** The comm unit of a necrolinked wight can be disabled for 1 hour with a successful DC 15 check to Disable a Device or Disable a System. A necrolinked wight with a disabled comm unit is Slowed 1, gains a +6 bonus to Perception, and can't Check its Feed.

**Social Media Addiction.** The necrolinked wight is driven by a desire to continue their cycles of spiteful hatred and media consumption on the infosphere. They spend their first action of each round to Check Feed. Eternally obsessed, a necrolinked wight will always try to stay within range of an active infosphere signal. A necrolinked wight with no infosphere access or perceived threats functions as if their aligned comm unit was disabled and does whatever it can to regain infosphere access.

**Check Feed.** The necrolinked wight looks up information on their aligned comm unit about a specific creature using Computers instead of any other skill. On a success, the creature takes a –2 status penalty to its next Will save against necrotic transmission for 1 minute ( –3 status penalty on a critical success).

**Necrotic Transmission.** A creature that takes damage from a necrolinked wight's Shriek must succeed at a DC 15 save, or its subconscious is scanned and used to infect its non-augmentation tech items with a virus. Infected tech items display algorithmically generated content catering specifically to the creature's deepest desires, causing the creature to become Off-Guard as long as they're holding or wearing the tech item. On a critical failure, the creature is also Fascinated, and all creatures and objects other than the tech item are Concealed from the creature. The creature or its allies can end the effect on any specific tech item by Interacting to reboot the affected item and succeeding at a DC 15 check; on a failure, the item becomes glitching 1 (glitching 2 on a critical failure).

**Spawn Registration.** A living creature that dies while Fascinated by necrotic transmission rises as a necrolinked wight after 1d4 rounds.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, unconscious

Notes.Skills: Acrobatics +18, Computers +27, Crafting +24, Deception +24, Diplomacy +24, Occultism +27
Notes.Abilities:
**Clear Mind.** **Trigger** The necrovite is targeted by a spell with the emotion trait

**Effect** The necrovite attempts to counteract the triggering spell (counteract rank 7, counteract modifier +30). If the spell is disrupted, the necrovite gains temporary Hit Points equal to twice the rank of the counteracted spell that last for 1 minute.

**Fatiguing Presence.** 30 feet. A creature that first enters the aura must succeed at a DC 33 save or become Fatigued. Regardless of the result of the saving throw, the creature is temporarily immune to the necrovite's fatiguing presence for 24 hours.

**Void Healing.** 

**Entropic Touch.** Void damage dealt by a necrovite damages undead and creatures with void healing as if it were vitality damage. A necrovite's melee Strikes have the benefits of the ghost killer upgrade on attacks against incorporeal undead.

**Painful Mark.** When the necrovite damages a living creature with its wrackstaff, the creature must succeed at a DC 33 save or become Drained 1. Further wrackstaff damage increases the drain value by 1 on a failed save, to a maximum of Drained 4.

**Rejuvenation.** When a necrovite is destroyed, their consciousness is immediately transferred to their electroencephalon. A necrovite can be permanently destroyed only if their electroencephalon is found and destroyed.

**Scramble Psyche.** The necrovite touches an adjacent creature and scrambles its thought patterns. The creature must succeed at a DC 33 save or become Confused for 1 minute. The necrovite is considered hidden to the confused target for as long as the confusion lasts.
Notes.Spells: Mask of Terror, Dominate, Slice Reality, Telekinetic Strangulation, Shadow Blast, Subconscious Suggestion, Eldritch Wrath, Weight of Ages, Entropy Strike, Vampiric Feast, Darkness, Dispel Magic, Invisibility, Resist Energy, Analyze Target, Detect Magic, Enfeeble, Force Barrage, Message, Mind Skewer, Shield, Summon Undead, Void Warp

entities.name: Nihili
entities.description:
Dying from exposure in space is horrific, and many starship crews obsessively monitor their hull and armor integrity to avoid such a fate. It can also lead to the creation of the foul undead known as nihilis. A nihili arises after an individual in vacuum dies of asphyxiation while all gases exit their body and their lungs collapse from attempts to hold their breath. Legends say the first person to die in such a terrible manner had a vision of the goddess of undeath, Urgathoa, who bestowed upon them a single kiss, transforming them into the very first nihili. The same legends go on to claim that this nihili still floats aimlessly through space, waiting to cling to an unsuspecting starship.

The physical appearance of a given nihili varies. Most appear as zombie-like versions of their respective ancestries, but with gruesome stretch marks and pockets of bloat caused by escaping gases during their death. A nihili maintains their prior intellect, subverted entirely to inflicting the same suffering on the living that they endured. By focusing their gaze on a target, a nihili can impart to that creature the memories of their own demise, potentially suffocating them.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, unconscious

Notes.Abilities:
**Decompressing Glance.** **Trigger** A creature within 30 feet that the nihili can see starts its turn

**Effect** The target must attempt a DC 20 save. If it fails, it's Fatigued for 1 minute as it struggles to catch its breath.

**Void Healing.** 

**Decompressing Gaze.** The nihili stares at a creature they can see within 30 feet and imparts vivid visions of their prior death by decompression. A creature affected by this gaze must attempt a DC 20 save. If it fails and hasn't already been Fatigued by Decompressing Glance or this ability, it becomes fatigued. If the creature is already fatigued, a failed save causes the creature to begin suffocating until the end of the nihili's next turn. The creature remains conscious and can take actions on its turn, such as casting a spell or searching for a source of air. The creature can hold its breath as normal.

A creature can attempt a DC 20 save at the end of its turn to break free from the experience being projected into its mind; on a success, the effect of Decompressing Gaze ends. The nihili can Sustain Decompressing Gaze on their turn or end this effect as a free action. The targeted creature's access to air is restored when the nihili targets a new creature with their Decompressing Gaze or the creature successfully saves against the effects. This otherwise follows the rules for suffocation.

**Gravity Grab.** The nihili generates a field of gravity that pulls all creatures and unsecured objects toward it. Each creature within a 30-foot emanation must attempt a DC 20 save.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Success** The creature is pulled 5 feet toward the nihili.

**Failure** The creature is pulled 15 feet toward the nihili.

**Critical Failure** The creature is pulled 30 feet toward the nihili.

entities.name: Noquasar Spark
entities.description:
A noquasar spark appears as a glimmer of intensely bright light with an agonized face.

When a solarian perishes while out of sync with the cycle of stars, their soul might become entangled with their solar mote. Extreme cosmic forces act on the soul as it attempts to reach the River of Souls, stretching it infinitely thin for all of eternity.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, precision, unconscious

Notes.Abilities:
**Void Healing.** 

**Gravity Lurch.** A creature critically hit by a noquasar spark's graviton flare is knocked Prone.

**Ionized Plasma Blast.** The noquasar spark unleashes plasma in a 10-foot emanation or 30-foot line. Each creature in the area takes 2d4 fire |options:area-damage damage (DC 16 save). A creature that critically fails its save also takes 1d4 persistent,electricity |options:area-damage damage and is knocked Prone. The noquasar spark can't use Ionized Plasma Blast again for 1d4 rounds.

entities.name: Nyssholora
entities.description:
Adult nyssholoras band together in pairs only when mating and raising a newly hatched brood, during which time they consider the borders between their territory communal—they're otherwise extremely territorial.

Incredibly ferocious, nyssholoras are dinosaur-like creatures that number among the most dangerous and feared apex predators on the planet of Castrovel. These walking weapons brandish lethal biology: a massive maw lined with twin rows of razor-sharp teeth, scythe-shaped phasic blade forearms that vibrate at ultrasonic speeds, and a scourge-like tail capable of absorbing electricity from the surrounding atmosphere. Yet, nyssholoras are also cunning and perceptive—a frill of tentacles that crowns their head detect telepathic signals, making it impossible for the local formians and lashuntas to escape their notice. Their phasic blades can cut through walls and vehicles as easily as underbrush, ensuring prey have nowhere safe to hide.

Notes.Abilities:
**Telepathy Sense.** A nyssholora senses all creatures that have telepathy, limited telepathy, or a similar ability, such as a mystic's bond, as an imprecise sense at the listed range. This sense works through walls and other obstacles.

**Crunch.** **Frequency** once per round

**Requirements** A creature is Grabbed in the nyssholora's jaws

**Effect** The nyssholora chomps down on the creature, dealing 1d12+13 piercing damage.

**Discordant Bellow.** The nyssholora unleashes a blast of discordant sound that deal 12d6 sonic |options:area-damage damage in a 40-foot cone (DC 30 save). Objects and constructs in the area are treated as if they had half as much Hardness as usual. Creatures that critically fail their saving throw are also Slowed 1 for 1 round. The nyssholora can't use Discordant Bellow again for 1d4 rounds.

**Phasic Strike.** A nyssholora's phasic blade Strike treats any object or construct it hits as if the target had half as much Hardness as usual.

**Swallow Whole.** Small, 4d6+7 bludgeoning, Rupture 27

entities.name: Obrhinnshee
entities.description:
Obrhinnshees travel the Universe to expedite the return of fey souls to the First World after they die, preventing psychopomps from bringing them to the Boneyard. They believe the Eldest shouldn't allow the gods to take those they turned their backs on. In addition to this duty, the small fey seem drawn to people in need and feel compelled to render aid if they can. They're most commonly encountered in areas influenced by the First World but can be found traveling any region of space.

An obrhinnshee resembles a gnome with a shock of green, purple, or deep blue hair and glowing marks on their bodies that resemble star charts. These marks glow brighter when an obrhinnshee uses magic or whenever their hammer contains a soul. Obrhinnshees are small but strong creatures who prefer to wreathe themselves in flame and charge into battle, using their spells only if necessary.

Notes.Abilities:
**Soul Warden.** **Trigger** A willing fey or creature sworn to serve an Eldest dies within 100 feet of an obrhinnshee

**Effect** The creature's soul is drawn into the obrhinnshee's hammer to be carried home.

**Stardust.** When an obrhinnshee dies, they burst into a 10-foot aura of blinding stardust. All non-fey in the area must succeed at a DC 16 save or be Dazzled for 1 minute and Blinded for 1 round (dazzled for 1 hour and blinded for 1 minute on a critical failure).

**Deathly Nimbus.** **Frequency** once per hour

**Requirements** A soul is contained in the obrhinnshee's hammer

**Effect** The obrhinnshee wreathes themself in flame. All of the obrhinnshee's Strikes deal an additional 1d6 fire damage for 1 minute.

**Feyhammer.** In the hands of an obrhinnshee, all hammers gain a reach of 10 feet and are treated as magical weapons.

**Minor Wish.** The obrhinnshee grants a willing creature within 100 feet a +2 circumstance bonus on its next attack roll, check, or saving throw before the end of its next turn. The target becomes immune to Minor Wish for 1 minute.

**Starlight Charge.** The obrhinnshee Strides twice and makes a melee Strike. On a critical hit using this action with a feyhammer, the target is automatically shoved 10 feet away from the obrhinnshee.
Notes.Spells: Enhance Weapon, Glow Up, Prestidigitation, Reorient, Stabilize, Vitality Lash, Wisp Ally

entities.name: Observer-Class Security Robot
entities.description:
Programmed to patrol small areas, an observer-class security robot is akin to a watch dog, but with a built-in gun. Some manufacturers design these robots with canine forms, and their capability to fly can surprise would-be burglars who were expecting a more terrestrial defense.

Security robots are ubiquitous throughout industrialized space and have major presences in both the Pact Worlds and Veskarium, employed and customized by corporations and private citizens alike.

While most soldier robot models are built to be as destructive as possible, and elimination robots are designed to kill, security robots usually have fail-safes programmed into their behavior to prevent them from causing any more violence than is necessary to perform their designated security function. This makes them especially useful in cities, where unintended destruction might harm bystanders or cause legal issues, and even on starships, where a stray laser blast might cause serious damage to vital starship systems.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, doomed, drained, fatigued, healing, mental, nonlethal-attacks, paralyzed, poison, sickened, spirit, unconscious, vitality, void

Notes.Abilities:
**Exigency.** **Frequency** once every 10 minutes

**Trigger** A creature targets the security robot with an attack

**Effect** The robot overclocks its processing power to attempt to avoid an attack, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to its AC against the triggering attack.

entities.name: Oma
entities.description:
Also known as space whales, omas project powerful magical electromagnetic fields that protect them from both vacuum and toxic atmospheres while allowing them to feed. Omas gain sustenance from the particulate rings and dense atmospheres of gas giants, although exactly which substances are nutritious to an oma is still unknown. Studying a feeding oma isn't without danger. Omas sometimes accidentally swallow drones and small starships, such as fighters and interceptors, and they've been known to do so deliberately when provoked.

Most omas have been observed traveling alone. On occasion, omas form pods of three to five individuals and migrate across systems, on currents and schedules only they know. In very rare cases, omas gather among the rings of a planet in massive numbers. Their energy fields intermingle and react with local gases to light up large areas of space in a multicolored show.

Their most enigmatic yet well known feature is their starsong. Traveling through space for billions of miles, the starsong is a haunting telepathic melody. Most people perceive starsong as crooning, slow and mournful. No one can agree on the details, suggesting that each listener hears something different. Attempts to translate starsong have failed thus far, stumping even the most brilliant magic and linguistics experts. Since the Drift Crisis, for unknown reasons pods of omas have begun bombarding Drift beacons with a seemingly new starsong frequency, in some cases causing catastrophic malfunctions.

Notes.Abilities:
**Starsong.** While not a language, starsong allows omas to communicate telepathically with one another across space; omas can communicate with other omas in the same star system. Any other creature with telepathy can receive but not necessarily understand starsong at a range of 10,000 miles.

**No Breath.** 

**Cavatina.** **Frequency** once per hour

**Effect** The oma sings a telepathic song that encourages its friends and dispirits its foes within 120 feet. Each ally who can hear the song gains a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, saving throws, and skill checks for 1 minute. Each enemy must attempt a DC 35 save or be Sickened 2 (Sickened 3 on a critical failure), as the song affects their inner ear.

**Overloading Shock.** When an oma scores a critical hit with its electric discharge Strike, the target must succeed at a DC 35 save or all tech items held by the target become Glitching 2.

**Swallow Whole.** Huge, 3d8+10 bludgeoning, Rupture 37
Notes.Spells: Chain Lightning, Overload Systems, Discharge

entities.name: Omnipath
entities.description: Omnipaths are military leaders who pilot god-killing starships or command fleets of remote war machines. Omnipaths achieve their lofty positions through ambition and have few scruples, never hesitating to control other beings when it suits their schemes. Minds touched by an omnipath often lose important memories when released or, worse, glimpse shards of the omnipath's alien mindscape that linger long after the connection is severed.

Notes.Skills: Athletics +25, Deception +34, Diplomacy +32, Intimidation +34, Occultism +37, Piloting +32
Notes.Abilities:
**Nanite Mesh.** An omnipath maintains a bond with up to 20 other willing creatures. Creatures in the mesh always know the general distance and direction toward other bonded creatures, any conditions affecting them, and if they're Unconscious, dying, or dead. These creatures can communicate telepathically while on the same plane and can Recall Knowledge using the highest relevant skill modifier of any creature in the mesh. An omnipath can target any creature in its mesh with a mental spell from any distance as long as they can telepathically communicate with it, and any of these spells with the incapacitation trait lose that trait while targeting a creature in the omnipath's mesh.

**Nanite Projection.** A omnipath can share the senses and read the surface thoughts of creatures affected by their nanite mesh. A voidsage can project its mind into just one creature at a time, and choose which affected creature is the focus of its nanite projection as a single action, which has the concentrate trait. The creature also takes a –1 circumstance penalty to Will saves against any of the voidsage's spells as long as it's the focus of the voidsage's nanite projection.

**Nanite Network.** An omnipath exudes a cloud of nanites. Creatures in the aura take a –3 status penalty to saving throws against the omnipath's spells and its Merge Minds ability.

**Revert.** **Frequency** once per hour

**Trigger** The omnipath takes damage while projecting

**Effect** The omnipath stops projecting and gains 100 temporary Hit Points that last for 10 minutes.

**Merge Minds.** The omnipath forces an unwilling creature within 500 feet to join their nanite mesh. The creature attempts a DC 33 save.

**Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Failure** The creature joins the nanite mesh for 10 minutes.

**Critical Failure** The creature joins the nanite mesh for 24 hours.

**Quantum Nanites.** **Saving Throw** DC 33

**Maximum Duration** 1 day

**Stage 1** Sickened 2 (1 day)

**Stage 2** Sickened 3 (1 day)

**Stage 3** Sickened 4 and Paralyzed (1 day)

**Release the Nanites.** The omnipath severs a creature from their nanite mesh. The creature must attempt a DC 33 save. On a failure, the target is Stupefied 2 for 1 round, and the memory of any time spent while inside the nanite mesh is permanently erased; on a critical failure, the target is also Confused for 1 round.
Notes.Spells: Telekinetic Tantrum, Akashic Revival, Disappearance, Phantasmal Fleet, Interplanar Teleport, Warp Mind, Dominate, Telekinetic Strangulation, X-Ray Vision, Control Machine, Overload Systems, Eldritch Wrath, Weight of Ages, Void Whispers, Logic Bomb, Skim Data (at will), Akashic Download, Analyze Target, Delete, Implant Data, Mind Skewer

entities.name: Ordinance-Class Civil Robot
entities.description:
Ordinance-class civil robots exist to help others learn the local laws, navigate around a location, and generally remind everyone to follow the rules. What they lack in raw strength, they make up for with an extensive database of knowledge. Most of these robots are designed to mimic the shape of prevalent humanoid ancestries, and thus the standard configuration for such robots includes two arms and two legs. Some have been modified with extra attachments, providing maps produced from a rectangular opening in their chest plate or featuring touchscreens that allow passersby to consult every ordinance, law, and other legal documents relevant to the area.

Some pranksters enjoy leaving doodles and other drawings in spots the robot can't easily detect, and thus an ordinance-class civil robot that has been operating for an extensive period of time can be found with a rainbow of shapes, colors, and the occasional advertisement placed on its back.

Civil robots can be found in almost any large settlement, employed by the local government. They aren't meant to function as keepers of the peace, but instead perform minor functions, such as collecting refuse, aiding citizens with information, or collecting taxes. However, they can still defend themselves against vandals if necessary.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, doomed, drained, fatigued, healing, mental, nonlethal-attacks, paralyzed, poison, sickened, spirit, unconscious, void, vitality

Notes.Abilities:
**Exigency.** **Frequency** once every 10 minutes

**Trigger** A creature targets the robot with an attack

**Effect** The robot overclocks its processing power to dodge, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to its AC against the triggering attack.

**Photographic Recall.** After receiving a request for information about a named location or a local law from a non-hostile creature, the ordinance-class robot spends 5 minutes to consult its database, automatically succeeding at a Recall Knowledge check to answer the question. At the GM's discretion, the information might not be available to the robot.

**Scrutinize.** The ordinance-class civil robot scans all creatures in a 15-foot cone, attempting a single Legal Lore check and comparing the result to the Deception DC of each creature in the area. If the robot succeeds and the creature is known to have broken local laws, the robot gains a +1 circumstance bonus to Strikes and Athletics checks to grapple the creature for 24 hours.

entities.name: Orocoran
entities.description:
Most orocorans latch onto the shards of Aucturn that were cast through space or scattered throughout the Gelid Edge, consuming what fragments of the Newborn's womb they can and attacking anyone who happens upon them in a wild feeding frenzy. Orocorans act with especially intense and unrelenting violence toward anyone trying to harvest or relocate aucturnite.

Native to the now-destroyed planet of Aucturn, orocorans are foul and desperate creatures, cast adrift in space as they yearn to consume once more the essence of the Newborn god or fragments of the womb it gestated within. They're irritable, violent, and utterly anguished.

While some orocorans have broken free of their addiction and regained their clarity of mind and sense of self, the orocorans presented here are those who still rely on Aucturn's eldritch fluids.

Notes.Abilities:
**Hallucinate.** An orocoran's stomach fluids are laced with hallucinogens due to their consumption of the ichor-like birthing fluids expelled by Aucturn during the hatching of the Newborn.

A creature hit with the projectile vomit must succeed at a DC 24 save or be Confused for 1 round (1d4 rounds on a critical failure).

**Lick Wounds.** **Frequency** once per round

**Requirements** A creature within reach of the orocoran's proboscis is taking persistent bleed damage

**Effect** The orocoran flicks out their proboscis and sups on the flowing blood of their enemy. The orocoran regains Hit Points equal to the target's persistent bleed value.

**Spew Vomit.** The orocoran spews vomit in a 15-foot cone, dealing 3d6 acid |options:area-damage damage (DC 24 save). Creatures that fail their save are Confused for 1 round (1d4 rounds on a critical failure). This confusion is a mental effect.
Notes.Spells: Augury, Daze

entities.name: Oscriss
entities.description:
The menacing war machines known as the oscriss are found only in the ancient sites associated with the First Ones. Resembling two stacked pyramids with a white energy core of unknown composition, oscriss infuriate foes by routinely teleporting across the battlefield. Found wandering alone throughout Aballon's First One cities, the war machines were later identified in locations outside the Pact Worlds, lending credence to theories of the First Ones' expansion efforts throughout the cosmos.

The oscriss defy proper engagement, staying far away from their foes and unleashing coruscating beams of energy that slice off the limbs of those unlucky enough to engage with them. They meticulously render their foes apart at extreme range using pinpoint accuracy. If pressured into a close-range engagement, they can unleash a blast of chronal energy to slow their attackers and allow themselves the time to better reposition and continue their dismembering bombardment.

Like other constructs of the First Ones, these guardians refuse to communicate and defy almost all attempts to override or hack their programming. Some of the galaxy's finest minds have managed to temporarily overcome the intricate programming within the oscriss, though such intrusions are quickly detected and repelled, indicating that an evolving intelligence dwells within each of the strange machines.

When engaged at multiple vectors, it becomes easy to overwhelm an oscriss's detection grid and reactions. Anacite scholars propose that the constructs were fashioned to battle foes who engaged strictly in two-dimensional warfare, and while the oscriss themselves are exceptionally capable of acting in three dimensions, they battle as though their foes could engage them only in two.

It's speculated that the unique tactics and weapons employed by the oscriss are intended to deal with one specific threat: the planashars of the Planashar Dominion. The planashars hail from a different reality known as the Infinite Loop that has only two dimensions. They've recently slowly begun invading the galaxy, taking on the title of Those Who Converge and attacking Aballonian First Ones cities and the solar settlement of Noma. That the oscriss are intended to battle them only provides more evidence of some connection between the planashars and the First Ones.

Because the oscriss are accustomed to fighting beings that exist only in two-dimensional space, they're vulnerable to tactics involving three dimensions—attacking from multiple angles, for example. While an oscriss doesn't entirely understand such tactics, they can sense when they're being outmaneuvered with three-dimensional thinking and use their potent teleportation abilities to move into a less vulnerable position at every opportunity.

Notes.Skills: Acrobatics +40, Athletics +35, Computers +0, Occultism +34, Stealth +38, Survival +34
Notes.Abilities:
**Telepathy.** 300 feet

**At-Will Spells.** 

**Constant Spells.** 

**+1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic.** 

**Transposition.** **Trigger** A creature takes any move action within 15 feet of the oscriss

**Effect** The oscriss teleports into an unoccupied space within 30 feet.

**Two-Dimensional Thinking.** An oscriss is designed for fighting two-dimensional foes. If more than one enemy has the oscriss within reach, they count as flanking regardless of their actual position. An oscriss made Off-Guard by flanking foes takes a –3 circumstance penalty to AC (instead of the usual –2).

An oscriss has weakness 15 against melee attacks benefiting from flanking, and whenever a creature scores a critical hit with a melee Strike against the oscriss while flanking them, the oscriss becomes glitching 1.

If the oscriss is already glitching, they instead become Confused until the end of their next turn.

**Amputating Strikes.** When an oscriss scores a critical hit with their relativity saw or bifurcating beam Strike, the target must attempt a DC 44 save.

**Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Failure** The creature takes an additional 2d10 slashing damage.

**Critical Failure** The creature takes an additional 4d10 slashing damage and loses one limb (arm, leg, or a similar ambulatory limb such as a tentacle, randomly determined by the GM).

**Dimensional Pounce.** The oscriss Strides up to their Speed or casts translocate; at the end of that movement, the oscriss Strikes. If the oscriss began this action hidden, they remain hidden until after this ability's Strike.

**Hover.** 

**Passing Through.** The oscriss ignores all non-magical difficult terrain and greater difficult terrain.

**Pause Pulse.** The oscriss releases a pulse of temporal energy in a 30-foot burst that deals 10d8 force |options:area-damage damage to creatures in the area with a DC 44 save. The oscriss can't use Pause Pulse again for 1d4 rounds.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Success** The creature takes half damage and is Slowed 1.

**Failure** The creature takes full damage and is slowed 1 for 1 minute.

**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage and is slowed 1 for 1 minute and Stunned 2.

**Secondary Target.** **Frequency** once per round;

**Effect** The designates a creature within 100 feet to be the secondary target of their attacks until the end of the oscriss's next turn.

Whenever the oscriss makes a Strike against a different creature, they can make the same Strike against their secondary target as a free action, using the same multiple attack penalty as the attack against the initial target. The initial and secondary Strikes count as one attack for the purposes of increasing the oscriss's multiple attack penalty.

**Whirling Assault.** The oscriss Strikes with their relativity saw six times.
Notes.Spells: Event Horizon, Slice Reality, Slice Reality (At Will), Truesight (Constant), Translocate (At Will)

entities.name: Othinni
entities.description:
Along Embroi's perilous seas, residents speak in hushed tones of the othinni. Considered by some to be a myth, the enormous, squid-like aberrations supposedly bear sinister glowing runes suggestive of an infernal lineage. Those dragged into the deep by their writhing tentacles and swallowed by their gaping maws are said to go straight to Hell, their final screams fueling the legends.

The myths are true. Othinni possess a cruel intelligence and dominating influence over the minds of mortals. Survivors suffer disturbing visions, intense feelings of fear and confusion, and visions of unholy fire burning atop the waves. Hearing the insidious psychic screech of an othinni or sailing into their massive shadow is a frightful experience for anyone braving the oceans of Embroi.

Angels and their allies hunt othinni with massive holy harpoons and enchanted silver nets. One legendary hunt is recorded in the documentary film Umiqon (produced by Zo! Media), which is named for the 40-foot tall monster brought down by four Knights of Iomedae.

Notes.Abilities:
**+2 Status Bonus Vs Magical Effects.** 

**Abyssal Ink.** 20 feet. The othinni is constantly surrounded by a cloud of poisonous black ink. Any creature that enters the aura or begins its turn inside the aura must attempt a DC 32 save or becomes Sickened 2 for 1 minute (Sickened 3 on a critical failure).

**Infernal Origin.** **Trigger** The othinni is targeted by a magical effect with the holy trait

**Effect** The othinni's infernal runes flare to life, attempting to counteract the effect (counteract rank 7, counteract modifier +26).

**Greater Constrict.** 3d6+12 fire, DC 32

**Infernal Binding.** The othinni binds a creature within 100 feet with diabolic runes, and the target must attempt a DC 32 save. On a failure, the target is Immobilized for 1 round. On a critical failure, the creature is immobilized for 1 minute but can attempt a new saving throw at the start of each of its turns to end the effect.

**Psychic Screech.** The othinni unleashes a mental wail in a 30-foot emanation. All creatures in this area must attempt a DC 32 save.

**Critical Success** No effect.

**Success** The creature becomes Frightened 1.

**Failure** The creature becomes Frightened 2 and Confused for as long as it's frightened.

**Critical Failure** As failure, but Frightened 3.
Notes.Spells: Diabolic Pact (DC 36)

entities.name: Pachinyam Swarm
entities.description:
Pachinyam swarms can release a cloud of billowing dust as individual rodents constantly reapply dust to their comrades.

These dusty, long-eared fluffy burrowing rodents are native to Daimalko and emerged alongside the colossi during the Awakening 200 years ago. They were initially heralded as potential pets and affectionately referred to as "dust bunnies," but the survivors of the Awakening soon found the species were as dangerous as the colossi rampaging across the planet.

While one or two pachinyams behave as calm herbivores, they reproduce rapidly. When the pachinyam population reaches a tipping point, they become vicious predators. Their dust's ability to disrupt both visual and telecommunications makes it challenging for settlements to warn or organize against them. Outside civilization, the pachinyam population is kept in check by their swarms' instinctually drive to be near colossi despite the obvious danger. Some also hypothesize that the scent of a pachinyam swarm's dust cloud attracts hungry colossi.

Notes.Abilities:
**Dust.** 30 feet. The pachinyam swarm shakes it thick fur and releases a cloud of dust and dander in a 30-foot radius burst centered on a corner of one of its squares that functions as a mist spell. This dust cloud blocks electronic communication to and from anyone inside the cloud. Any item with the tech trait becomes Glitching 1 if it's inside the dust cloud.

**Swarming Bites.** Each enemy in the swarm's space takes 2d8 piercing damage (DC 20 save). Creatures that fail this save are Sickened 1 (Sickened 2 on a critical failure). While within a pachinyam's dust cloud and sickened, the creature is also suppressed until it leaves the cloud or recovers from the sickened condition.

entities.name: Pachinyam
entities.description:
A single pachinyam isn't much of a threat but can be a nuisance around those who rely on technology. Some pachinyam owners take extra time to play with their pets after their daily dust baths, especially before entering a starship or other facility where an unexpected cloud of dust could have catastrophic consequences.

These dusty, long-eared fluffy burrowing rodents are native to Daimalko and emerged alongside the colossi during the Awakening 200 years ago. They were initially heralded as potential pets and affectionately referred to as "dust bunnies," but the survivors of the Awakening soon found the species were as dangerous as the colossi rampaging across the planet.

While one or two pachinyams behave as calm herbivores, they reproduce rapidly. When the pachinyam population reaches a tipping point, they become vicious predators. Their dust's ability to disrupt both visual and telecommunications makes it challenging for settlements to warn or organize against them. Outside civilization, the pachinyam population is kept in check by their swarms' instinctually drive to be near colossi despite the obvious danger. Some also hypothesize that the scent of a pachinyam swarm's dust cloud attracts hungry colossi.

Notes.Abilities: **Dusting.** The pachinyam shakes it thick fur and releases a cloud of dust and dander in a 5-foot burst radius centered on a corner of one of its squares that functions as a mist spell. This dust cloud blocks electronic communication to and from anyone inside the cloud. Any item with the tech trait becomes Glitching 1 if it's inside the dust cloud. The pachinyam can't use this ability again until they take a dust bath as a 3-action activity with the move trait.

entities.name: Paradox 17
entities.description:
As Paradox 17 is normally invisible, most recorded observations of it start with hearing a roar "like static from a dead signal." All reports mention a profound yet hard-to-place sense of meaningfulness. One survivor saw it illuminated by a blast of light she described as "a spiral galaxy made up of shining eyes and glass feathers." Another described it as "dozens of interleaved wings scattered with embers." The only thing consistent about Paradox 17, however, is how deadly it can be if confronted directly.

Can you ever really know that the Universe you perceive exists? That you'll never awaken one day to find it was all a dream? A planet full of philosophers sought the answers to these questions once upon a time… shortly before they all vanished en masse. They left behind confusing records stating that the light of a "whirling star" revealed that physical matter had no substance and the Universe was secretly a mental prison. These records are all that remain from the first known encounter with the being known as Paradox 17.

Notes.Abilities:
**Causational Moments.** **Frequency** once per round

**Trigger** A creature would trigger Paradox 17's Reactive Strike, but it has no reactions remaining

**Effect** Paradox 17 Steps or Strikes prior to resolving the triggering action.

**Reject Reality.** 100 feet. When a creature in the aura observes Paradox 17 for the first time each day, it must attempt a DC 42 save or Performance check. On a failure, reality rejects the creature for as long as it can observe Paradox 17. The affected creature becomes hidden from all other creatures (except Paradox 17) as though invisible itself.

**Bridge of Perception.** **Requirements** Another creature is observing Paradox 17 or has triggered interdict definition in the last hour

**Effect** Paradox 17 teleports to any location that both Paradox 17 and the required creature can observe across any distance, even to another galaxy or plane.

**Disregard Reality.** Paradox 17 can move through all creatures, objects, and structures as though they were incorporeal.

**Interdict Definition.** Paradox 17 automatically and instantly learns and can observe the exact location of any creature on any plane that succeeds at a Recall Knowledge check to learn any information about Paradox 17 or any creature who communicates information about Paradox 17 in any way. The ability to observe the creature and its surroundings, wherever the creature goes, lasts 1 hour.

**Natural Invisibility.** Paradox 17 is naturally invisible. It becomes visible only when using a hostile action.

**Waking Light.** Paradox 17 burns away the fabric of reality with intense sunlight. If no creatures are observing Paradox 17, the light fills a 60-foot cone. If any creature is observing Paradox 17, the area is a 60-foot line. Creatures and unattended objects in the area turn temporarily translucent. Creatures in the area take 24d6 fire |options:area-damage damage and must attempt a DC 45 save. Paradox 17 can't use Waking Light again for 1d4 rounds.

**Critical Success** The target takes no damage.

**Success** The target takes half damage becomes Doomed 1.

**Failure** The target takes full damage and becomes Doomed 2.

**Critical Failure** The target takes double damage and becomes Doomed 3.
Notes.Spells: Event Horizon, Indestructibility, Implosion, Slice Reality, Truespeech (constant), Wave of Warning

entities.name: Paradoxical Solipsist
entities.description:
On six recorded occasions, individuals having prolonged contact with Paradox 17 continued to display anomalous behavior afterward. Two expressed belief they were dreaming, four that they were in a hostile simulation. One of these latter individuals insisted on "finding the light again" during an interview before walking through their guards and the holding cell wall, and they haven't been seen since.

Can you ever really know that the Universe you perceive exists? That you'll never awaken one day to find it was all a dream? A planet full of philosophers sought the answers to these questions once upon a time… shortly before they all vanished en masse. They left behind confusing records stating that the light of a "whirling star" revealed that physical matter had no substance and the Universe was secretly a mental prison. These records are all that remain from the first known encounter with the being known as Paradox 17.

Notes.Skills: Acrobatics +17, Computers +18, Deception +16, Occultism +18, Stealth +20, Thievery +20
Notes.Abilities:
**Elude Consequences.** **Trigger** The solipsist succeeds at a Will save, or an attack against them is a critical failure

**Effect** The solipsist teleports up to 25 feet in any direction of their choice. Creatures adjacent to the solipsist after they teleport are Off-Guard to them until the end of the solipsist's next turn.

**Perceive Unreality.** The solipsist treats all creatures, objects, and structures they're observing (except for Paradox 17) as quasi-illusory, allowing the solipsist to move through them as though the solipsist were incorporeal. They can also choose to use Will for any saving throw against any non-damaging effect.

**Area Fire (Flash Grenade).** **Flash Grenade** (10-foot burst, range 70 feet, tracking +1)

**Effect** Dazzled for 2 rounds on failure (DC 26 save)

**Baffling Attack.** The solipsist deals an additional 2d6 precision damage to Off-Guard creatures, and on the first successful melee Strike they make against an off-guard creature each turn, the target must succeed at a DC 28 save or be Stunned 1 and Blinded while stunned.
Notes.Spells: Subjective Reality, Suggestion, Translocate, Calm, Vibe Check, Wisp Ally

entities.name: Plasma Ooze
entities.description:
Plasma oozes pose a significant menace to seasoned spacefarers within the Pact Worlds. These entities materialize as expansive networks of crackling electromagnetic energy, assuming a captivating spherical form pulsating with luminous hues of purple and blue, with searing white-hot bursts scattered throughout.

These oozes primarily lurk near the surface of stars but are also drawn to potent electromagnetic phenomena elsewhere in the Universe. The electromagnetic fields exuded by the ooze present dangers in space, potentially even incapacitating shielded starships. Armed scions connected to the Plane of Fire, known as the Sunkillers, claim to actively hunt these enigmatic beings, armed with specialized gear and sonic weaponry.

Oozes of many types lurk in dark and abandoned places across the galaxy, emerging only to satiate their appetites and threaten adventurers, explorers, and hapless workers alike.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, critical-hits, electricity, fire, precision, unconscious, visual

Notes.Abilities:
**Thoughtsense.** The plasma ooze can sense all non-mindless creatures within the listed range.

**Electromagnetic Field.** 100 feet. When an item with the tech trait is activated inside the aura, it must succeed at a DC 36 save or become Glitching 1 (Glitching 2 on a critical failure).

A tech creature that starts its turn within the aura must attempt a DC 35 save. If it fails, it becomes Glitching 1 (Glitching 2 on a critical failure).

An item or creature that succeeds at this save becomes immune to this aura for 1 hour.

**Magnetic Draw.** Large and smaller creatures and all unattended objects within 100 feet must succeed at a DC 36 save or be pulled 15 feet toward the plasma ooze (30 feet on a critical failure).

**Plasma Drain.** **Frequency** once per day

**Effect** each creature and wielded object with the tech trait within 100 feet of the plasma ooze must attempt a DC 36 save. For each target that fails this save, the ooze regains 15 healing Hit Points and the object loses half of its remaining charges (if battery-powered).

**Plasma Slag.** A creature damaged by the ooze's pseudopod must succeed at a DC 36 save or be Slowed 1 (Slowed 2 on a critical failure). A creature with the tech trait uses the outcome one degree of success worse than the result of its roll.

entities.name: Plasmazer
entities.description:
Plasmazers are air elementals of vivid colors and grumpy disposition who became commonly found in the Universe after the invention of neon lighting. They manifest as dangerous explosions of light and color that shut down city grids, redirecting the power into a strobing neon kaleidoscope. They often take the shape of legendary birds or other creatures from local myths. Experimental club owners have tried harnessing plasmazers to produce special effects for their dance parties, but such situations usually end with dancers dodging plasma beams. The plasma slide is the name of a line dance that went viral after a plasmazer broke free at the Neon Crypt, an all-hours club on Eox with a reputation for rowdy fetes.

Elementals are energetic intrusions from the primal planes of existence. They take many forms, from mindless eddies in the wind or water to complex entities capable of wielding primal magic.
