A mortal who demonstrates the right attitude and abilities, such as by protecting a stellar body from destruction or creating an especially beautiful work of art, might draw a space nymph's attention. From time to time, space nymphs will offer their services as mentors to solarians or mystics, though they seldom seek pupils on their own. Space nymphs rarely enter into more than one such arrangement at a time and typically only make commitments that promise to last decades or centuries, so they're extremely selective in their choice of mentee.

Notes.Abilities:
**Sense Transponder.** While on their bonded celestial body, a nymph can sense approaching starships within a day's travel from the celestial body. This doesn't give them any information about the ship, its occupants, or its exact position. The nymph can send a message to the ship as if using a personal comm unit.

**Asteroid-Dependent.** A sterieid is mystically bonded to a small asteroid, no more than 1 mile across. If they're away from their bonded asteroid for more than 24 hours, they become Drained 1 and must succeed at a DC 21 save each additional 24 hours or increase their drained value by 1. A sterieid can perform a 24-hour ritual to bond themself to a new asteroid.

**Debris Field.** **Trigger** The sterieid takes physical damage

**Effect** Shards of rocky debris fly off the sterieid's body, dealing 2d12 bludgeoning damage to all adjacent creatures (DC 21 save) and giving the sterieid the Concealed condition until the end of their next turn.

**Icy Nimbus.** 10 feet. A sterieid's body radiates an icy chill. Creatures entering or starting their turns in the aura take 2d6 cold damage (DC 21 save); a creature that critically fails its save is also Clumsy 1 until the start of its next turn as it grows sluggish from the cold.
Notes.Spells: Speak with Stones, Cairn Form, One with Stone, Resist Energy, Sure Footing, Glow Up, Pummeling Rubble, Scan Environment, Seek the Stars

entities.name: Supenga Pup
entities.description:
Supengas reproduce by fruiting, a process that can take months in a harsh desert environment. Pups often spend years learning to survive before they are ready to strike out on their own—or are kicked out.

When rains grow sparse in this succulent's native habitat, it turns to another source for liquid: blood. The supenga has adapted to a world of scarcity and takes advantage of any chance to hunt using its sharp leaves and paralyzing toxin.

Notes.Abilities:
**Slowing Enzyme.** **Saving Throw** DC 20

**Maximum Duration** 6 rounds

**Stage 1** –10-foot status penalty to all Speeds (1 round)

**Stage 2** –10-foot status penalty to all Speeds and Slowed 1 (2 rounds)

**Stage 3** –20-foot status penalty to all Speeds and Slowed 2 (1 round)

**Spinning Charge.** The supenga pup curls into a ball and launches itself forward. It Strides up to twice its Speed in a straight line. If it ends this movement adjacent to an enemy, it bashes into that enemy, dealing 3d8+3 bludgeoning damage (DC 22 save). A creature that critically fails this save is knocked Prone.

entities.name: Supenga Titan
entities.description:
These toxic titans can drain a living creature's blood in moments.

When rains grow sparse in this succulent's native habitat, it turns to another source for liquid: blood. The supenga has adapted to a world of scarcity and takes advantage of any chance to hunt using its sharp leaves and paralyzing toxin.

Notes.Abilities:
**Siphon Blood.** **Requirements** A Grabbed, Paralyzed, Restrained, or Unconscious living creature is within the supenga titan's reach

**Effect** The supenga titan absorbs the creature's blood with its spines. This requires an  check against the creature's Fortitude DC if the creature is grabbed but is otherwise automatic. The creature becomes Drained 1, and the supenga titan regains 21 healing Hit Points.

**Slowing Enzyme.** **Saving Throw** DC 36

**Maximum Duration** 6 rounds

**Stage 1** –10-foot status penalty to all Speeds (1 round)

**Stage 2** –10-foot status penalty to all Speeds and Slowed 1 (2 rounds)

**Stage 3** –20-foot status penalty to all Speeds and Slowed 2 (1 round)

**Spine Volley.** The supenga titan makes up to four spine Strikes, each against a different target. The supenga titan's multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after it makes all the attacks.

**Swallow Whole.** Large, 3d6+9 bludgeoning ,4d8 acid plus slowing enzyme, Rupture 35

entities.name: Surnoch
entities.description:
Surnochs inhabit lifeless asteroids and small moons throughout the cosmos. A surnoch's mouth is deep, funnel-like, and lined with numerous rows of sharp, pointed teeth, which allow it to grind matter down as it chews and melts its way through rock and stone. Surnochs have an innate sense of which minerals their bodies require most and can find these minerals even through miles of rocks. Surnochs excrete condensed forms of these minerals, leaving tunnels full of strange alloys and gem-quality materials in their wake.

When multiple surnochs gather together, their appetites synchronize, causing them to hunt for specific minerals en masse. The worms rain destruction on whole regions until their need is sated, then suddenly turn on each other in a show of dominance.

"Space worm" is a nonscientific term for a xenobiologically complex clade of invertebrate animals and beasts that make their home in the vastness of space. Some, like the diaspora and dust worms, show signs of intelligence and are directly related to each other. Others, like the surnoch, evolved separately, with their origins completely unknown to science.

Notes.Abilities:
**Reactive Strike.** 

**Corrosive Spines.** With impressive control, the surnoch can launch its spines in a tight grouping over a great distance. All creatures in a 30-foot line take 8d8 piercing |options:area-damage damage with a DC 25 save. On a failure, the creature also takes 1d8 persistent,acid |options:area-damage damage (or 2d8 persistent,acid |options:area-damage damage on a critical failure). The surnoch can't use Corrosive Spines again for 1d4 rounds.

**Surnoch's Kiss.** **Saving Throw** DC 25

**Maximum Duration** 6 rounds

**Stage 1** 1d6 poison damage and Sickened 1 (1 round)

**Stage 2** 1d6 poison damage and Sickened 2 (1 round)

**Stage 3** 1d6 poison damage and Sickened 3 (1 round)

**Tail Smash.** The surnoch's tail smash has a burst centered on a corner of its space. It's excluded from the burst.

**Tunneling Expert.** Surnochs have adapted to move swiftly underground. When burrowing, a surnoch worm leaves a tunnel behind itself. When moving through a previously created surnoch tunnel, it gains a +10-foot status bonus to its Speed.

entities.name: Szynegator Swarm
entities.description:
A single szynegator vibrating causes slight vertigo, but when these tiny beetle-like components harmonize, the atmospheric disruption they generate renders most forms of communication inoperable. Szynegators can usually be found in isolated or desolate areas of planets so their number can grow unimpeded. Their presence harbingers a full Swarm invasion.

Developing far out in the Vast from an insectile species known as kucharns, the Swarm is considered the greatest threat in existence for several cultures. Composed of countless subcolonies, each consisting of myriad component subspecies, the Swarm is a vast host that acts in psychic union for the purpose of consuming all matter across the cosmos. Most frightening of all is the Swarm's ability to assimilate the knowledge and DNA of those they consume. Thanks to its pre-Gap development of star travel, the Swarm had already consumed innumerable systems before history short-circuited, and the Swarm's pace only accelerated once it received access to the Signal and the hyperspace dimension known as the Drift.

Worlds touched by the Swarm are drained of their natural resources and rendered barren places known as huskworlds. What outsiders consider to be "Swarm space" is little more than a swathe of lifeless worlds that the Swarm have consumed in its reckless advance. The Swarm so thoroughly strips these worlds that surveyors struggle to find even trace amounts of inorganic resources, such as rare minerals and water. Few of these huskworlds have been thoroughly explored, as oftentimes exploration awakens inert drones, theorized to have been left behind in case the devoured system was ever colonized and repopulated. Pockets of Swarm activity exist well beyond this region of space, as the Swarm sent out countless subcolonies in the ages before the Gap, and even now, only some of them have reached their intended destinations.

The Swarm is perhaps most known in the current era for two important facts. First, its assault on the Pact Worlds and the Veskarium led to the cessation of hostilities and tenuous alliance between the two powers. Second, the Swarm is the direct ancestor of the shirren species. Having broken away sometime during the Gap, shirrens found succor with the deity Hylax, who was believed to have evolved from a pre-Swarm kucharn and who turned her back on the ravenous entity the Swarm has evolved into.

In recent years, the Swarm had been seen as little more than a distant boogeyman with no activities save for classified actions in the Suskillon system in the Vast. However, the recent discovery of the missing Szandite world of Krethiskar inadvertently awoke a dormant subcolony that had been responsible for the world's consumption. Since then, the newly dubbed Krethiskar subcolony has become a scourge of Near Space, engaged in an active invasion of Szandite Collective worlds and poised to spill over into other powers like the Veskarium and Pact Worlds. This rediscovered subcolony has begun rapid evolution of its components and remains cut off from the wider Swarm, but it still represents a clear danger to Near Space.

Notes.Abilities:
**Motion Sense.** An szynegator swarm can sense nearby creatures through vibrations in air or water caused by movement as an imprecise sense at the listed range.

**Colony Mind.** 30 feet. All allies with colony mind within the listed range of each other are in constant telepathic communication and are aware of all threats any individual knows about. While within range of at least one ally with colony mind, when a creature rolls a success on a save against a mental effect, it gets a critical success instead.

**Comm Occlusion.** 40 feet. All electronic and telepathic communication, except for that with the colony mind ability, ceases to function, and affected creatures take a –2 circumstance penalty to Perception checks. When three or more szynegator swarms are aware of each other using colony mind, the range of comm occlusion increases to 100 feet. This range increases to planetary when 10 or more szynegator swarms are aware of each other using colony mind.

**Sonic Distortion.** Each enemy in the szynegator swarm's space takes 1d8 sonic damage (DC 18 save).

entities.name: Tashtari Alpha
entities.description: Native to the green world of Castrovel, the tashtari has become known throughout the wider galaxy as the laser wolf. Wolflike pack hunters, tashtaris have a layer of flexible filaments that emit phosphorescent lights and allow them to silently communicate through a bespoke visual language. Each tashtari possesses a node within their throat that allows them to channel their stored solar energy and unleash a beam of focused light, giving them their moniker of laser wolves. A mating pair, consisting of one or two alphas, leads packs of tashtaris, who generally become the apex predators of large areas with one or more forested regions. The presence of trees is important for the nocturnal tashtaris, who sleep on the treetops during the day to bask in sunlight and recharge their solar energies.

Notes.Abilities:
**Bristle Flash.** The tashtari causes their filaments to glow with intense light. Non-tashtari creatures within a 40-foot emanation must attempt a DC 21 save. A creature that attempts this save is immune to all Bristle Flashes for 1 minute. The tashtari's fur then dims, and they can't use this ability until they bask in sunlight for at least 10 minutes.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Success** The creature is Dazzled for 1 round.

**Failure** The creature is dazzled for 1 minute.

**Critical Failure** The creature is Blinded for 1 round and dazzled for 1 minute.

**Solar Cry.** The tashtari alpha unleashes a searing, rainbow muzzle beam that soars into the sky before splitting into countless rays of multicolored light that crash down in every direction. Each non-tashtari creature in a 20-foot emanation takes 4d6 fire |options:area-damage damage (DC 19 save). On a critical failure, a creature that can see the tashtari alpha is also Dazzled for 1 minute. Other tashtaris in the area recharge their Bristle Flash. The tashtari alpha's glowing heart dims, and they can't use this ability until they bask in sunlight for at least 1 hour.

entities.name: Tax-Class Civil Robot
entities.description:
Robotic tax collectors are used to track down debtors with outstanding payments and harass them into paying what they owe. AbadarCorp was the first such entity to utilize the technology and owns, operates, and rents a majority of the tax-class civil robots in the Pact Worlds to this day. AbadarCorp takes a portion of the payment and monitors their robots to make sure the transaction is legal, adding to the perceived legitimacy of these devices and shame of being followed by one in public. The robots will usually leave once given a small portion of the payment, often enough to pay any late fees, fines, and the cost of using the robot just to remind the debtor of their obligations; they're often treated as a minor but embarrassing nuisance and paid to leave without any trouble. Robots repurposed by loan sharks are often accompanied by other agents and programmed to collect payment in full.

Civil robots can be found in almost any large settlement, employed by the local government. They aren't meant to function as keepers of the peace, but instead perform minor functions, such as collecting refuse, aiding citizens with information, or collecting taxes. However, they can still defend themselves against vandals if necessary.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, doomed, drained, fatigued, healing, mental, nonlethal-attacks, paralyzed, poison, sickened, spirit, unconscious, vitality, void

Notes.Skills: Athletics +6, Computers +4, Diplomacy +3, Intimidation +5, Society +5, Survival +5, Thievery +3
Notes.Abilities:
**Reactive Disarm.** **Trigger** A creature within the robot's reach attempts a melee or ranged Strike against the tax-class civil robot with a held weapon

**Effect** The robot uses its gasping hook to attempt to disarm the triggering creature's weapon with a +1 circumstance bonus to its check.

**Tax Collector.** A tax-class civil robot can be placated by paying the fees, fines, or taxes it seeks to collect by offering the robot a credstick with an Interact action. If the robot takes a target's equipment (see repossession), it will count half the equipment's value toward the total tax owed. A creature can attempt a 3-action activity to fool the robot by Hacking it using a hacking toolkit and succeeding at a DC 18 or Accounting Lore check. Programmed to accept many forms of payment, the robot takes a –2 penalty to AC and saving throws against actions that use a Computers check, such as the Combat Hack skill feat.

**Repossession.** When a tax-class civil robot succeeds at a check to steal or critically succeeds at a check to disarm an item, it immediately picks up the item (if necessary) and stows it in a lockbox in the robot's frame. The robot can open the lockbox with a single Interact action without difficulty, but others must Pick the Lock (DC 18); a creature that attempts to do so while the tax-class civil robot is aware takes a –4 circumstance penalty to the check.

Notes.Skills: Acrobatics +28, Arcana +26, Athletics +25, Computers +26, Deception +23, Intimidation +23, Occultism +26, Piloting +28, Religion +26, Society +26, Stealth +28, Thievery +28
Notes.Abilities:
**Change Shape.** A temporai can take the appearance of any Small, Medium, or Large humanoid. This doesn't change their Speed or their attack and damage modifiers with their Strikes, but it might change the damage type their Strikes deal.

**Multidexterous.** A temporai can Switch Hands as a free action.

**Out of Time.** The temporai turns their gaze to a single target within 120 feet, forcing upon it all the fragments of time it has shed. The target takes 12d8 mental damage and must attempt a DC 34 save. Regardless of the result, the target then becomes temporarily immune to Out of Time for 1 day.

**Critical Success** The target takes no damage.

**Success** The target takes half damage and becomes Clumsy 1, Drained 1, and Enfeebled 1, or increases these conditions by 1.

**Failure** As success, but full damage and the conditions' value is 2.

**Critical Failure** As success, but double damage and the conditions' value is 3.

**Sands of Time.** With a flick of their wrist, the temporai disperses a wave of time-altering sand, dealing 15d6 spirit |options:area-damage damage to all creatures in a 60-foot cone (DC 34 save). Creatures that fail their save are additionally slowed for 1d4 rounds. The temporai can't use Sands of Time again for 1d4 rounds.

**Sense Fate.** A temporai always rolls a 20 for initiative

**Shepherd's Touch.** An erabryth's Strikes have the benefit of a ghost killer upgrade and deal an extra 5d6 void damage to living creatures or 5d6 vitality damage to undead.
Notes.Spells: Contingency, Retrocognition, True Target, Call Spirit, Truespeech (constant), Read Omens, Talking Corpse, Translocate, Haste, Slow, Augury, Blur, Dispel Magic, See the Unseen, See the Unseen (constant), Detect Magic, Divine Lance, Injury Echo, Shield

entities.name: Tergaiator
entities.description:
Amid space's asteroid belts and atop their rocky exteriors rest the homes of these massive, competition-loving elementals. Tergaiators augment their bodies with pieces of asteroid as they wrestle and jump around. They thrive off the nutrients within asteroids and fight to protect their homes from being excessively farmed by greedy mining ventures.

Elementals are energetic intrusions from the primal planes of existence. They take many forms, from mindless eddies in the wind or water to complex entities capable of wielding primal magic. The advent of space travel and the progress of technology have allowed even more living embodiments of the elements to manifest in the Universe.

Natural events like wildfires, solar storms, and floods can unleash hordes of unruly elementals on a planet or into a region of space. Sometimes, a gathering of powerful elementals causes a natural disaster on an epic scale, like an off-the-charts solar flare that fries a planet's power grid or a ceaseless storm swirling in a gas giant's atmosphere.

Notes.Abilities:
**Reactive Strike.** 

**Meteoric Death Drop.** **Frequency** once per day

**Requirements** The tergaiator has a creature Grabbed

**Effect** The tergaiator launches themself and their victim high up in the air before crashing down. The creature takes 5d8 bludgeoning damage and 1d6 fire damage with a DC 30 save. On a failure, the creature also falls Prone in an unoccupied adjacent square of the tergaiator's choice; on a critical failure, the creature is also Stunned 1. After using Meteoric Death Drop, reduce the tergaiator's size by one category, their reach by 5 feet, and their Strike damage by 2 for 1 day.

**Orbital Lariat.** **Frequency** once per minute

**Effect** The tergaiator hurtles toward their foes, using the momentum to launch a spinning flurry of attacks with outstretched arms. They Stride and make a melee Strike against any number of creatures within reach at the end of their movement. Each Strike applies to the tergaiator's multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after they make all of their attacks. After making these attacks, the tergaiator is also Clumsy 1 until the start of their next turn.

entities.name: Terror of Ukulam
entities.description:
When a massive ooze-like being emerged from the polluted caverns of Castrovel's industrial moon, Elindrae, the planet's leaders made the mistake of assuming the ooze posed no threat to Castrovel itself. When the ooze destroyed several of the moon's shipyards, then launched itself through space to the remote reaches of Ukulam, they made the mistake of assuming they had time to quarantine the threat in that continent's remote wilderness. When its radiation began to spread, and long-dead elindrian cultists rose from their nest-necropolises beneath the Singing Range to worship the ooze, the planet's leaders finally understood they couldn't ignore it. They called it the Terror of Ukulam. They still don't understand quite what it is, why it exists, or what it wants.

The Terror is an enormous ooze-like thing, somewhat resembling layered flaps of oily dark green flesh. It conceals its only anatomical feature—a large purple eye—beneath its undulating surface. The creature spends most of its time floating in deep subterranean caverns or ocean trenches, remaining immobile for days at a time, then suddenly traversing a great distance, almost always in a straight line, before stopping again. These stops are seemingly random, but they've displaced settlements with increasing regularity. The vengeful worshippers who follow the Terror's path are almost as dangerous as the radiation it spreads, though their reasons for following it are as inscrutable as the Terror itself.

Thanks to the nature of atomic energy and especially atomic weapons, Castrovel's scientists have deduced that the radioactive Terror is likely to cause as much destruction in death as it has caused in life—or perhaps more. Even if the combined military might of Castrovel and its allies was sufficient to defeat the Terror, these scientists have warned that they need more time to study the Terror and assess the risks of destroying it outright. Of course, every day that passes is another day that more elindrians flock to the Terror, and yet more victims cross its destructive path.

Stats.Immunities: controlled, critical-hits, disease, emotion, mental, paralyzed, poison, precision, sleep

Notes.Skills: Acrobatics +31, Athletics +42, Intimidation +36, Nature +38, Stealth +31, Survival +42
Notes.Abilities:
**Voice of Linked Minds.** The Terror doesn't speak, but it can psychically communicate complex concepts with any creature within 200 feet that is part of a hive mind, husk mind, or similar shared mind. Other creatures that can communicate telepathically can somewhat understand the Terror, but their understanding is vague.

**Regeneration 25 (deactivated by fire).** 

**+1 to all saves vs. primal.** 

**Ancient Bond.** The Terror commands obedience from creatures on Castrovel, suggesting an ancient connection to the planet. Wild creatures native to Castrovel or its moon must succeed at a DC 45 saving throw when they first come within 200 feet of it on a given day; on a failure, they improve their attitude toward the Terror to friendly. Creatures that become friendly typically approach the Terror, resulting in a painful death by radiation sickness.

**Radioactive Death.** When the Terror of Ukulam dies, it explodes in a radioactive blast that instantly vaporizes all creatures and objects within 30 miles and deals 45d12 fire damage to all creatures, objects, and structures in a 150-mile-radius emanation with a DC 45 save. Creatures in the area are also exposed to terrible radiation sickness. The terrain and any bodies of water (or suitable portions of larger bodies, such as oceans, at the GM's discretion) become terribly radioactive for a minimum of 50 years, after which time they slowly become less radioactive, using less severe degrees of radiation from GM Core at the GM's discretion.

**Terribly Radioactive.** 120 feet. The Terror spreads radiation everywhere it goes. Non-creature plants near the Terror quickly wither and die. Any creature that begins its turn within the aura is Sickened 3 and is exposed to terrible radiation sickness each round.

**Induce Frenzy.** **Frequency** once per day

**Effect** The Terror stirs creatures in hive minds into a frenzy. Each creature within 200 feet that's part of a hive mind gains the Quickened condition for 1 minute, and it can use the extra action each round only to Stride or Strike.

**Terrible Radiation Sickness.** This radiation causes unimaginably painful burns, unrelenting nausea, and death

**Saving Throw** DC 45

**Onset** 1 hour

**Stage 1** 13d6 poison damage and Sickened 1 (1 hour)

**Stage 2** 14d6 poison damage and Sickened 2 (1 hour)

**Stage 3** 15d6 poison damage and Sickened 3 (1 hour)

**Stage 4** death

**Toxic Touch.** Creatures struck by the Terror's sludge tendril gain weakness 10 to poison and take a –2 status penalty to Fortitude saves for 1 round.

**Undulating Wrath.** The Terror Strikes with its sludge tendrils six times.

**Vorpal Eye Beam.** The Terror pulls back a lid of oozy "skin" to reveal its only anatomical feature—an enormous dark purple eye—firing an invisible particle beam along the path of its gaze. The beam is 10 feet wide and 120 feet long. Creatures in the area take 18d8 slashing damage (DC 45 save). Creatures that critically fail their save are instantly decapitated. This kills any creature except ones that don't require a head to live. For creatures with multiple heads, this usually kills the creature only if its last head is severed. The Terror can't use Vorpal Eye Beam again for 1d4 rounds. During this time, it loses immunity to critical hits and precision damage.
Notes.Spells: Cataclysm, Indestructibility, Atomic Blast, Unfettered Movement (constant)

entities.name: Thasteron Khefak
entities.description:
When khefaks consume thasteron, they take on a crystalline appearance and grow into territorial, ravenous threats.

Khefak Biogenetics bioengineered khefaks to consume scrap thasteron so the waste could be refined into starship fuel. These creatures eventually became a prime example of a solution becoming a problem of its own. After the discovery of Drift travel, Akiton's thasteron market plummeted, removing the need for mining infrastructure, including khefaks. Khefak Biogenetics destroyed the production facilities, thinking they'd completely eradicated their creations. Khefaks are hardy, however, and the few survivors left the facilities. Beyond thasteron, they subsisted on inorganic materials, and their rapid reproduction rate allowed them to quickly spread all over Akiton. Some stowed away on starships, allowing them to spread throughout the Pact Worlds.

Notes.Abilities:
**Gnaw Scrap.** A khefak chews on an unattended object to feed, dealing 4 piercing damage every 10 minutes to the object. This damage ignores 10 points of Hardness. If a khefak doesn't spend at least 1 hour Gnawing Scrap per day, it begins to starve until it spends 10 minutes Gnawing Scrap.

**Thasteron Radiation.** 10 feet. A thasteron khefak gives off an aura of mild radiation. A creature who starts its turn in the aura must succeed at a DC 20 save or take 1d6 poison damage and become Sickened 1.

entities.name: Thermatrod Caldera
entities.description:
Under certain electromagnetic conditions, two or more thermatrods might eject their molten cores into a shared magma chamber. The conjoined material forms a caldera, a mighty beast with starmetal veins running through its plates.

Originally thought to be exiles from the Plane of Fire, thermatrods actually developed independently in multiple star systems in the Universe. A thermatrod resembles a molten bipedal creature, though they often walk on their front knuckles to support their heavy frames. Thermatrods sport distinctive raised dorsal plates that resemble hexagonal basalt columns, which researchers use to estimate an individual's age. A thermatrod's hardened exterior varies greatly based on local mineral deposits that make up a thermatrod's diet.

Notes.Abilities:
**Temperature Sense.** A thermatrod caldera can detect nearby changes in temperature as a precise sense to detect living creatures and other heat sources.

**Melting Aura.** 15 feet. A creature that begins its turn within this aura takes 4d6 fire damage (DC 26 save).

**Slag Barrage.** The thermatrod sprays part of its molten core in a 15-foot cone that hardens moments later. Each creature in the area takes 11d6 fire |options:area-damage damage (DC 29 save). A creature that fails the save is also Immobilized (escape dc=29). The thermatrod can't use Slag Barrage again for 1d4 rounds.

entities.name: Thermatrod
entities.description:
A standard thermatrod dwells near volcanic vents and other sources of intense heat.

A creature that fails the save is also Immobilized (escape dc=20). The thermatrod can't use Slag Barrage again for 1d4 rounds.

entities.name: Thresher Lord
entities.description:
