However, the recent discovery of the missing Szandite world of Krethiskar inadvertently awoke a dormant subcolony that had been responsible for the world's consumption. Since then, the newly dubbed Krethiskar subcolony has become a scourge of Near Space, engaged in an active invasion of Szandite Collective worlds and poised to spill over into other powers like the Veskarium and Pact Worlds. This rediscovered subcolony has begun rapid evolution of its components and remains cut off from the wider Swarm, but it still represents a clear danger to Near Space.

Notes.Abilities:
**Motion Sense.** A thresher lord can sense nearby creatures through vibrations in air or water caused by movement as an imprecise sense at the listed range.

**Colony Mind.** 30 feet. All allies with colony mind within the listed range of each other are in constant telepathic communication and are aware of all threats any individual knows about. While within range of at least one ally with colony mind, when a creature rolls a success on a save against a mental effect, it gets a critical success instead.

**Deflecting Blades.** **Trigger** A creature adjacent to the thresher lord targets the thresher lord with a melee attack

**Effect** The thresher lord gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack.

**Blade Storm.** The thresher lord makes three arm blade Strikes. Each Strike uses the thresher lord's current multiple attack penalty, but each Strike takes a –2 penalty. This counts as three attacks when calculating its multiple attack penalty.

**Hurtle.** **Frequency** three times per day

**Effect** The thresher lord Strides up to three times its Speed in a straight line.

**Serrated Blades.** On a critical hit with an arm blade Strike, the thresher lord inflicts 1d8 persistent,bleed damage to its target.

entities.name: Tool Rat
entities.description:
The tool rat resembles an infant of their kind, but closer study reveals coppery whiskers akin to a dwarven beard and eyebrows. Intuitive spellcraft helps them turn junkyards into minefields for the unwary

When pileups of metal garbage begin to conquer the wilderness, rodents conquer the garbage. Scrap rats adapt to every civilization that disposes their ruined gadgets and industrial debris, all of which the rats recycle and reuse to potentially deadly effect. While not especially intelligent, they have an innate knack for crafting.

Notes.Abilities:
**Scoring.** When the tool rat's tail Strike deals damage to an object or creature with the tech trait, the tail also gains the following traits until the beginning of the scrap rat's next turn: deadly d4, hampering, and razing.

Effect: Scoring

**Upscaled Recycling.** Over the course of 1 hour of uninterrupted work, a tool rat can assemble a simple tactical weapon of any type, up to 2nd level, including a single commercial battery or a full magazine of projectile ammunition. using nothing but junk. It falls apart and becomes unusable junk after 10 minutes.
Notes.Spells: Inject Nanobots, Instant Virus, Electric Arc, Mending, Recharge Weapon, Stumble, Supercharge Weapon

entities.name: Trained Squox
entities.description:
The tiny vulkarikis are a common animal in the Pact Worlds, originating from the planet Castrovel. Human explorers from Lost Golarion gave them the name "squox," as they interpreted the creatures as being a mix of fox and squirrel. Squoxes are cunning to the point of being devious and employ scare tactics to routinely abscond with shiny items they uncover on their travels. They exhibit complex social behaviors, including a distinct hierarchy between individuals in a skulk, and have a vast vocal repertoire used to assign signature sounds to different individual squoxes.

Having long since been exported from the Pact Worlds, squoxes are found throughout the galaxy, with many civilizations in Near Space maintaining growing communities of these tiny furry creatures, much to the growing consternation of the Xenowardens who worry that the highly adaptable squox has become an invasive species in several biomes. While some advocate for culling these populations, the popularity of the animal as a pet has made this view an incredibly unpopular stance.

Young squoxes are referred to as kits and can be purchased from the open market on most Pact Worlds. Squoxes tend to live for about 10 years. A typical squox weighs about 10 pounds and is about 3 feet long, with much of its length being its tail. Squoxes come in all colorations, and many even take on unique environmental adaptations to specific climates, such as desert-dwelling squoxes growing longer ears to help disperse heat.

Notes.Abilities:
**Go for the Eyes!.** The squox Strides, attempts an  check against an adjacent creature's Perception DC, and then makes a jaws Strike.

**Critical Success** Thrown by the squox's sudden leap, the target is Off-Guard until the end of the squox's next turn.

**Success** The target is only momentarily startled and is off-guard until the end of the squox's current turn.

**Critical Failure** The squox misjudges the distance to its target's face and falls Prone.

**Squox Tricks.** A squox can disarm skill=acrobatics and trip skill=acrobatics creatures with its tail using Acrobatics instead of Athletics, even if it doesn't have a free hand. A squox can attempt to Disarm or Trip Off-Guard creatures up to two sizes larger than it and gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Disarm or Trip an off-guard target

entities.name: Trawler
entities.description:
Experienced explorers of Castrovel know to monitor the sky, lest they be caught unaware by a diaphanous trawler. A trawler can spin a filament with sticky coating that has a mild anesthetic effect, allowing them to stalk at a distance and then pull their prey in close, all while comfortably airborne.

It's extremely rare for an adult trawler to land or alight on anything voluntarily. Usually, they maintain at least a minimal air gap between themself and any object. If forced to be on the ground, a trawler can use their tentacles to clumsily ambulate, though more often than not, they'll launch themself into the air given the first opportunity.

Notes.Abilities:
**Transparency.** Unless they've fed recently, the trawler is naturally fully transparent, allowing them to hide without concealment or cover and granting them a +4 circumstance bonus to Stealth checks to Hide. A trawler loses this transparency if they take a hostile action of any kind.

**Reel In.** **Requirements** The trawler has a Medium or smaller creature Grabbed with its lasso filament

**Effect** The trawler pulls the creature toward themself. They attempt an Athletics check against the target's Fortitude DC. A trawler can lift a creature off the ground in this way.

**Critical Success** The target is moved 20 feet closer to the trawler.

**Success** The target is moved 10 feet closer to the trawler.

**Critical Failure** The trawler releases the target.

**Sticky Filaments.** A creature hit by the trawler's lasso filament becomes Grabbed by the trawler. The creature isn't Immobilized, but it can't move beyond the range of the lasso filament. A creature is Clumsy 1 for as long as it's grabbed by a lasso filament. A creature can sever the filament with a Strike against AC 19 that deals at least 6 fire or slashing damage. This deals no damage to the trawler but destroys the filament. A trawler has three lasso filaments, and they can't use their lasso filament Strike if all three are destroyed. It takes a week for the trawler to regrow all three of their filaments.

**Trawler Venom.** **Saving Throw** DC 20

**Maximum Duration** 6 rounds

**Stage 1** 1d4 poison damage and Enfeebled 1 (1 round)

**Stage 2** 1d6 poison damage and Enfeebled 2 (1 round)

**Stage 3** 2d4 poison damage, enfeebled 2, and Sickened 1 (1 round)

**Stage 4** 2d6 poison damage, enfeebled 2, and Sickened 2 (1 round)

entities.name: Tregalxi
entities.description:
Tregalxis generally look like a knotted bundle of electrical wiring. Their true form is a shifting ball of radioactive energy safely nestled within their wired shell. Tregalxis need a near-constant source of power to safely maintain their radiation. They're most often found parasitically integrated into a ship's wiring, secretly siphoning power or wedged into a reactor. They leech power from the chosen source until they become either satiated or bored enough to seek out a new power source.

Theoretically, a wayward tregalxi could find their way into a large ship's power core, a city power grid, or the control center for a satellite, where they would most certainly cause power outages and malfunctions, all while becoming incrementally more powerful and destructive.

Elementals are energetic intrusions from the primal planes of existence. They take many forms, from mindless eddies in the wind or water to complex entities capable of wielding primal magic. The advent of space travel and the progress of technology have allowed even more living embodiments of the elements to manifest in the Universe.

Natural events like wildfires, solar storms, and floods can unleash hordes of unruly elementals on a planet or into a region of space. Sometimes, a gathering of powerful elementals causes a natural disaster on an epic scale, like an off-the-charts solar flare that fries a planet's power grid or a ceaseless storm swirling in a gas giant's atmosphere.

Notes.Abilities:
**Wire Sense.** A tregalxi can sense the presence of electrical wires within 30 feet as an imprecise sense.

**Insulated Shell.** When a tregalxi is reduced to less than half their Hit Points, their insulated wire shell breaks, freeing their contained radiation. All electricity damage dealt by the tregalxi instead becomes poison damage. When a creature takes poison damage from a tregalxi, it becomes Sickened 1 for 1 minute with no way to reduce the condition.

**Circuit Splice.** The tregalxi extends their wire frame to all enemies within 30 feet. Each creature takes 2d6 piercing and 2d6 electricity damage (DC 20 save). The tregalxi can't use Circuit Splice again for 1d4 rounds.

**Short Circuit.** When a creature makes direct contact with a tregalxi's wires, the creature takes 1d6 electricity damage with a DC 20 save.

entities.name: Typodaemon
entities.description:
These child-sized daemons represent the horrors of death through dictation errors, transcription woes, or incorrect copying and pasting of text. Typodaemons make discreet adjustments to text, changing a word, adding a taunting emote, or adjusting punctuation to create entirely new meanings for written words. These changes lead to conflicts, and the typodaemon thrives on the strife and potential for death because of these simple errors.

Hailing from the plane of Abaddon, daemons are utterly devoted to the destruction of all life. Their existence is based around specific means of death, and they seek the death of all things in service to their lords: the Apocalypse Riders. Each daemon represents a different way to die, and they use their specific powers to further that means of death.

Advents in technology have only created new means of death and torment, so new types of daemons enter existence with regularity, each created once a sufficient mass of new deaths occurs to spawn them. These new advent daemons often prefer to spend their time in the galaxy rather than Abaddon, as they can better spread their torments to the mortals of creation.

Notes.Abilities:
**Telepathy.** 100 feet

**Input Overload Aura.** 20 feet. Enemies in the aura take a –1 status penalty to AC and all saves against sonic effects or effects that alter written or stored data. A creature within this aura attempting to read a document must succeed at a DC 5 or cannot read the document for the next 1d4+1 rounds.

**Pedant Annoyance.** Typodaemons paradoxically despise having their errors pointed out. If a creature Interacts to correct the grammar or syntax of something the typodaemon has written or is writing, including with a spell such as implant data, the typodaemon becomes Sickened 1. While sickened this way, the daemon must spend an action to justify its actions instead of retching, attempting a  save instead to remove the condition.

**Error Injection.** The typodaemon remotely accesses the code of a visible item with the tech trait within 60 feet and injects erroneous data. The item becomes Glitching 2; if the item is in possession of a creature, the creature must attempt a DC 18 save, negating the effect on a success. The item is then immune to Error Injection for 1 hour.
Notes.Spells: Speak with Computers, Instant Virus, Skim Data, Delete (At Will), Implant Data, Measure, Scan Environment

entities.name: Ulgaazan Nyssholora
entities.description:
The largest nyssholora ever recorded was Ulgaaza the Ageless, a mythical creature so old and so massive it was said to dwarf mountains. Today, any nyssholora that reaches epic proportions is called "Ulgaazan," though even these mighty beasts pale in comparison to their namesake.

Incredibly ferocious, nyssholoras are dinosaur-like creatures that number among the most dangerous and feared apex predators on the planet of Castrovel. These walking weapons brandish lethal biology: a massive maw lined with twin rows of razor-sharp teeth, scythe-shaped phasic blade forearms that vibrate at ultrasonic speeds, and a scourge-like tail capable of absorbing electricity from the surrounding atmosphere. Yet, nyssholoras are also cunning and perceptive—a frill of tentacles that crowns their head detect telepathic signals, making it impossible for the local formians and lashuntas to escape their notice. Their phasic blades can cut through walls and vehicles as easily as underbrush, ensuring prey have nowhere safe to hide.

Notes.Abilities:
**Telepathy Sense.** A nyssholora senses all creatures that have telepathy, limited telepathy, or a similar ability, such as a mystic's bond, as an imprecise sense at the listed range. This sense works through walls and other obstacles.

**Sonic Snarl.** **Trigger** A creature fails or critically fails a melee Strike against the nyssholora

**Effect** The nyssholora snarls at the triggering creature, dealing 3d6+6 sonic damage.

**Crunch.** **Frequency** once per round

**Requirements** A creature is Grabbed in the nyssholora's jaws

**Effect** The nyssholora chomps down on the creature, dealing 2d12+16 piercing damage.

**Discordant Bellow.** The nyssholora unleashes a blast of discordant sound that deal 18d6 sonic |options:area-damage damage in a 60-foot cone (DC 38 save). Objects and constructs in the area are treated as if they had half as much Hardness as usual. Creatures that critically fail their saving throw are also Slowed 1 for 1 round. The nyssholora can't use Discordant Bellow again for 1d4 rounds.

**Phasic Flurry.** The nyssholora Strides up to its Speed then makes a phasic blade Strike against each creature within reach. Each attack counts toward the nyssholora's multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until after all the attacks.

**Phasic Strike.** A nyssholora's phasic blade Strike treats any object or construct it hits as if the target had half as much Hardness as usual.

**Swallow Whole.** Medium, 4d8+8 bludgeoning, Rupture 35

entities.name: Vanguard-Class Soldier Robot
entities.description:
Vanguard-class soldier robots are hulking machines of battle. They often have four clawed hands, digitigrade legs, a long tail, and a featureless, diamond-shaped head. Their back-mounted plasma launcher and burst-duration jump jets give them a hunched, predatory appearance, augmented by top-of-the-line weapons. Each is 8 feet tall and weighs 700 pounds.

Though their striking image has captured media attention, the vanguard-class soldier robot is too expensive to mass-produce on the scale of an army, and so they are used as special forces, vanguards, bodyguards, and even field commanders for all-robotic forces. A lack of large-scale feasibility is, admittedly, poor comfort to any soul within seeker warhead range.

Living soldiers are a liability. They have families who don't want them to die, need salaries, have morale, require discipline, commit atrocities, and have opinions on the war. They're a necessary, but unfortunate, part of warfare for any society without an abiding love for necromancy.

Cutting-edge soldier robots promise to solve this problem. Soldier robots have no loved ones, opinions, self-preservation instinct, or tendency toward random atrocities. Many companies market their soldier robots as a humane solution to modern combat.

In practice, they're anything but.

Without lives on the line, soldier robots encourage their owners to engage more often and more violently. Standoffs turn into skirmishes, skirmishes into battles, and inevitably the innocent are caught up in the mix. They're particularly popular with corporations and non-governmental organizations that appreciate being able to throw a dozen soldier robots at any naysayer, public critic, or explorer they dislike while being able to deny true responsibility for what happens.

Though there's constant public fear of soldier robots going rogue, it has yet to prove a serious concern. If a soldier robot wants you dead, it's because someone doesn't mind if it kills you.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, doomed, drained, fatigued, healing, mental, nonlethal-attacks, paralyzed, poison, sickened, spirit, unconscious, vitality, void

Notes.Abilities:
**Assault Jump.** The vanguard-class soldier robot Leaps to a space it can see within 60 feet. All creatures within 5 feet of where the robot lands must succeed at a DC 33 save or be knocked Prone. The robot then makes a painglaive Strike against one creature within reach. The robot can't use Assault Jump again for 1d4 rounds.

**Linked Senses (60 feet).** The vanguard-class soldier robot shares senses with other allied vanguard-class soldier robots within 60 feet.

**Seeker Warhead.** **Frequency** once per day

**Effect** The vanguard-class soldier robot fires a plasma warhead at an intersection within 200 feet it can see. All creatures in a 15-foot burst take 8d12 fire |options:area-damage damage (DC 33 save). On a failure, a creature is also Dazzled and Deafened for 1 minute. The area in which the warhead exploded becomes difficult terrain.

**X-Ray Vision (60 feet).** The vanguard-class soldier robot can see through most materials and walls within 60 feet. Its sight is blocked by 2 feet of wood or plastic, 1 foot of stone, 2 inches of metal, or any amount of lead or starmetal, and it can see only in black and white.

entities.name: Veolisk
entities.description:
Veolisks, formidable creatures from remote planets within the Vast, are reminiscent of prehistoric megafauna, despite their relatively smaller size. These lumbering quadrupeds, characterized by their reptilian features and bony exoskeletons, evoke the mystery and fear often associated with ancient colossal creatures. The reason for their seclusion becomes apparent as most xenobiologists posit that the creature's gaze, capable of inducing mental distress in other species, renders habitation near veolisk territory a daunting challenge. Encounters with veolisks near established communities lead to ruthless hunts.

The creatures, with their signature Void Gaze ability, have sparked speculation about their lineage. Some theories propose that veolisks descended from ancestors with more potent gaze attacks, earning them the moniker "void basilisks" among those versed in Lost Golarion's ancient folklore. An intriguing hypothesis suggests that millennia ago, destruction-loving cultists of the Devourer might have selectively bred the first veolisks, a narrative predating the Gap

Despite their fearsome reputation, veolisks find utility as guardians for Devourer cult bases and even as pets to individuals embracing the chaos of the universe. Interestingly, veolisks are docile and harmless when equipped with blinders, veils, or other means to nullify their gaze—a quirk rarely explored in cross-cultural attempts at domestication.

Surviving on minimal sustenance, veolisks consume a single meal daily, feeding on flesh, fruits, fungus, or any available plant life. The physiological systems of veolisks remain a subject of study among scientists. Theories range from hyperefficient metabolisms to feeding on cosmic radiation, akin to trees photosynthesizing sunlight. A fringe notion suggests veolisks might subsist solely on background arcane energies pervasive throughout the galaxy, challenging the boundaries of scientific understanding.

Notes.Abilities:
**Void Glance.** **Trigger** A creature within 30 feet that the veolisk can see starts its turn

**Effect** The target must attempt a DC 24 save. If it fails, it's Off-Guard until the end of the veolisk's next turn from distracting thoughts of the emptiness of space.

**Null Bite.** The veolisk makes a jaws Strike against a Confused creature, which gains the deadly d10 trait. If the target attempts the flat check to recover from its confusion when it takes damage from this Strike, it rolls twice and takes the lower result.

**Void Gaze.** The veolisk's eyes exude the dark, claustrophobic aspects of deep space. A creature the veolisk can see within 30 feet must attempt a DC 24 save. If it fails, it becomes Off-Guard until the end of the veolisk's next turn. On a critical failure, or on a failure if the creature was already off-guard from this ability or Void Glance, the creature instead becomes Confused until the end of the veolisk's next turn.

entities.name: Void Ooze
entities.description:
A scourge to spacefarers across the galaxy and beyond, void oozes slip into the Universe from the Netherworld. These creatures float through space in eternal hibernation until they land on a planetoid or spaceship, awoken by the subtle signs of life. Entire colonies can form overnight from a single ooze lucky enough to find a battlefield, consuming the deceased and wounded in no man's land before spreading to consume the camps of war-weary soldiers.

Oozes of many types lurk in dark and abandoned places across the galaxy, emerging only to satiate their appetites and threaten adventurers, explorers, and hapless workers alike.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, critical-hits, mental, precision, unconscious, visual, void

Notes.Abilities:
**Vitality Siphon.** 20 feet. A creature attempting to restore Hit Points with a magical effect to one or more creatures inside the aura must succeed at a DC 25 save for each target or else the magic heals the void ooze instead. If a creature gains the dying condition while inside the aura, the ooze regains 10 healing Hit Points.

**Numb Senses.** A living creature hit by a void ooze's pseudopod Strike must succeed at a DC 25 save or become Dazzled and Deafened until the end of the creature's next turn (Blinded and deafened on a critical failure).

This numbs all of the creature's perceptive senses (such as smell, taste, and touch), applying the dazzled and blinded conditions' effects to other precise senses the creature might have.

**Shades Linger.** The void ooze unleashes a pulse of magical darkness in a 30-foot emanation. Nonmagical light is automatically extinguished for 1 minute. The ooze also attempts to counteract any 3rd-rank or lower magical light effect in this area (counteract rank 3, counteract modifier +17).

entities.name: Void Palm
entities.description:
A void palm poses a danger to sentient creatures and their antigravity technology alike. The plant propagates slowly yet steadily by catapulting an annual yield of brilliant blue seeds spaceward. The imparted momentum provides sufficient velocity for most seeds, aided by their supernatural ability to ignore gravity, to escape into the depths of space. Each seed drifts unremittingly until it encounters an object suitable for sustaining it, whether a wandering asteroid, planetary body, or sizable starship.

Once embedded in a fitting surface, a void palm seed germinates rapidly. Upon sprouting, the plant begins drawing nutrients from its surroundings, which periodically become enriched by the decomposing corpses or the oxidizing scraps of the plant's victims. The plant's fronds routinely sweep its area clear of remains or other debris that could serve as handholds or counterbalance or that could alert potential prey to their peril.

Notes.Abilities:
**Antigrav Interference.** 120 feet. The void palm causes antigravitational technology to malfunction. Upon entering this aura, any items or objects with the tech trait that employ some form of antigrav tech, including antigrav harnesses as well as most hover vehicles and starships, become glitching 1.

**Disorienting Patterns.** **Trigger** A creature with darkvision within 60 feet of the void palm begins its turn

**Requirements** The void palm is in darkness

**Effect** The patterns on a void palm's mottled red fronds resemble a distant star field when viewed in the darkness. The void palm sways its fronds in a disorienting manner. The triggering creature must attempt a DC 25 save.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected and becomes immune to Disorienting Patterns for 24 hours.

**Success** The creature is Dazzled until the end of the void palm's next turn.

**Failure** As success, and the creature is also Off-Guard to the void palm's melee Strikes while it's dazzled.

**Critical Failure** As failure, and the creature is also Stupefied 1 for 1 minute

**Double Lash.** The void palm makes two sweeping frond Strikes against the same target, each using its current multiple attack penalty. If both attacks hit, combine their damage. This counts as two attacks when calculating the void palm's multiple attack penalty.

**Gravity Void.** **Frequency** once per day

**Effect** The void palm creates a zero-gravity area of darkness in a 20-foot emanation, negating the effects of gravity and non-magical light sources in the area. Magical light sources in the area work normally. The void palm is unaffected by this lack of gravity, but other creatures that enter or start their turn in the area become untethered unless they can move normally in zero-gravity environments; they're also Clumsy 1 and Off-Guard while untethered in the area. An untethered creature attempting to Push Off in the area must succeed at a DC 5 or the action is disrupted. The Gravity Void lasts for 10 minutes.

entities.name: Void Zombie
entities.description:
When an akata bites a humanoid, it infests them with microscopic, parasitic larvae. Those who perish from this parasitization, a condition known as void death, rise again as void zombies. While they resemble a typical rotting corpse, an elongated bluish-gray feeding tendril extends from their shattered lower jaw. When the immature akata within the body senses potential prey, this tendril often undulates and writhes with nauseating eagerness.

Once the host body dies, the larvae feed on each other until the strongest makes its way to the victim's brain. After several hours of rapid gestation, it attaches to the brain and infuses it with a mote of necromantic energy. This process leaves the larva ravenous, driving it to consume the blood of living creatures. Void zombies tend to last several weeks as the larva grows, but eventually its host compels it to seek out a safe, secluded place where it can disgorge the larva for one last surge of growth before the host body goes inert. Several hours later, a fully formed akata emerges from the frothing puddle, typically consuming the corpse as its first meal.

In general, akatas leave void zombies alone, and the larval parasites attempt to spread out to avoid competing for food. In a confined and undisturbed space, void zombies stand completely still to conserve energy. The juvenile akatas within become dormant and feed on the host body's tissue until they either reach maturity or sense a viable food source. Given the void zombie's relatively short existence, those who stumble upon a previous attack might find the void zombies already devoured or discarded and an eerie colony of silent, glassy cocoons full of ravenous hibernating akatas instead.

Void zombies tend to ignore other undead, but they become inexplicably aggressive when confronted with other creatures that are infested by parasites or otherwise controlled or influenced by external forces. Many have tried experimenting with void zombie behavior by forcing them to confront, for example, a rendworm host or a creature under the thrall of a spellcaster. Most such experiments end inconclusively at best, and many have ended in disaster.

Notes.Abilities:
**Salt Water Vulnerability.** Salt water quickly attacks a larval akata's cells as a strong acid. If the void zombie is fully immersed in salt water, it takes 4d6 acid damage from the water immediately and at the end of each of its turns as long as it remains immersed. Its weakness to salt water applies to this damage. On any round in which the void zombie takes damage due to its salt water weakness, the larval akata withdraws to hide within the host's body and renders the void zombie Slowed 1.

**Void Healing.** 

**Feed on Blood.** **Requirements** The void zombie's previous action was a successful feeding tendril Strike against a living creature

**Effect** The void zombie drains blood from the required creature using its feeding tendril. The void zombie regains 4 healing Hit Points, and the creature is Drained 1 until it receives healing of any kind or amount.

entities.name: Voidsage
entities.description: Voidsages are alghollthus who survived the battles of youth with an intact nanite network. After consuming many of their peers' own nanites, a voidsage's network grows strong enough to control a remote war machine.

Notes.Skills: Athletics +15, Deception +17, Intimidation +15, Occultism +19, Piloting +20, Society +17, Stealth +18
Notes.Abilities:
**Nanite Projection.** A voidsage can share the senses and read the surface thoughts of creatures affected by their quantum nanites. A voidsage can project its mind into just one creature at a time, and choose which affected creature is the focus of its nanite projection as a single action, which has the concentrate trait. The creature also takes a –1 circumstance penalty to Will saves against any of the voidsage's spells as long as it's the focus of the voidsage's nanite projection.

**Nanite Network.** 5 feet. A voidsage exudes a cloud of nanites. A creature entering the aura or starting its turn in the aura is exposed to quantum nanites.

**Revert.** **Frequency** once per hour

**Trigger** The voidsage takes damage while projecting

**Effect** The voidsage stops projecting and gains 50 temporary Hit Points that last for 10 minutes.

**Quantum Nanites.** **Saving Throw** DC 24

**Maximum Duration** 1 day

**Stage 1** Sickened 2 (1 day)

**Stage 2** Sickened 3 (1 day)

**Stage 3** Sickened 4 and Paralyzed (1 day)
Notes.Spells: Eldritch Wrath, Hypnotize (at will), Mind Reading (at will), Void Whispers, Logic Bomb, Skim Data (at will), Akashic Download, Analyze Target, Delete (at will), Eldritch Lance, Implant Data, Mind Skewer

entities.name: Vorthuul
entities.description: Vorthuuls are undead beings with two overlapping yet incongruous forms: a distorted spirit shrieking in unending torment and a pitch-black skeleton overflowing with serenity. One form might seem more real than the other, only for the opposite to be true the next moment.

Stats.Immunities: bleed, death-effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, unconscious

Notes.Abilities:
**Crushing Gravity.** 5 feet. A vorthuul is surrounded by the crushing gravitational forces of a black hole. A creature that enters or begins its turn in the aura takes 3d6 bludgeoning damage (DC 26 save).

**Event Horizon.** A vorthuul naturally draws in light. The DC of the flat check to target a vorthuul Concealed or hidden due to dim light or darkness is reduced by 2. A vorthuul takes a –2 circumstance penalty to AC and saving throws against light effects and to AC against attacks from weapons in the laser group.

**Quantum Duality.** Vorthuuls exist in two states: one in perfect tranquility, the other in perpetual agony. The vorthuul gains bonuses depending on the dominant state. They decide which is dominant as a free action when they roll initiative.

- **Absolute Tranquility** The vorthuul gains a +1 status bonus to saves against emotion effects and resistance 10 to mental damage.
- **Everburning Agony** The vorthuul gains a +1 status bonus to saves against vitality effects and resistance 10 to fire damage.

**Reactive Strike.** 

**Void Healing.** 

**Gravity Maelstrom.** **Frequency** once per hour

**Effect** The vorthuul intensifies their gravitational pull for 1 minute, increasing the radius of their crushing gravity aura to 20 feet. Additionally, while this aura is expanded, creatures moving in any direction other than directly toward the vorthuul treat squares in the aura as difficult terrain.

**Quantum Agony.** **Frequency** once per round

**Requirements** The vorthuul is in absolute tranquility state

**Effect** The vorthuul enters everburning agony in torrents of anguish. Each creature in the vorthuul's crushing gravity aura must succeed at a DC 28 save or be Sickened 1 (or Sickened 2 on a critical failure).

**Quantum Tranquility.** **Frequency** once per round

**Requirements** The vorthuul is in everburning agony state

**Effect** The vorthuul enters absolute tranquility in a wave of oppressive stillness. Each creature in the vorthuul's crushing gravity aura must succeed at a DC 28 save or be Slowed 1 for 1 round (or slowed 1 for 3 rounds on a critical failure).

**Singularity Pocket.** The vorthuul forces their physical and psychological torment upon a creature they touch. The target must succeed at a DC 28 save or become Immobilized for 1 minute (escape dc=28). As long as it's immobilized in this way, it takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage and 1d6 mental damage at the end of each of its turns. Creatures that Escape become temporarily immune to this vorthuul's Singularity Pocket for 24 hours.

entities.name: Vracinea
entities.description: The vracinea is a large, shambling, multi-mawed plant, originally native to Castrovel but now found on many more planets. Slow and clumsy, it prefers to lure animals and other protein-rich prey with its blossoms. It then seeks to make a quick kill while the prey is befuddled by its spores. Though the paralytic effect of a vracinea's spores isn't potent at great distances, when these spores catch the wind, they help the plant spread to new habitats. A vracinea is a particularly cunning and territorial hunter that knows how to use local hazards. It's skilled at hiding its body in the underbrush, extending just its blossoms to lure in prey.

Notes.Abilities:
**Invasive Spores.** 10 feet. A vracinea constantly exudes sweet-smelling spores. Any creature that enters or starts its turn in the area must attempt a DC 18 save.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected and immune to the vracinea's aura for 24 hours.

**Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Failure** The creature is Clumsy 1 and Enfeebled 1 for 1 round.

**Critical Failure** As success, plus the creature is Paralyzed for 1 round.

**Blossom Lure.** The vracinea's violet blossoms emit a magical glow that compels all onlookers to approach. Each non-vracinea creature within a 120-foot emanation must attempt a DC 21 save to avoid the lure. The effect lasts for 1 round, but the vracinea can Sustain this ability on subsequent rounds, extending the duration by 1 round for all affected creatures. Once a creature succeeds at any save against Blossom Lure, that creature is temporarily immune to Blossom Lure for 24 hours.

**Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Failure** The creature must spend each of its actions to move closer to the vracinea as expediently as possible while avoiding obvious dangers. If a lured creature is adjacent to the vracinea, it stays still and doesn't act. If a lured creature takes damage from any source or is targeted by an enemy with an attack or hostile effect, the creature is freed from this effect at the end of the current turn.

**Critical Failure** As failure, but if damaged, attacked, or targeted, the creature attempts a new save at the start of its next turn, rather than being automatically freed at the end of the current turn.

**Feeding Frenzy.** The vracinea makes up to three jaws Strikes, each against a different target. These attacks count against the vracinea's multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after the vracinea makes all its attacks.

entities.name: Wahtunshna
entities.description:
Wahtunshnas are brokers, business negotiators, and war profiteers. They operate in the cities of Malfane and the watery planet Embroi and, increasingly, attend meetings with corporate legal teams in Near Space. Trained in negotiation, business administration, and the corporate buzzwords of a hundred cultures, wahtunshnas offer a competitive advantage to corporations while building a reputation of their own. The knowledge and industrial power of Hell are tempting to many companies looking to get an edge over their competitors, and wahtunshnas are more than happy to assist. In exchange for the incorporation of spyware into their products and Diabolic clauses in their terms of service, corporations gain access to the intellectual property of Hell, passing on infernal bloatware to their customers. Rumors claim that wahtunshnas contribute to the constant churn of start-ups whenever possible, sabotaging any companies that seek to break or circumvent the terms of their diabolical agreements.

In the shadows of space stations, halls of courtrooms, and offices of corporations, devils tempt mortals with promises of power and lay the groundwork for their conquest. A devil's pacts can vary from elaborate contracts to quick promises, but they all end the same way: a mortal soul condemned, and Hell's forces bolstered. From the open rule of Malfane, the unseen control of Embroi, and hidden pacts with souls across the galaxy, devils continue their relentless work to spread tyranny and force the universe to resemble the hellish bureaucracy of their home.

Notes.Skills: Computers +10, Deception +13, Diplomacy +12, Intimidation +12, Religion +10, Society +12
Notes.Abilities:
**Infernal Tracking.** For as long as a creature is taking persistent bleed damage from the wahtunshna's claw Strike, that creature can't be Concealed from, Hidden from, or Undetected by the wahtunshna.

**Planned Obsolescence.** The devil points at an item with the tech trait that they can see within 60 feet, forcing a firmware update so it becomes Glitching 3. A creature about to use the item can spend an Interact action to read through the item's new terms of service to remove this condition.
Notes.Spells: Void Whispers, Detect Thoughts, Doom Scroll, Sift the Sphere, Bane, Diabolic Pact, Eldritch Lance, Guidance, Message, Mind Skewer, Mind Skewer, Protection

entities.name: Warp Troll
entities.description:
Warp trolls appear in areas where powerful magic or cosmic phenomena tear the fabric of space and time. Perhaps originating from another reality entirely, they find themselves trapped in a universe that's at once confusing to them but filled with delicious prey.

Warp trolls typically stand approximately 15 feet tall and weigh about 1,500 pounds. Their skin is pale green and partially translucent, showing glowing purple veins and the shadows of misshapen organs inside. Each limb has up to a dozen sharp, glass-like spikes that the trolls can detach and throw. A spike removed in this way regrows within the hour.

Warp trolls seem to have an instinctual understanding of Jotun and can learn other languages, but they rarely speak. Noise in general seems to alarm and disturb them, and in combat, they often target the creature making the most noise unless a greater threat presents itself. Unusually for trolls, these creatures possess telepathy with a limited range as well as somewhat complex minds. Getting close enough to communicate telepathically with a warp troll usually means standing within claw's reach, however, and few individuals take such a risk.

In pre-Gap times, trolls were renowned as vicious killers with the ability to regenerate their flesh, rebounding from nearly any injury and reacting with devastating violence. In the intervening centuries, even more horrifying troll specimens have emerged from the depths of space.

Notes.Abilities:
**Regeneration 15 (Deactivated by Sonic).** 

**Defensive Phase.** **Trigger** An enemy scores a critical hit against the warp troll, or the warp troll critically fails a saving throw against a damaging spell

**Requirements** The warp troll's regeneration hasn't been deactivated

**Effect** The warp troll's body phases partially out of reality. They become incorporeal until the end of their next turn, gaining resistance 5 to all damage except force and Strikes with the ghost killer weapon property. This resistance is doubled against non-magical damage. The triggering damage is calculated using this resistance.

**Fold Reality.** The warp troll disappears into a pocket dimension until the start of their next turn. They can reappear in any unoccupied space within 60 feet of their previous location. The warp troll can't Fold Reality again for 1d4 rounds.

**Spike Shift.** A warp troll's phasic spikes shift out of reality until they reach their target, ignoring circumstance bonuses to the target's AC granted by cover.

entities.name: Warpstitcher
entities.description:
Warpstitchers are self-proclaimed guardians of existence, holding the belief that they were created by the gods to sew together the space between alternate realities. These horrifying aberrations relentlessly hunt anything they suspect abuses magic or technology to change the fabric of the multiverse. Once they find their quarry, they wait only long enough to confirm their suspicions before attacking. Potential threats—a neophyte spellcaster trying their first cantrips, an academic theorist exploring interstellar travel—instead earn a telepathic warning of what awaits should they pursue their efforts too far. Everything other than threats (potential or otherwise) is a possible tool, a target for warpstitcher lies and coercion.

Their mere appearance is fuel for nightmares, with insectile limbs supporting a massive, bulbous torso. From their back spring five multi-segmented limbs ending in wicked claws threaded with the very stuff of reality that they use to skewer their prey, who they then sew into their bodies. Such unfortunate creatures quickly dissolve, possibly sustaining the warpstitchers, though whether that's through their flesh, thoughts, or alternate reality potential is unknown. Those few who survive are plagued by disturbing, haunting visions; a smaller percentage instead see visions of happier possible lives, gaining peace and sometimes unprecedented witchwarper powers.

Notes.Abilities:
**Resist Reality.** **Trigger** The warpstitcher would take damage

**Effect** The warpstitcher gains resistance 12 to the triggering damage type until the start of their next turn. The resistance applies to the triggering damage.

**Fold Reality.** The warpstitcher collapses the space between themself and another location. They choose a 10-foot square within 120 feet. The warpstitcher then Strides, treating the chosen area as adjacent to them.

**Threads of Quintessence.** The warpstitcher's claws are laced with strands of quintessence they force into victims' wounds. This functions as Grab, or Improved Grab on a critical hit.

**Warp Suture.** **Requirements** The warpstitcher has a creature Grabbed or Restrained

**Effect** The warpstitcher sews the creature into themself. The creature is pulled into the warpstitcher's space and moves with the warpstitcher. It becomes restrained and takes 3d12 force damage at the end of each of its turns until freed. Additionally, it takes 1d12 force damage whenever the warpstitcher uses Resist Reality (DC 34 save). The Escape DC is 34 (escape dc=34), or the sutures can be severed (AC 25, Hardness 8, HP 30, weakness to slashing 5), freeing the creature. The warpstitcher can have up to 12 Bulk of creatures sewn into their body. The body of a creature that dies while sutured is absorbed into the warpstitcher's body and destroyed 1d4 rounds later.
Notes.Spells: Truespeech (constant)

entities.name: Wastewither
entities.description:
When left untreated for too long, standing industrial wastewater attracts wastewithers from the elemental Plane of Water as it evaporates. Wastewithers contaminate everything they touch, turning solid ground and clean water into sludge. Many corporate dumping sites and toxic spills attract or spawn wastewithers, whose mere presence further contaminates the ecosystem.

Elementals are energetic intrusions from the primal planes of existence. They take many forms, from mindless eddies in the wind or water to complex entities capable of wielding primal magic. The advent of space travel and the progress of technology have allowed even more living embodiments of the elements to manifest in the Universe.

Natural events like wildfires, solar storms, and floods can unleash hordes of unruly elementals on a planet or into a region of space. Sometimes, a gathering of powerful elementals causes a natural disaster on an epic scale, like an off-the-charts solar flare that fries a planet's power grid or a ceaseless storm swirling in a gas giant's atmosphere.

Stats.Immunities: acid, bleed, drained, paralyzed, poison, sleep

Notes.Abilities:
**Toxic Exhaust.** 15 feet. A poisonous mist lingers around the wastewither. When a creature enters or starts its turn in the aura, it must attempt a DC 23 save. If the creature fails, it's Sickened 1 and Slowed 1 until it leaves the aura. Environmental protections or an appropriate spell provides a +2 circumstance bonus to saves against the aura.

**Acid Rain.** The wastewither vaporizes into a cloud and rains down acid drops. The wastewither Flies up to twice their Speed. Any creature the wastewither passes over takes 9d8 acid damage with a DC 23 save. A wastewither can't use Acid Rain again for 1d4 rounds.

**Contaminated Sludge.** **Frequency** once per day

**Effect** All terrain in a 30-foot emanation becomes difficult terrain for 1 minute. All creatures that enter or begin their turn in the affected area must attempt a DC 23 save or become Drained 1. This drained value is cumulative, to a maximum of Drained 4.

**Swallow Whole.** Medium, 2d8+12 bludgeoning plus 2d6 acid, Rupture 21

entities.name: Wayward Warp
entities.description: A wayward warp is a living dimensional rift that causes unexpected havoc as they twist the world around them. No two wayward warps look the same, and no wayward warp keeps the same appearance for very long; every time a wayward warp moves, a different potential reality reveals itself. The warp themself is a rift at the center of the aura that appears like a tear in reality, often taking a shape vaguely resembling a feather star whose tentacles are lined with shard-like cracks in space itself.

Notes.Abilities:
**Warp Sense.** A wayward warp can sense creatures within their warp field as a precise sense at the listed range.

**Reality Shimmer.** The wayward warp has concealment against attacks originating outside of their warp field.

**Warp Field.** 15 feet. Reality within the area becomes a different type of terrain. Structures and creatures in the area aren't transformed, and the change immediately ends when the aura moves or the wayward warp dies. The nature of the aura is chosen randomly using the table below each time the wayward warp moves. A wayward warp is immune to their own warp field's effects and to the aligned damage type, but they gain weakness 5 to the opposing damage type.

D6FIELDALIGNED DAMAGEOPPOSING DAMAGEFIELD EFFECT

1CosmicVoidVitalityZero gravity

2EarthPiercingAcidDifficult terrain (sand)

3InfernoFireColdHazardous terrain (1d6 fire)

4StormElectricityBludgeoningHazardous terrain (1d6 electricity)

5FrozenColdFireUneven ground (ice)

6WaterBludgeoningElectricityUnderwater (flooded)

**Spatial Rending.** A creature hit by a wayward warp's spatial tendril must succeed at a DC 26 save or become misaligned to reality for 1 minute, gaining a condition based on the field effect while it remains in the warp field: Untethered (cosmic), Suppressed (earth or water), Clumsy 1 (inferno or frozen), or Glitching 1 (any tech creature or held tech item in storm).
Notes.Spells: Void Whispers, Illusory Creature, Illusory Creature, Stupefy, Dizzying Colors, Dream of Home, Eldritch Lance, Figment, Illusory Object, Seek the Stars, Telekinetic Hand, Void Warp

entities.name: Whiptail Renkroda
entities.description:
Whiptail renkrodas live along mountain slopes and rocky foothills, nesting in dark caves and rocky crags. They soar through the skies on powerful wings and attack with their long, lashing tails, which can coil around their prey like a whip. Many an unlucky traveler has been lashed by a whiptail renkroda's tail, hauled up into the air, and dropped to their death.

Renkrodas are a family of large dinosaur-like predators native to the planet Castrovel. They've spread beyond the jungle planet's boundaries thanks to smugglers, poachers, and ultra-wealthy big-game hunters. Bipedal and strong with long necks and decorative spines, renkrodas are best known for their terrifying roars, which they bellow frequently as a form of long-range communication and to scare away other predators and scavengers. Over a dozen species of renkrodas exist, each specially adapted to their environment or ecological niche.

Notes.Abilities:
**Twisting Tail.** **Trigger** A creature within reach of the whiptail renkroda's tail uses a move action or leaves a square during a move action it's using

**Effect** The whiptail renkroda Strikes the target with its tail. If it hits, the whiptail renkroda disrupts the creature's action.

**Aerial Predator.** When a whiptail renkroda has a Medium or smaller creature Grabbed, its Grab doesn't end if it moves away. Instead, when it moves, it carries the grabbed creature with it.

**Fling.** **Requirements** A creature is Grabbed in the whiptail renkroda's tail

**Effect** The whiptail renkroda flings the creature through the air, launching the creature up to 10 feet up from its tail and 30 feet away. The creature takes falling damage accordingly. If the flung creature lands on another creature, the creature it lands on takes the same amount of bludgeoning damage (DC 26 save).

**Terrifying Roar.** The whiptail renkroda bellows ferociously. Each non-renkroda creature within 60 feet must attempt a DC 29 save. The creature is then temporarily immune for 10 minutes.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Success** The creature is Frightened 1.

**Failure** The creature is Frightened 2.

**Critical Failure** The creature is Frightened 3.

entities.name: Whiskered Renkroda
entities.description:
The smallest of all renkrodas, whiskered renkrodas have adapted to move easily through dense jungles and forests and blend in amid the vibrant green flora. Whiskered renkrodas have whisker-like antennae growing from their chins that detect vibrations, enabling them to detect prey hiding amid the dense foliage. When they spot their prey, renkrodas charge into the fray and slam into their prey with enough force to topple trees or vehicles. Occasionally, whiskered renkrodas live and hunt in packs, to better protect themselves from larger predators.

Renkrodas are a family of large dinosaur-like predators native to the planet Castrovel. They've spread beyond the jungle planet's boundaries thanks to smugglers, poachers, and ultra-wealthy big-game hunters. Bipedal and strong with long necks and decorative spines, renkrodas are best known for their terrifying roars, which they bellow frequently as a form of long-range communication and to scare away other predators and scavengers. Over a dozen species of renkrodas exist, each specially adapted to their environment or ecological niche.

Notes.Abilities:
**Motion Sense.** A whiskered renkroda can sense nearby creatures through vibration and air or water movement as an imprecise sense at the listed range.

**Circling Reposition.** **Trigger** A creature ends its movement within the whiskered renkroda's reach

**Effect** The whiskered renkroda circles its prey, Striding up to its Speed. The renkroda must move to a location where the triggering creature is within its reach.

**Forest Passage.** The whiskered renkroda ignores any difficult terrain caused by plants, such as bushes, vines, and undergrowth.

**Terrifying Roar.** The whiskered renkroda bellows ferociously. Each non-renkroda creature within 60 feet must attempt a DC 22 save. The creature is then temporarily immune for 10 minutes.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Success** The creature is Frightened 1.

**Failure** The creature is Frightened 2.

**Critical Failure** The creature is Frightened 3.

**Upending Charge.** The whiskered renkroda charges forward and slams into its prey. It Strides twice. If the whiskered renkroda ends its movement with an enemy within its reach, it makes a body Strike against that enemy. On a hit, the enemy is knocked Prone.

entities.name: Wyspiria
entities.description:
Whether they were created by the god Triune, the arc spectra Facilian, or by the Drift itself, wyspirias are a new evolution of spectra first encountered within the last few decades. Metaphysicians often explain wyspirias in contrast against iridias as spectra emissaries; where iridias travel the galaxy to share gifts of technology and information, wyspirias instead come to mortal worlds on a mission to collect and preserve mortal art and knowledge, storing it within themselves or bringing it back to the Drift for reasons as of yet unknown.

Wyspirias' glass-like bodies include a cascade of tentacle-like cords descending from their waists, which they use to plug themselves directly into both people and machines. Because their tentacles can resemble the outstretched roots of a small, floating tree, the librarian spectra are sometimes known as "trees of knowledge." They use their networks to transfer data and share emotional or sensory experiences between participants.

Though accounts of wyspirias appearing on mortal worlds are extremely rare, they've been known to sometimes involve themselves as mediators between warring civilizations. They work to ease tense negotiations at peace talks by connecting the opposing delegates to one another, enabling various parties to experience each other's perspectives. It's widely believed that spectra only dispatch wyspirias to intervene in mortal conflicts when a war could result in the loss of important information, prevent the discovery of future innovations, or interfere with the Drift itself.

In the Great Beyond, time is measured not in hundreds, thousands, or millions of years, but rather in eons—in iterations of reality itself. Only rising to prominence within the last three centuries alongside the advent and proliferation of Drift technology, spectra have thrived in a burgeoning niche of the otherwise stagnant zeitgeist of the Great Beyond.

Though their origins and objectives remain shrouded in mystery, encounters with spectra revolve around new technological discoveries, sharing the knowledge of faster-than-light travel, and protecting the Drift. No one knows if spectra existed before the Drift, but their connection to the hyperspace plane is indisputable. Prominent metaphysicians believe spectra were created as amalgams of raw quintessence pulled into the Drift, just as the Drift itself grows from pieces of the Multiverse. If this is true, spectra's interest in the proliferation of Drift technology takes a subtle sinister turn, as each new Drift engine serves to harvest the Great Beyond and all its denizens for the growth of the Drift and spectra themselves.

Notes.Skills: Athletics +20, Computers +24, Deception +21, Occultism +22, Piloting +22, Stealth +20
Notes.Abilities:
**Arc Network.** The wyspiria can communicate through items and creatures with the tech trait, projecting sound from and speaking through the item or creature's voice, speakers, or other audio output. In addition, the excuba can use any item or creature with the tech trait within their digital telepathy aura as the point of origin for their spells and abilities when calculating range, distance, line of effect, and area of effect.

**Slip Drive.** An wyspiria has an internal biomechanical Drift engine, allowing them to function as a Drift engine for a starship or vehicle they pilot as a 1-minute activity. An excuba can enter or exit the Drift themself as a 1-minute activity. When an excuba gets a critical failure on a Piloting check to Navigate or Plot a Course through the Drift, they get a failure instead.

**Techsense.** The wyspiria senses creatures and objects with the tech trait as a precise sense within the listed range.

**Digital Telepathy.** 100 feet. A wyspiria can communicate telepathically with any item or creature with the tech trait within their aura as well as with other technologically telepathic creatures (such as those with shortwave and similar abilities). This ability also allows the spectra to remotely attempt Computers checks within their aura.

**Borrow Time.** **Frequency** once per minute

**Trigger** The wyspiria's turn begins

**Effect** The wyspiria pulls potential energy from their future self to use in the present. The wyspiria becomes Quickened this turn and can use the extra action only for Fly, Stride, and Strike actions. At the end of the wyspiria's turn, they become Slowed 1 until the end of their next turn.

**Connect.** When a wyspiria Grabs a creature with a tentacle Strike, they automatically plug one of their many cord-like appendages into it. The sudden connection feeds the creature a stream of information and fabricated sensory data, making them Stunned 1 unless they succeed at a DC 30 save. If the wyspiria moves, they bring the Grabbed creature along with them. The wyspiria doesn't need to use additional actions to keep the creature grabbed; the creature remains grabbed as long as it's connected. The grabbed creature can attempt to escape dc=30 as normal. The wyspiria can connect with up to 10 creatures simultaneously.

**Overload Connections.** **Requirements** At least one creature is connected to the wyspiria's tentacles

**Effect** The wyspiria maintains their connection. All connected creatures must attempt a DC 30 save.

**Critical Success** No effect.

**Success** The creature becomes Stunned 1.

**Failure** The creature becomes Stunned 2.

**Critical Failure** The creature becomes Paralyzed for 1 round.

**Piercing Signal.** The wyspiria emits a series of synthesized squeals. Each creature in a 20-foot emanation takes 6d6 electricity |options:area-damage damage and 6d6 sonic |options:area-damage damage (DC 30 save) and is Deafened for 1 minute on a failure (or 10 minutes on a critical failure). While a creature is deafened in this way, it also can't understand telepathic communication or any message conveyed by a tech device—for example, the target perceives text on comm units or other digital displays as scrambled text. The wyspiria can't use Piercing Signal again for 1d4 rounds.
Notes.Spells: X-Ray Vision, Chrono Push, Overload Systems, Truespeech (constant), Translocate (at will), Discharge, Haste, Holographic Memory, Slow, Time's Edge, Caustic Conversion, Detect Thoughts, Inject Nanobots, Skim Data (at will), Analyze Target, Delete, Implant Data, Mending, Seek the Stars, Wisp Ally

entities.name: Xenowarden Biohulk
entities.description:
Biohulks are devoted Xenowardens who purposefully fused their body with plants and other flora to gain formidable strength. This transformation is usually accomplished using biotech, magic, or genetic experimentation, and can't be reversed. Regardless of their method, biohulks are incredibly strong and capable of battering down most artificial barriers with ease. Xenowarden biohulks are usually extremists, entirely and passionately devoted to the Xenowardens' cause.

The Xenowardens are a powerful and well-respected organization who aim to safeguard and study the natural world and ensure that technological advances are ecologically responsible. With an incredibly diverse membership, their ranks include, among others, hermits who practice nature magic and eschew technology and scientists who create renewable energy from algae. On the other end of the spectrum are elite combat units like the Wildknights and the Greenguards and feared ecoterrorists like the enigmatic Oleander. The Xenowardens are led by a Greenspeaker, who's elected by acclaim and advised by their peers.

Notes.Abilities:
**Battering Charge.** The Xenowarden biohulk Strides three times, then makes a melee Strike, dealing an additional 4d6 bludgeoning damage on a hit. If the target of this Strike is an object or construct, this Strike ignores 5 Hardness.

**Destructive Power.** Whenever a Xenowarden biohulk makes a melee Strike that would deal bludgeoning damage, that Strike gains the razing trait.

**Nature's Fury.** The Xenowarden biohulk bellows with rage, causing plants to sprout from the ground and hinder the biohulk's enemies. Creatures within 30 feet of the biohulk take 6d8 slashing damage from the thrashing plants (DC 26 save), and the area becomes difficult terrain for 10 minutes. The Xenowarden biohulk ignores difficult terrain created by Nature's Fury. Then, the Xenowarden biohulk can attempt an Intimidation check to demoralize each creature in the area.

entities.name: Xenowarden Greenhorn
entities.description:
The Greenguards are an elite combat unit of Xenowardens known for their nature magic, often dispatched to sites of extreme ecological upheaval. New recruits to the Greenguards are given the rank of "root" but are colloquially called "greenhorns." Xenowarden greenhorns train extensively in tight-knit units.

The Xenowardens are a powerful and well-respected organization who aim to safeguard and study the natural world and ensure that technological advances are ecologically responsible. With an incredibly diverse membership, their ranks include, among others, hermits who practice nature magic and eschew technology and scientists who create renewable energy from algae. On the other end of the spectrum are elite combat units like the Wildknights and the Greenguards and feared ecoterrorists like the enigmatic Oleander. The Xenowardens are led by a Greenspeaker, who's elected by acclaim and advised by their peers.

Notes.Abilities: **Grown Together.** A Xenowarden greenhorn's AC increases by +1 when they're within reach of at least one other Xenowarden greenhorn.
Notes.Spells: Gouging Claw, Scan Environment, Tangle Vine

entities.name: Xenowarden Rootsworn
entities.description:
Xenowarden rootsworn are mentors and teachers, tasked with overseeing the training and command of a platoon of roots. Most rootsworn are talented spellcasters who can manipulate plants, using them to shield the Xenowarden from harm and to deploy allies across the battlefield.

The Xenowardens are a powerful and well-respected organization who aim to safeguard and study the natural world and ensure that technological advances are ecologically responsible. With an incredibly diverse membership, their ranks include, among others, hermits who practice nature magic and eschew technology and scientists who create renewable energy from algae. On the other end of the spectrum are elite combat units like the Wildknights and the Greenguards and feared ecoterrorists like the enigmatic Oleander. The Xenowardens are led by a Greenspeaker, who's elected by acclaim and advised by their peers.

Notes.Skills: Acrobatics +7, Diplomacy +7, Intimidation +7, Medicine +9, Nature +9, Survival +9
Notes.Abilities:
**Root Deflection.** **Trigger** The rootsworn is standing on a solid surface and would be hit by a ranged Strike

**Effect** A mass of magical roots rapidly sprout from the ground and shield the Xenowarden rootsworn from harm. The Xenowarden rootsworn gains a +2 status bonus to their AC against the triggering Strike.

**Root Network.** 1 to 2

The Xenowarden rootsworn conjures magical roots to move their allies around the battlefield. They select one willing ally within 100 feet who's standing on a solid surface, or three willing allies if they spend 2 actions to perform Root Network. The roots move each target up to their Speed in a direction of their choice, then deposit them safely on a solid surface.
Notes.Spells: Entangling Flora, Verdant Code, Detect Magic, Electric Arc, Gouging Claw, Heal, Hydraulic Push, Scan Environment, Sonic Scream, Summon Plant or Fungus, Tangle Vine, Thunderstrike

entities.name: Yearling Arabuk
entities.description:
Yearling arabuks collect in glarings. They're abandoned by their mothers days after birth, then adopted by a mature arabuk that raises them as a group.

Those traveling through Akiton's Winterlands risk stumbling on its apex predator: the carnivorous arabuk.

Notes.Abilities:
**Snow Vision.** Snow doesn't impair a yearling arabuk's vision; it ignores Concealment from snowfall.

**Glacial Stride.** The arabuk Strides twice with a +10-foot circumstance bonus to Speed, ignoring difficult terrain caused by ice, snow, or other arctic conditions.

entities.name: Zalyop
entities.description:
The jet streams of the gas giant Bretheda are filled with large, bulbous silhouettes called zalyops, sometimes referred to as balloon plants. Gas-filled and hardy, they're buffeted around by the planet's eternal storms. It's common for a cascade of these plants to be found trailing in the wake of an oma or plastered against one of the many spacecrafts and aircrafts frequenting the gas giant.

The sound of zalyops bouncing against a metal hull at high velocity can be a humorous one, but travelers should be careful not to assume these plants are harmless. Zalyops are known to expel high-speed organic shrapnel by reflex. Additionally, their confusion-inducing gaseous waste easily spreads across the atmosphere and can be caught in a ship's air-intake valve.

Zalyops can also cause chaos at ground level. When they float into small settlements, flocks of them will descend on small creatures, which they engulf for nutrients. The widespread befuddling clouds caused by such incursions are a dangerous nuisance. Pedestrians and pets alike must take care during such events to stay inside and simply wait the invasive balloons out.

Pact Worlds chemists have developed (and patented) Balyoon, an anesthetic drug from zalyop gases. In addition to being difficult to obtain in the first place, the drug is highly unstable until refined in the laboratory, and more than one starship has been lost when its crew failed to properly store the gases they just harvested from a zalyop.

Balyoon also plays a role in Eoxian soap operas and other dramatic vidshows across the Pact Worlds. It's used as a plot device in a myriad of ways, such as a villain contriving to discredit a hero or for a family member to suddenly lose their mind or memory in a soap opera. How these characters obtained the processed gas of a predatory Brethedan plant is rarely as important as the exciting drama, however.

Notes.Abilities:
**Explosive Burst.** **Trigger** The zalyop is reduced to 0 Hit Points by physical or fire damage

**Effect** The zalyop explodes, dealing 4d6 sonic |options:area-damage damage to all creatures in a 20-foot burst centered on itself (DC 18 save). This also triggers a Befuddling Cloud, even if it's been used in the last hour.

**Befuddling Cloud.** **Frequency** once per hour

**Effect** The zalyop expels a gaseous cloud in a 30-foot emanation. Creatures within the cloud must succeed at a DC 18 save or become Confused for 1 round (or 1 minute on a critical failure). Confused creatures that are also engulfed by the zalyop don't receive flat checks to end the confused condition.

**Engulf.** DC 18, 2d6 acid damage, escape dc=18, Rupture 7

entities.name: Zitteroc
entities.description:
Zitterocs are vicious reptilians native to the Kazmurg's Absurdity world of Azhan Prime. Due to the native Azhans' propensity for trading, these creatures have made their way across the cosmos and found new homes in the galaxy's various wetlands. Zitterocs are renowned across the galaxy for their ability to innately detect and somehow ignore even the most virulent poisons. They can siphon such poisons from targets and convert them into a fuel source for their digestive acids. Even after this siphoning process, trace amounts of poison can be found within a zitteroc, and the fresh bodies of zitterocs are often a cornucopia of medicinal substances for biotechnicians and pharmaceutical experts.

At maturity, a zitteroc stands only 2 to 3 feet tall, with a length roughly double that size. They possess a sickly blue hide that shimmers like an oil slick and can take on the rough properties of its surroundings with concentration. Additionally, they can feign a sickening death when threatened by hunters or more dangerous predators. These typically docile carnivores can become vicious when they run out of abundant food from less threatening animals, at which point they make their way into the fringes of civilization.

Notes.Abilities:
**Poison Sense.** A zitteroc can detect poison as an imprecise sense at the listed range, including poisonous substances, poisoned creatures, and creatures with attacks that inflict poison.

**Sickening Death.** **Frequency** once per day

**Trigger** The zitteroc takes damage

**Effect** The zitteroc releases a spray of acid in a 15-foot emanation, dealing 4d4 acid |options:area-damage damage to each creature in the area (DC 18 save), then uses Still as a Corpse.

**Shimmer Hide.** **Frequency** once per round

**Effect** The zitteroc focuses on shifting its hide pattern to match its surroundings. The zitteroc becomes Concealed to creatures more than 15 feet away from it until the start of its next turn.

**Siphon Poison.** **Requirements** The zitteroc's last action was a successful mandibles Strike

**Effect** The zitteroc siphons poison from the struck target's bloodstream. If the target is afflicted by a poison or possesses a natural poison, the zitteroc consumes that poison to empower its own abilities. The poison effect is suppressed on the target for 1 round, or the target can't use its natural poison until the end of its next turn. Until the end of the zitteroc's next turn, the zitteroc increases its acid damage die size for its mandibles and acid spit Strikes, and Sickening Death, by one step (typically to d6s).

**Still as a Corpse.** Until the next time it acts, the zitteroc appears to be dead. It has an automatic result of 21 on  checks and DCs to pass as a dead zitteroc.
